title: INDIA AND UZBEKISTAN SHARE CENTURIES-OLD HISTORICAL, CULTURAL AND CIVILIZATIONAL TIES: LOK SABHA SPEAKER
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Lok Sabha Secretariat INDIA AND UZBEKISTAN SHARE CENTURIES-OLD HISTORICAL, CULTURAL AND CIVILIZATIONAL TIES: LOK SABHA SPEAKER INDIA–UZBEKISTAN PARLIAMENTARY FRIENDSHIP GROUP WILL GIVE FRESH IMPETUS TO BILATERAL RELATIONS: LOK SABHA SPEAKER H.E. MR. BAKHTIYOR SAIDOV, MINISTER OF FOREIGN AFFAIRS OF UZBEKISTAN, CALLS ON LOK SABHA SPEAKER प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                04 AUG 2026 3:43PM by PIB Delhi Lok Sabha Speaker Shri Om Birla observed today that India and Uzbekistan are bound by centuries-old historical, cultural, and civilizational ties that continue to provide a robust foundation for their enduring friendship. He expressed confidence that growing political trust, expanding trade and investment, and enhanced people-to-people exchanges will further strengthen the bilateral partnership in the years ahead. Shri Birla made these remarks during a meeting with H.E. Mr. Bakhtiyor Saidov, Minister of Foreign Affairs of Uzbekistan, who called on him at Parliament House. The two leaders held wide-ranging discussions on India–Uzbekistan relations, with a particular emphasis on parliamentary cooperation, trade and investment, education, culture, and issues of mutual regional and global significance. Speaking on India's democratic traditions, Shri Birla stated that India, as the world's largest democracy, features a vibrant parliamentary system that effectively reflects the aspirations and diversity of its people. He noted that the 543-member Lok Sabha represents millions of citizens nationwide and that India's multi-party framework provides equal space for diverse perspectives and constructive debate. Referring to the functioning of the institution, Shri Birla informed the visiting dignitary that Parliament meets across three sessions annually, with the ongoing Monsoon Session actively deliberating on several matters of national importance. Shri Birla highlighted India’s significant achievements in infrastructure development, digital innovation, technology, connectivity, investment and trade. He observed that India's youth are increasingly assuming leadership roles globally and that collaboration with leading universities and international institutions continues to expand. Referring to the India–Uzbekistan Parliamentary Friendship Group constituted in March 2026, Shri Birla expressed confidence that the initiative will impart fresh momentum to legislative engagement and deepen cooperation across economic, educational, cultural, and people-to-people spheres. Recalling his participation in the 150th Assembly of the Inter-Parliamentary Union (IPU) held in Tashkent in April 2025, Shri Birla noted his interactions with H.E. Mr. Shavkat Mirziyoyev, President of Uzbekistan; H.E. Ms. Tanzila Narbayeva, Chairperson of the Senate and Mr. Nuriddin Ismailov, Speaker of the Legislative Chamber. He observed that these high-level visits laid a strong cornerstone for ongoing parliamentary collaboration. Expressing satisfaction with the steady progress of bilateral relations, Shri Birla hoped that the current visit would further reinforce the comprehensive partnership between the two nations. H.E. Mr. Bakhtiyor Saidov reaffirmed Uzbekistan's firm commitment to deepening its multifaceted partnership with India, stating that Tashkent attaches high importance to expanding political, economic, and parliamentary cooperation. Appreciating India's robust democratic traditions, he noted that Uzbekistan stands to benefit significantly from the legislative experience of the world's largest democracy. Mr. Saidov further emphasized that enhanced parliamentary engagement will contribute meaningfully to advancing the comprehensive strategic partnership. He called for a shared vision to expand cooperation in trade, investment, joint projects, and emerging sectors. To mark the occasion, H.E. Mr. Bakhtiyor Saidov presented Shri Om Birla with a special commemorative publication detailing the 150th Assembly of the Inter-Parliamentary Union hosted by Uzbekistan. It was a pleasure to meet H.E. Mr. Bakhtiyor Saidov, Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Uzbekistan, at Parliament House today. title: Ayurveda Day and Promotion of Preventive Healthcare
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau AYUSH Ayurveda Day and Promotion of Preventive Healthcare प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                04 AUG 2026 3:05PM by PIB Delhi The 10 th Ayurveda Day was celebrated on 23 rd September 2025 under the aegis of the Ministry of Ayush, with All India Institute of Ayurveda (AIIA), Goa as the nodal institute. The celebrations were held on the theme “Ayurveda for People and Planet,” emphasizing holistic health and environmental sustainability. The main event at AIIA, Goa was held in the august presence of Shri Pusapati Ashok Gajapathi Raju, Hon’ble Governor of Goa (Chief Guest), and was graced by Dr. Pramod Sawant, Hon’ble Chief Minister of Goa; Shri Prataprao Jadhav, Hon’ble Union Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Ayush & Minister of State for Health & Family Welfare; and Shri Shripad Yesso Naik, Hon’ble Union Minister of State for Power and New & Renewable Energy. The prestigious National Dhanwantari Ayurveda Awards were conferred upon eminent Vaidyas in recognition of their outstanding contributions to the field of Ayurveda. Multiple projects/initiatives were also inaugurated/launched during the event.   The details of major projects/initiatives are given at Annexure I . Beyond the main event at AIIA Goa, extensive activities were organised across the country and abroad as a part of Ayurveda Day 2025 including Ayurveda health camps providing free consultations, diagnostic services, and distribution of medicines; specialized camps focusing on non-communicable diseases, geriatric care, women and child health, and lifestyle disorders; and outreach services in rural and underserved areas to improve accessibility to traditional healthcare. Educational and awareness initiatives formed a major component, with the organization of seminars, national and international conferences, CME programmes, workshops, and expert lectures. Schools, colleges, and community institutions actively participated through quizzes, essay competitions, painting competitions, and awareness drives to sensitize the younger population about healthy lifestyles rooted in Ayurveda. In alignment with the theme “Ayurveda for People and Planet,” numerous activities focusing on environmental sustainability were also conducted, including plantation drives, herbal garden development, medicinal plant distribution, and cleanliness campaigns under Swachhta initiatives. Digital outreach played a significant role, with webinars, social media campaigns, online pledge drives, and interactive programmes conducted through platforms such as MyGov, significantly amplifying public engagement and awareness.  The Day was observed across more than 150 countries. A total of 32 States and Union Territories reported organization of activities in connection with Ayurveda Day 2025. The major activities included Ayurveda medical camps, medical screening and outreach programmes, awareness campaigns, seminars, workshops, webinars, Yoga sessions, medicinal plant exhibitions, plantation drives, distribution of medicinal plants, cleanliness drives, rallies, walkathons, competitions, media and Information Education and Communication (IEC) activities. The list of States and Union Territories that reported Ayurveda Day 2025 activities is placed at Annexure II . To further institutionalise Ayurveda Day as a nationwide movement for preventive healthcare, and public awareness, the Government has notified 23 rd September as the annual date for its observance, thereby providing a fixed date for its celebration every year. The Ministry of Ayush adopts a Whole-of-Government approach by involving Central Ministries/Departments, States/UTs, National Institutes, Research Councils, academic institutions and other stakeholders. A dedicated theme is identified each year, and a framework of suggested activities aligned with the theme is circulated to stakeholders to facilitate coordinated nationwide implementation, with a consistent focus on preventive healthcare, health promotion, and public awareness through Ayurveda. A nodal institution under the Ministry is designated annually for overall coordination for planning, implementation, and monitoring of activities. A dedicated Ayurveda Day microsite serves as a central repository of the IEC materials, and other resources, besides enabling online reporting and documentation of activities. These measures facilitate coordinated nationwide outreach, promote preventive healthcare, and enhance public awareness of Ayurveda. Annexure I Details of projects/initiatives inaugurated/launched during the main event of 10 th Ayurveda Day held at All India Institute of Ayurveda, Goa 1.         Inauguration of facilities Integrative Oncology Unit at All India Institute of Ayurveda, Goa Central Sterile Supply Department (CSSD) - Unit at All India Institute of Ayurveda, Goa Blood Storage Unit at All India Institute of Ayurveda, Goa Hospital Linen Processing & Care Unit at All India Institute of Ayurveda, Goa 2.         Launches Guidelines for Examining Ayush Related Interventions by the Office of the Controller General of Patents, Designs, and Trade Marks (CGPDTM) Launch of nationwide campaign - “Desh ka Swasthya Parikshan” - for the assessment of the health status of individuals Launch of the website - ‘Admirable Personalities to Transform Ayurveda (APTA)’- prepared by CCRAS as a tribute to the luminaries in the field of Ayurveda. Launch of web- based portal – ‘Digitized Retrieval Application for Versatile Yardstick of Ayush Substances (DRAVYA)’ - developed by CCRAS Annexure II List of States and Union Territories that reported Ayurveda Day 2025 activities Sl. title: Integration of Ayush Services into Ayushman Arogya Mandir

Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau AYUSH Integration of Ayush Services into Ayushman Arogya Mandir प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                04 AUG 2026 3:04PM by PIB Delhi Under Centrally Sponsored Scheme National Ayush Mission (NAM), as per the proposals received from State / UT Governments through their State Annual Action Plans (SAAPs), 12500 units of existing Ayush Dispensaries and Sub Health Centres (SCs) have been upgraded for operationalisation as Ayush Health & Wellness Centres, now renamed as Ayushman Arogya Mandir (Ayush) [(AAM(Ayush)]. The State/UT-wise status of approved and functional AAM (Ayush) is furnished at Annexure-I. Further, State/UT-wise status of Public health facilities offering Ayush OPD services in the country is furnished at Annexure-II. As per the operational guidelines, AAM (Ayush) were approved with an objective to establish a holistic wellness model based on Ayush principles and practices (Yoga therapy, Ayurveda consultations, Naturopathy treatments, etc.) focusing on preventive, promotive, curative, rehabilitative healthcare by establishing integration with existing public healthcare system to provide informed choice to the needy public by making Ayush services available in a team based approach including involvement of field level workers specially ASHAs etc. As reported by States/UTs, the footfall of the beneficiaries visiting to the AAM (Ayush) has been subsequently increased after upgradation of Ayush Dispensaries/Sub health centres into AAM (Ayush) because in addition to OPD services, these facilities are also providing various other services like Prakriti Parikshan, Yoga related activities at the level of facility as well as community and awareness about uses of common medicinal plants etc. There are NABH assessment and also third party review besides visit by the Central team in different States/UTs to ensure quality, accreditation, training of Ayush practitioners deployed at these centres and monitoring of the implementation progress of different activities/services being provided by operational AAM (Ayush). Further, State/UT Governments have been suggested by the visiting team for appropriate training & capacity building of AAM (Ayush) team, strengthening of referral linkages with other public health facilities, effective involvement of field level workers specially ASHAs etc. for better outcome of the activities being conducted through AAM (Ayush). Under NAM, consolidated funds are released to the State/UT Governments against the proposals submitted through SAAPs, as per provisions of the NAM guideline. Financial assistance is allocated at a unit cost of Rs.16.22 lakhs per Ayush Dispensaries & Rs.15.744 lakhs per Sub-Centres for upgrading them into AAM (Ayush). title: Establishment of New Ayush Institutes and Hospitals in the Country
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau AYUSH Establishment of New Ayush Institutes and Hospitals in the Country प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                04 AUG 2026 3:03PM by PIB Delhi Public Health being a State subject, establishment of new Ayush institutes, integrated hospitals and strengthening Ayush infrastructure across the country including Odisha particularly in Eastern India comes under the purview of respective State/UT Governments. However, Ministry of Ayush is implementing the Centrally Sponsored Scheme of National Ayush Mission (NAM) through State/UT Governments with the provision of providing financial assistance for strengthening of Ayush infrastructure by establishment of new Ayush colleges in the States where availability of Ayush teaching institutions is inadequate in Government Sector, setting up of 50/30/10 bedded integrated Ayush Hospitals, Upgradation of existing standalone Government Ayush Hospitals, Upgradation of existing Government/Panchayat/Government aided Ayush Dispensaries/Construction of building for existing Ayush Dispensary (Rented/ dilapidated accommodation), Construction of building to establish new Ayush Dispensary in the area where there are no Ayush facilities available and Operationalization of Ayushman Arogya Mandir (Ayush). States/UTs including Odisha may avail financial assistance by submitting suitable proposals through State Annual Action Plans (SAAPs) as per the provision of NAM guidelines. Under NAM, as per the proposals received from State/UT Governments through SAAPs, an amount of Rs. 6,40,699.24 lakhs has been released to States/UTs including Odisha from 2014-15 to 2025-26 for implementation of different approved activities including strengthening of Ayush infrastructure. title: Steps Taken to Promote Ayush Medicine
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau AYUSH Steps Taken to Promote Ayush Medicine प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                04 AUG 2026 3:02PM by PIB Delhi Ministry of Ayush has undertaken various measures through regulatory bodies i.e. the National Commission for Indian System of Medicine (NCISM) and the National Commission for Homoeopathy (NCH), established under the National Commission for Indian System of Medicine Act, 2020 and the National Commission for Homoeopathy Act, 2020, respectively, to enhance the quality of medical education in Ayurveda, Unani, Siddha and Homoeopathy. The major steps taken during the last three years are annexed as Annexure. Public Health being a State subject, the primary responsibility for the establishment of new Ayush Educational Institutions comes under the purview of respective State Governments, including Uttarakhand. However, under the Centrally Sponsored Scheme of National Ayush Mission (NAM), there is a provision for financial assistance to the State/UT Governments for the establishment of new Ayush colleges where the availability of Ayush teaching institutions is inadequate in Government Sector. Accordingly, States/UTs may avail financial assistance by submitting suitable proposal through State Annual Action Plans (SAAPs) within the provision of NAM guidelines. However, the State Government of Uttarakhand has not submitted any proposal for establishment of new Ayush Educational Institute through SAAPs for Financial Year 2026-27. The Central Council for Research in Ayurvedic Sciences (CCRAS) an autonomous organisation operates a key research facility in Uttarakhand through its peripheral unit, namely the Regional Ayurveda Research Institute (RARI) located in Ranikhet (Tarikhet). At present, there is no proposal for the establishment of a new research institute in Uttarakhand. Annexure Major steps taken during the last three years to enhance the quality of medical education in Ayush systems (A) Step taken by the National Commission for Indian System of Medicine (NCISM) for Indian System of Medicine. (i) Regulations: To improve the quality of education in Ayurveda, Siddha & Unani the following regulations were framed, published and implemented by NCISM at the Undergraduate and Postgraduate level. National Commission for Indian System of Medicine (Minimum Standards of Undergraduate Ayurveda Education) Regulations-2022. National Commission for Indian System of Medicine (Minimum Standards of Undergraduate Unani Education), Regulations 2022. National Commission for Indian System of Medicine (Minimum Standard of Undergraduate Siddha Education) Regulations, 2022. National Commission for Indian System of Medicine (Recognition of Qualifications) Regulations, 2023. National Commission for Indian System of Medicine (National Examinations for Indian System of Medicine) Regulations, 2023. National Commission for Indian System of Medicine (Ethics and Registration) Regulations, 2023. National Commission for Indian System of Medicine (Minimum essential standards, assessment and rating for undergraduate Ayurveda colleges and attached teaching hospitals) Regulations, 2024. National Commission for Indian System of Medicine (Minimum Essential Standards, Assessment and Rating for Undergraduate Unani Colleges and Attached Teaching Hospitals) Regulations, 2023. National Commission for Indian System of Medicine (Minimum Essential Standards, Assessment and Rating for Undergraduate Siddha Colleges and Attached Teaching Hospitals) Regulations, 2024. National Commission for Indian System of Medicine (Minimum Essential Standards, Assessment and Rating for Postgraduate Institutions and Minimum Standards for Postgraduate Education in Ayurveda) Regulations, 2024. National Commission for Indian System of Medicine (Minimum Essential Standards, Assessment and Rating for Postgraduate Institutions and Minimum Standards of Postgraduate Siddha Education) Regulations, 2024. National Commission for Indian System of Medicine (Minimum Essential Standards, Assessment and Rating for Postgraduate Institutions and Minimum Standards of Postgraduate Unani Education) Regulations, 2024. National Commission for Indian System of Medicine (Pre-Ayurveda-Programme for Bachelor of Ayurvedic Medicine and Surgery) Regulations, 2024. (ii) Curriculum: To align with New Education Policy 2020, global standards in medical education, and to produce meritorious and skilled Ayurveda, Siddha & Unani graduates, NCISM has brought significant reforms in medical education policy, essential standards in education, educational administration, teaching/training methodologies, assessment process, technological assistance in education, and competency-based syllabus curriculum. The Board of Unani, Siddha and Sowa-Rigpa and Board of Ayurveda framed, published and implemented the following curriculum and syllabus. Competency based Course Curriculum and Syllabus for First Professional BSMS Competency based Course Curriculum and Syllabus for Second Professional BSMS Competency Based Dynamic Curriculum and Syllabus development for Third Professional BSMS. Competency based Course Curriculum and Syllabus for First Professional BAMS. Competency based Course Curriculum and Syllabus for Second Professional BAMS. Competency based Course Curriculum and Syllabus for Third Professional BAMS. Competency based Course Curriculum and Syllabus for First Professional BUMS. Competency based Course Curriculum and Syllabus for Second Professional BUMS. Competency Based Dynamic Curriculum and Syllabus for Third Professional BUMS. Outcome based Curriculum and Syllabus for Ayurveda Post Graduate program for Biostatistics. Outcome based Curriculum and Syllabus for Ayurveda Post Graduate program for Research Methodology. Competency based Course Curriculum and Syllabus for Siddha Post Graduate programme for Biostatistics. Competency based Course Curriculum and Syllabus Siddha Post Graduate programme for Research Methodology. Competency based Course Curriculum and Syllabus for Unani Post Graduate programme for Biostatistics. Competency based Course Curriculum and Syllabus for Unani Post Graduate programme for Research Methodology. Outcome Based Curriculum and Syllabus for Post Graduate Ayurveda for PG programs for the 2nd and 3rd-6th semesters. Competency Based Dynamic Curriculum and Syllabus for Post Graduate Siddha for 16 PG programs for the 2nd and 3rd-6th semesters. Competency Based Dynamic Curriculum and Syllabus for Post Graduate Unani for 15 PG programs for the 2nd and 3rd-6th semesters. (iii) Curriculum reforms at Undergraduate level: The ratio between Lecture and Non-Lecture hours has been reversed to 1:2 to promote professional skill, and soft skills. The introduction of electives is intended to provide opportunity to students to get introduced, oriented and exposed to various allied subjects, to build inter-disciplinary approach, and to promote self-directed/guided learning. Induction program with transitional curriculum has been introduced for newly admitted students before the commencement of regular classes. Competency Based Dynamic Curriculum and Syllabus h as been introduced with well-defined graduate’s attributes, programme outcomes, course outcomes, difficulty level, advanced teaching-training methods at par with global standards, formative assessment for continuous evaluation of the students, summative assessment methods, the blue print of the question paper, vertical/horizontal integration, etc. Early Clinical exposure begins with the first professional session to provide more clinical training exposure and build self-confidence. Separate hours for library, sports, and recreation in the regular time-table of all batches for effective utilisation of library, express talent in co/extracurricular events and promote physical and mental wellness. Methodologies for supplementation of modern advances, scientific and technological developments in Ayurveda, Siddha & Unani have been introduced. In addition to the university examination (summative assessment), formative assessment is introduced, which includes nine periodical tests and two term tests. Clinical Skill/ Simulation Lab introduced in Undergraduate for upliftment of clinical knowledge. (iv) Curriculum reforms at Post graduate level: Semester system has been introduced and semester specific subjects/ papers are maintained. Credit framework has been implemented in PG. Each credit will have lecture, practical training and experiential learning in the ratio of 1:2:3 to produce highly confident and competent specialist of concerned speciality. Formative Assessment including unit-wise assessment, modular assessment were introduced to calculate Semester Grade Point Average (SGPA) and to assess the eligibility to appear for university summative examination. Electives courses for post graduate program have been also introduced along with core Subjects under Domain specific and Capacity enhancing categories. Molecular Biology lab is introduced in Post Graduate institutes for carrying out advanced studies in immunology and histopathology related tests. Thrust areas for research are prescribed for each PG program along with speciality specific program out comes and promoted multi-disciplinary research. Department of integrative health and translational research has been implemented to regulate and coordinate research activities of PG institutions. (v) Other Initiatives by NCISM to increase the Quality of Education: An academic calendar for the entire course period is introduced to ensure uniform academic administrative patterns throughout the country. Each teacher is communicated with by mail with an article on teaching technology on the first Friday and a research article on the third Friday of every month to get updated knowledge in the area of education technology and research. (vi) Use of Technology: QR code embedded syllabus: uploaded on NCISM site. Elective courses through LMS (Learning Management System). NCISM platforms/portals under AYUSH Grid. Portal for Educational Planning and Administration Workshops for Principals in ISM. Portal for Entrepreneurship Development and training Programme Workshops for coordinators of Research and Innovation cell of ISM institutions. Portal for postgraduate guide orientation workshops for PG guides of ISM postgraduate institutions on Scientific writing, Research integrity and Publication ethics. Portal for textbook quality assessment as per the developed assessment scale. Software for framing ISM curriculum and syllabus. Educational Lifecycle Management System, Learning Management System and Collaborative System and integrated with Ayush Grid. Portal for Azadi ka Amrit Mahotsav activities in ISM institutions. Portal for online data submission of admitted students by institution and counselling authorities. Portal for electives. Portal for Degree recognition system. Developed portal for academic performance of ISM institutions. (vi)  Examinations: NCISM has implemented National Teachers’ Eligibility Test (NTET) for each discipline of Ayurveda, Siddha and Unani of Indian Systems of Medicine who desire to take up teaching profession. NCISM conducted NCISM PRE-TIB Exam, counselling and seat allotment for the admission of Unani Pre-Tib Program. National Entrance cum Eligibility Test (NEET) has been conducted by NTA for the admission of Undergraduate BAMS, BSMS and BUMS courses of Ayurveda, Siddha and Unani. All India AYUSH Post Graduate Entrance Test (AIAPGET) has been conducted by NCISM through NTA. (B) Step taken by the National Commission for Homoeopathy (NCH) (i) Regulations: To improve the quality of education in Homoeopathy the following regulations were framed, published and implemented by NCH at the undergraduate and postgraduate level: - National Commission for Homoeopathy (Homoeopathy Graduate Degree Course – Bachelor of Homoeopathic Medicine and Surgery (B.H.M.S). Regulations- 2022. National Commission for Homoeopathy (Professional Conduct, Etiquette and Code of Ethics for Practitioners of Homoeopathy) Regulations, 2022. National Commission for Homoeopathy (Manner of Preparation and Maintenance of National Register for Practitioner of Homoeopathy) Regulations, 2022. National Commission for Homoeopathy (General) Regulations, 2023. National Commission for Homoeopathy (Recognition of Qualification of Homoeopathy) Regulations 2023. National Commission for Homoeopathy (National Examinations in Homoeopathy) Regulations 2023. National Commission for Homoeopathy (Medical Research in Homoeopathy) Regulations 2023. National Commission for Homoeopathy (Assessment and Rating of Medical Institutions) Regulations, 2024. National Commission for Homoeopathy (Minimum Essential Standards For Homoeopathic Colleges And Attached Hospitals), Regulations - 2024. Establishment of New Homoeopathic Medical Institution (Opening of New or Higher Course of Study or Training and Increase of Intake Capacity by a Medical Institution), Regulations-2024. National Commission for Homoeopathy (Homoeopathy Post-Graduate Degree Course- Doctor of Medicine in Homoeopathy) Regulations, 2024. (ii) Other Initiatives by NCH to increase the Quality of Education: Implementation of the Competency-Based Dynamic Curriculum (CBDC) at undergraduate and postgraduate levels in line with NEP 2020. Introduction of research-oriented electives and Research Methodology in the curriculum. Inclusion of psychology, modern pharmacology and yoga subjects in the BHMS curriculum to strengthen integrative learning. Mandatory establishment of skill laboratories and training in Basic Cardiac Life Support (BCLS), emergency care, and minor procedures. Digitization of medical education through the Education Life Cycle Management (ELCM) portal, Learning Management System (LMS), and e-learning modules. Strengthening of clinical exposure through internship postings at Primary Health Centres (PHCs), Community Health Centres (CHCs), and district hospitals. Introduction of Research Methodology at the undergraduate level and mandatory establishment of Research Methodology Departments at the postgraduate level. Mandatory appointment of modern medicine consultants (Physician, Surgeon, Gynaecologist and Pathologist) in Homoeopathic Medical Institutions under the Minimum Essential Standards (MES), 2024, to enhance interdisciplinary clinical training and collaborative patient care. Research methodology training for postgraduate students and faculty in collaboration with the Central Council for Research in Homoeopathy (CCRH). Formation of subject-wise committees to incorporate modern advancements under SMART (supplement modern advancement research and technology)-Hom. MoU between CCRH and NCH for elective courses on Good Clinical Practice (GCP) guidelines for clinical trials in Homoeopathy. Faculty training for implementation of CBDC, covering 3,145 undergraduate faculty, 602 postgraduate faculty, and 450 Medical Officers. CBDC trainings for UG and PG courses- conducted training for fourth year UG and PG subjects virtually-   HEB virtual training for UG- 16 June and 30 June 2026 and for PG – 18,25 and 26 May 2026. Total attendee UG were 1658 for five subject and for PG were Materia Medica-144, Organon -138, Psychiatry-43, Repertory- 132, Community Medicine-25, Research Methodology-73, Practice of Medicine- 96, Paediatrics-60, Homoeopathic Pharmacy-51 and Dermatology -7 Zone-wise capacity-building workshops on the AYUSH Education Portal. Online clinical research training programmes conducted during June–July 2022 covering around 600 faculty members and 2,300 postgraduate students. Conduction of National Teacher’s eligibility test in a year 2025 and 2026. Regular faculty development training cum interactive session for CBDC curriculum. Promotion of evidence-based education by encouraging undergraduate and postgraduate students and faculty to undertake research and publish research papers. Invited applications for the establishment of new Homoeopathic medical colleges/hospitals and enhancement of undergraduate and postgraduate seats. Periodic inspection and assessment of Homoeopathic medical colleges and attached hospitals to ensure compliance with prescribed standards. (C) Yoga Education: Ministry of Ayush promotes Yoga through its autonomous body, Morarji Desai National Institute of Yoga (MDNIY). MDNIY provides various courses for Yoga education. The activities and programmes of MDNIY are available on its website, https://www.yogamdniy.nic.in . This information was given by Union Minister of State (I/C) for Ayush, Shri Prataprao Jadhav in a written reply in Rajya Sabha today. *** SR/SV/SG (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2294220) आगंतुक पटल  : 197 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: हिन्दी , Tamil AYUSH Steps Taken to Promote Ayush Medicine प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                        04 AUG 2026 3:02PM by PIB Delhi Ministry of Ayush has undertaken various measures through regulatory bodies i.e. the National Commission for Indian System of Medicine (NCISM) and the National Commission for Homoeopathy (NCH), established under the National Commission for Indian System of Medicine Act, 2020 and the National Commission for Homoeopathy Act, 2020, respectively, to enhance the quality of medical education in Ayurveda, Unani, Siddha and Homoeopathy. The major steps taken during the last three years are annexed as Annexure. Public Health being a State subject, the primary responsibility for the establishment of new Ayush Educational Institutions comes under the purview of respective State Governments, including Uttarakhand. However, under the Centrally Sponsored Scheme of National Ayush Mission (NAM), there is a provision for financial assistance to the State/UT Governments for the establishment of new Ayush colleges where the availability of Ayush teaching institutions is inadequate in Government Sector. Accordingly, States/UTs may avail financial assistance by submitting suitable proposal through State Annual Action Plans (SAAPs) within the provision of NAM guidelines. However, the State Government of Uttarakhand has not submitted any proposal for establishment of new Ayush Educational Institute through SAAPs for Financial Year 2026-27. The Central Council for Research in Ayurvedic Sciences (CCRAS) an autonomous organisation operates a key research facility in Uttarakhand through its peripheral unit, namely the Regional Ayurveda Research Institute (RARI) located in Ranikhet (Tarikhet). At present, there is no proposal for the establishment of a new research institute in Uttarakhand. Annexure Major steps taken during the last three years to enhance the quality of medical education in Ayush systems (A) Step taken by the National Commission for Indian System of Medicine (NCISM) for Indian System of Medicine. (i) Regulations: To improve the quality of education in Ayurveda, Siddha & Unani the following regulations were framed, published and implemented by NCISM at the Undergraduate and Postgraduate level. National Commission for Indian System of Medicine (Minimum Standards of Undergraduate Ayurveda Education) Regulations-2022. National Commission for Indian System of Medicine (Minimum Standards of Undergraduate Unani Education), Regulations 2022. National Commission for Indian System of Medicine (Minimum Standard of Undergraduate Siddha Education) Regulations, 2022. National Commission for Indian System of Medicine (Recognition of Qualifications) Regulations, 2023. National Commission for Indian System of Medicine (National Examinations for Indian System of Medicine) Regulations, 2023. National Commission for Indian System of Medicine (Ethics and Registration) Regulations, 2023. National Commission for Indian System of Medicine (Minimum essential standards, assessment and rating for undergraduate Ayurveda colleges and attached teaching hospitals) Regulations, 2024. National Commission for Indian System of Medicine (Minimum Essential Standards, Assessment and Rating for Undergraduate Unani Colleges and Attached Teaching Hospitals) Regulations, 2023. National Commission for Indian System of Medicine (Minimum Essential Standards, Assessment and Rating for Undergraduate Siddha Colleges and Attached Teaching Hospitals) Regulations, 2024. National Commission for Indian System of Medicine (Minimum Essential Standards, Assessment and Rating for Postgraduate Institutions and Minimum Standards for Postgraduate Education in Ayurveda) Regulations, 2024. National Commission for Indian System of Medicine (Minimum Essential Standards, Assessment and Rating for Postgraduate Institutions and Minimum Standards of Postgraduate Siddha Education) Regulations, 2024. National Commission for Indian System of Medicine (Minimum Essential Standards, Assessment and Rating for Postgraduate Institutions and Minimum Standards of Postgraduate Unani Education) Regulations, 2024. National Commission for Indian System of Medicine (Pre-Ayurveda-Programme for Bachelor of Ayurvedic Medicine and Surgery) Regulations, 2024. (ii) Curriculum: To align with New Education Policy 2020, global standards in medical education, and to produce meritorious and skilled Ayurveda, Siddha & Unani graduates, NCISM has brought significant reforms in medical education policy, essential standards in education, educational administration, teaching/training methodologies, assessment process, technological assistance in education, and competency-based syllabus curriculum. The Board of Unani, Siddha and Sowa-Rigpa and Board of Ayurveda framed, published and implemented the following curriculum and syllabus. Competency based Course Curriculum and Syllabus for First Professional BSMS Competency based Course Curriculum and Syllabus for Second Professional BSMS Competency Based Dynamic Curriculum and Syllabus development for Third Professional BSMS. Competency based Course Curriculum and Syllabus for First Professional BAMS. Competency based Course Curriculum and Syllabus for Second Professional BAMS. Competency based Course Curriculum and Syllabus for Third Professional BAMS. Competency based Course Curriculum and Syllabus for First Professional BUMS. Competency based Course Curriculum and Syllabus for Second Professional BUMS. Competency Based Dynamic Curriculum and Syllabus for Third Professional BUMS. Outcome based Curriculum and Syllabus for Ayurveda Post Graduate program for Biostatistics. Outcome based Curriculum and Syllabus for Ayurveda Post Graduate program for Research Methodology. Competency based Course Curriculum and Syllabus for Siddha Post Graduate programme for Biostatistics. Competency based Course Curriculum and Syllabus Siddha Post Graduate programme for Research Methodology. Competency based Course Curriculum and Syllabus for Unani Post Graduate programme for Biostatistics. Competency based Course Curriculum and Syllabus for Unani Post Graduate programme for Research Methodology. Outcome Based Curriculum and Syllabus for Post Graduate Ayurveda for PG programs for the 2nd and 3rd-6th semesters. Competency Based Dynamic Curriculum and Syllabus for Post Graduate Siddha for 16 PG programs for the 2nd and 3rd-6th semesters. Competency Based Dynamic Curriculum and Syllabus for Post Graduate Unani for 15 PG programs for the 2nd and 3rd-6th semesters. (iii) Curriculum reforms at Undergraduate level: The ratio between Lecture and Non-Lecture hours has been reversed to 1:2 to promote professional skill, and soft skills. The introduction of electives is intended to provide opportunity to students to get introduced, oriented and exposed to various allied subjects, to build inter-disciplinary approach, and to promote self-directed/guided learning. Induction program with transitional curriculum has been introduced for newly admitted students before the commencement of regular classes. Competency Based Dynamic Curriculum and Syllabus h as been introduced with well-defined graduate’s attributes, programme outcomes, course outcomes, difficulty level, advanced teaching-training methods at par with global standards, formative assessment for continuous evaluation of the students, summative assessment methods, the blue print of the question paper, vertical/horizontal integration, etc. Early Clinical exposure begins with the first professional session to provide more clinical training exposure and build self-confidence. Separate hours for library, sports, and recreation in the regular time-table of all batches for effective utilisation of library, express talent in co/extracurricular events and promote physical and mental wellness. Methodologies for supplementation of modern advances, scientific and technological developments in Ayurveda, Siddha & Unani have been introduced. In addition to the university examination (summative assessment), formative assessment is introduced, which includes nine periodical tests and two term tests. Clinical Skill/ Simulation Lab introduced in Undergraduate for upliftment of clinical knowledge. (iv) Curriculum reforms at Post graduate level: Semester system has been introduced and semester specific subjects/ papers are maintained. Credit framework has been implemented in PG. Each credit will have lecture, practical training and experiential learning in the ratio of 1:2:3 to produce highly confident and competent specialist of concerned speciality. Formative Assessment including unit-wise assessment, modular assessment were introduced to calculate Semester Grade Point Average (SGPA) and to assess the eligibility to appear for university summative examination. Electives courses for post graduate program have been also introduced along with core Subjects under Domain specific and Capacity enhancing categories. Molecular Biology lab is introduced in Post Graduate institutes for carrying out advanced studies in immunology and histopathology related tests. Thrust areas for research are prescribed for each PG program along with speciality specific program out comes and promoted multi-disciplinary research. Department of integrative health and translational research has been implemented to regulate and coordinate research activities of PG institutions. (v) Other Initiatives by NCISM to increase the Quality of Education: An academic calendar for the entire course period is introduced to ensure uniform academic administrative patterns throughout the country. Each teacher is communicated with by mail with an article on teaching technology on the first Friday and a research article on the third Friday of every month to get updated knowledge in the area of education technology and research. (vi) Use of Technology: QR code embedded syllabus: uploaded on NCISM site. Elective courses through LMS (Learning Management System). NCISM platforms/portals under AYUSH Grid. Portal for Educational Planning and Administration Workshops for Principals in ISM. Portal for Entrepreneurship Development and training Programme Workshops for coordinators of Research and Innovation cell of ISM institutions. Portal for postgraduate guide orientation workshops for PG guides of ISM postgraduate institutions on Scientific writing, Research integrity and Publication ethics. Portal for textbook quality assessment as per the developed assessment scale. Software for framing ISM curriculum and syllabus. Educational Lifecycle Management System, Learning Management System and Collaborative System and integrated with Ayush Grid. Portal for Azadi ka Amrit Mahotsav activities in ISM institutions. Portal for online data submission of admitted students by institution and counselling authorities. Portal for electives. Portal for Degree recognition system. Developed portal for academic performance of ISM institutions. (vi)  Examinations: NCISM has implemented National Teachers’ Eligibility Test (NTET) for each discipline of Ayurveda, Siddha and Unani of Indian Systems of Medicine who desire to take up teaching profession. NCISM conducted NCISM PRE-TIB Exam, counselling and seat allotment for the admission of Unani Pre-Tib Program. National Entrance cum Eligibility Test (NEET) has been conducted by NTA for the admission of Undergraduate BAMS, BSMS and BUMS courses of Ayurveda, Siddha and Unani. All India AYUSH Post Graduate Entrance Test (AIAPGET) has been conducted by NCISM through NTA. (B) Step taken by the National Commission for Homoeopathy (NCH) (i) Regulations: To improve the quality of education in Homoeopathy the following regulations were framed, published and implemented by NCH at the undergraduate and postgraduate level: - National Commission for Homoeopathy (Homoeopathy Graduate Degree Course – Bachelor of Homoeopathic Medicine and Surgery (B.H.M.S). Regulations- 2022. National Commission for Homoeopathy (Professional Conduct, Etiquette and Code of Ethics for Practitioners of Homoeopathy) Regulations, 2022. National Commission for Homoeopathy (Manner of Preparation and Maintenance of National Register for Practitioner of Homoeopathy) Regulations, 2022. National Commission for Homoeopathy (General) Regulations, 2023. National Commission for Homoeopathy (Recognition of Qualification of Homoeopathy) Regulations 2023. National Commission for Homoeopathy (National Examinations in Homoeopathy) Regulations 2023. National Commission for Homoeopathy (Medical Research in Homoeopathy) Regulations 2023. National Commission for Homoeopathy (Assessment and Rating of Medical Institutions) Regulations, 2024. National Commission for Homoeopathy (Minimum Essential Standards For Homoeopathic Colleges And Attached Hospitals), Regulations - 2024. Establishment of New Homoeopathic Medical Institution (Opening of New or Higher Course of Study or Training and Increase of Intake Capacity by a Medical Institution), Regulations-2024. National Commission for Homoeopathy (Homoeopathy Post-Graduate Degree Course- Doctor of Medicine in Homoeopathy) Regulations, 2024. (ii) Other Initiatives by NCH to increase the Quality of Education: Implementation of the Competency-Based Dynamic Curriculum (CBDC) at undergraduate and postgraduate levels in line with NEP 2020. Introduction of research-oriented electives and Research Methodology in the curriculum. Inclusion of psychology, modern pharmacology and yoga subjects in the BHMS curriculum to strengthen integrative learning. Mandatory establishment of skill laboratories and training in Basic Cardiac Life Support (BCLS), emergency care, and minor procedures. Digitization of medical education through the Education Life Cycle Management (ELCM) portal, Learning Management System (LMS), and e-learning modules. Strengthening of clinical exposure through internship postings at Primary Health Centres (PHCs), Community Health Centres (CHCs), and district hospitals. Introduction of Research Methodology at the undergraduate level and mandatory establishment of Research Methodology Departments at the postgraduate level. Mandatory appointment of modern medicine consultants (Physician, Surgeon, Gynaecologist and Pathologist) in Homoeopathic Medical Institutions under the Minimum Essential Standards (MES), 2024, to enhance interdisciplinary clinical training and collaborative patient care. Research methodology training for postgraduate students and faculty in collaboration with the Central Council for Research in Homoeopathy (CCRH). Formation of subject-wise committees to incorporate modern advancements under SMART (supplement modern advancement research and technology)-Hom. MoU between CCRH and NCH for elective courses on Good Clinical Practice (GCP) guidelines for clinical trials in Homoeopathy. Faculty training for implementation of CBDC, covering 3,145 undergraduate faculty, 602 postgraduate faculty, and 450 Medical Officers. CBDC trainings for UG and PG courses- conducted training for fourth year UG and PG subjects virtually-   HEB virtual training for UG- 16 June and 30 June 2026 and for PG – 18,25 and 26 May 2026. Total attendee UG were 1658 for five subject and for PG were Materia Medica-144, Organon -138, Psychiatry-43, Repertory- 132, Community Medicine-25, Research Methodology-73, Practice of Medicine- 96, Paediatrics-60, Homoeopathic Pharmacy-51 and Dermatology -7 Zone-wise capacity-building workshops on the AYUSH Education Portal. Online clinical research training programmes conducted during June–July 2022 covering around 600 faculty members and 2,300 postgraduate students. Conduction of National Teacher’s eligibility test in a year 2025 and 2026. Regular faculty development training cum interactive session for CBDC curriculum. Promotion of evidence-based education by encouraging undergraduate and postgraduate students and faculty to undertake research and publish research papers. Invited applications for the establishment of new Homoeopathic medical colleges/hospitals and enhancement of undergraduate and postgraduate seats. Periodic inspection and assessment of Homoeopathic medical colleges and attached hospitals to ensure compliance with prescribed standards. (C) Yoga Education: Ministry of Ayush promotes Yoga through its autonomous body, Morarji Desai National Institute of Yoga (MDNIY). MDNIY provides various courses for Yoga education. The activities and programmes of MDNIY are available on its website, https://www.yogamdniy.nic.in . This information was given by Union Minister of State (I/C) for Ayush, Shri Prataprao Jadhav in a written reply in Rajya Sabha today. *** SR/SV/SG (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2294220)

title: Farmers voice strong support for Ethanol after meeting Union Agriculture Minister Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Agriculture &
Farmers Welfare Farmers voice strong support for Ethanol after meeting Union Agriculture Minister Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan AIKCC leaders said during the meeting with Union Minister Shri Shivraj Singh that Ethanol will increase farmers’ income and also secure the country’s energy During the meeting with Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan, farmers said, “Ethanol is a new opportunity for farming” “Farmers and the government should work together to break the wrong narrative on Ethanol”: AIKCC “Not petrol, but Ethanol coming from the fields is the future of the country,” Farmer leaders from various states told Union Minister Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan Open discussion held on Ethanol and farmers’ income by farmer leaders from across the country at Krishi Bhavan, New Delhi “The doors of Krishi Bhavan are open for farmers; farmers are like God”: Union Minister Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                04 AUG 2026 8:29PM by PIB Delhi A delegation of the All India Kisan Coordination Committee (AIKCC) met Union Minister of Agriculture and Farmers’ Welfare, and Rural Development, Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan on Tuesday and categorically stated that Ethanol is a big opportunity for the farming sector, provided its policy is farmer-centric and the correct price of the crop reaches the farmer directly. Union Agriculture Minister Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan carefully listened to all the suggestions of the farmer leaders and, while giving his guidance, assured that the Central Government will take the farmers’ views on Ethanol seriously. Shri Shivraj Singh said that farmers are like God for him and the doors of Krishi Bhavan are always open for farmers. Farmer leaders from across the country speak openly on Ethanol at Krishi Bhavan At Krishi Bhavan in New Delhi, a delegation of AIKCC met Union Agriculture Minister Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan. The delegation included farmer leaders from Punjab, Haryana, Maharashtra, Uttar Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, Telangana, Tamil Nadu and other parts of the country. The main focus of the meeting remained on Ethanol, farmers’ income, MSP (minimum support price), markets and the National Agriculture Policy. However, the farmers clearly said that they are in favour of Ethanol; they only want that the real benefit of this programme reaches the farmer and not only companies or middlemen. What farmers said in favour of Ethanol During the meeting, the farmer leaders made their stand on Ethanol clear and said that with Ethanol, the produce of the field will not remain limited only to the mandi (market), but will reach petrol pumps and the energy market. This will create a new and strong market for farmers. When Ethanol is made from sugarcane, maize, rice and other feedstocks, farmers will get more buyers and the problem of crop spoilage or storage will reduce. The farmers said that they are not against Ethanol but are fully in its support. However, it is necessary that proper prices of any crop, whether maize or sugarcane, reach the farmers. The farmer representatives said that they want an Ethanol policy to create a new path for farming and not become a new worry for them. They said they are with Ethanol, if Ethanol also is with them. ‘It is necessary to clear misunderstandings on Ethanol’ – Farmer leaders During the meeting, several farmer leaders said that confusion is being spread on social media and some platforms in the name of Ethanol – sometimes by saying that it damages vehicles, sometimes by saying that it harms farmers. The farmers demanded that the Union Agriculture Ministry and farmer organisations together clearly explain which crops will benefit in what way from Ethanol and how a shift can be made from water-intensive crops towards drought-tolerant crops. They said that to reach the young generation, it is necessary to show the correct picture of Ethanol through reels, short videos and ground-level meetings. Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan listened to suggestions and gave guidance Union Agriculture Minister Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan listened carefully to the farmers throughout and kept asking questions in between to understand the ground situation. He said that the thought process of the Central Government is clear – the benefit of the Ethanol programme should reach the entire chain, from the field to the fuel tank, but the largest share should go in the interest of the farmer. Shri Shivraj Chouhan said that Ethanol will strengthen the country’s energy security as well as the farmers’ pockets. Our emphasis is on ensuring that no crop and no state faces injustice. Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan gave the assurance in the meeting that the policy will be reviewed to maintain the balance of prices and demand of maize, rice, sugarcane and other feedstocks. Decisions will be taken only from the point of view of farmer interest, especially the benefit of maize farmers. Through the scientific studies and technical reports available on Ethanol, the negative narrative will be answered, and fact-based dialogue will be carried forward together with the farmers. Farmers’ views, Minister’s guidance – Message of partnership At the end of the meeting, the representatives of AIKCC said that they will take this message to the villages that the confusion regarding Ethanol will be broken on the basis of facts and ground experience, and the process of making policy in the interest of farmers will be strengthened by working together with the government. Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan also gave a clear message that farmer organisations are not opponents of the government but partners in policy. He said that we have carefully listened to the farmers’ views on Ethanol; now our work is to create such a framework on the basis of these suggestions in which the farmer, the country and energy – all three become strong. The AIKCC delegation included National President of AIKCC and former MP from Bharatiya Kisan Union (Mann) Shri Bhupinder Singh Mann, National Vice-President of AIKCC and President of National Association for Farmer Producer Organisations (NAFPO) Shri Binod Anand, National Vice-President of AIKCC Shri Gurusahib Singh Mann, National General Secretary of AIKCC and trainer of Shetkari Sanghatana (Sharad Joshi), Maharashtra Shri Gunwat Patil, Member of AIKCC and National General Secretary of Bharatiya Kisan Union Mann and President of Kisan Union Mann (UP) Shri Ajay Anmol, Member of AIKCC and Vice-President of Shetkari Sanghatana (Sharad Joshi), Maharashtra Shri Lalit Bahale Patil, Member of AIKCC and National General Secretary of Bharatiya Kisan Union Mann (Haryana) Shri Balraj Singh Sandhu, Member of AIKCC and President of BKU Mann (Haryana) Shri Surjit Singh Mani Gurjar, Member of AIKCC and State Vice-President of BKU Mann (Haryana) Shri Jugnu Rana, Member of AIKCC and State General Secretary of BKU Mann (Haryana) Shri Manphool Singh, Member of AIKCC and President of Vyamalan Kisan Sangathan (Tamil Nadu) Shri V. Manikkam, Member of AIKCC and President of Kisan Jagaran (Telangana) Shri Sugunakar Rao, Member of AIKCC and President of BKU Mann (Chandigarh) Shri Balwant Singh Nadiyali, Member of AIKCC and Spokesperson of Shetkari Sanghatana (Sharad Joshi), Maharashtra Shri Dinesh Sharma, Member of AIKCC and President of Malwa BKU Mann Shri Balveer Singh, and Member of AIKCC Shri Shivaraj Singh. **** RC/MS/MK (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2294576) आगंतुक पटल  : 37 Ministry of Agriculture &

title: AGRICULTURAL ROAD MAPS BASED ON AGRO-CLIMATIC CONDITIONS
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Agriculture &
Farmers Welfare AGRICULTURAL ROAD MAPS BASED ON AGRO-CLIMATIC CONDITIONS प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                04 AUG 2026 6:19PM by PIB Delhi As reported by the Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR), Agricultural Action Plans have been initiated for the States of Assam, Goa, Maharashtra, Uttarakhand, Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh, Andaman & Nicobar Islands. Comprehensive consultations have been undertaken with the concerned State Governments and other stakeholders for preparation of these agricultural Roadmaps. The Agricultural Roadmap are being prepared collaboratively by ICAR, Department of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare, ICAR, ICAR Institutes, State Governments, State Agricultural Universities, and experts. The planning is based on agro-climatic regions, natural resource endowments, climate resilience, technological interventions and farmers' needs. The roadmaps aim to ensure technical validation, alignment with State priorities, local agro-climatic conditions, and climate resilience. The Roadmap seek enhancement of productivity, profitability and resource-use efficiency in agriculture and allied sectors. The agricultural roadmaps is broad policy framework based on agro-climatic conditions. States/UTs may refer to these guiding principles while formulating annual action plans under various schemes.  The key outcomes of Agricultural Roadmap include enhancing farmers’ income, improve self-sufficiency in agricultural and allied commodities, generate rural employment opportunities and ensure sustainable growth of the agriculture sector, while addressing local agro-climatic conditions, climate resilience and farmers’ needs. This information was given by the Minister of State for Agriculture and Farmers Welfare SHRI RAMNATH THAKUR in a written reply in Lok Sabha today. ***** RC/MS (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2294463) आगंतुक पटल  : 178 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: Urdu , हिन्दी Ministry of Agriculture &

title: PREVENTION OF SOIL DEGRADATION
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Agriculture &
Farmers Welfare PREVENTION OF SOIL DEGRADATION प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                04 AUG 2026 6:18PM by PIB Delhi The Government has taken various measures to prevent soil degradation and promote judicious use of fertilizers, manures and herbicides by the farmers as follows- Balanced use of fertilizer is promoted under the Soil Health & Fertility Scheme, being implemented since 2014-15. Under the scheme, Soil Health Cards (SHCs) are generated which provide nutrient status of soil, based on which crop-wise fertilizer recommendations are provided to farmers, thereby promoting balanced and efficient nutrient management. SHC helps in enhancing crop productivity, reduce cultivation costs, and promote sustainable agriculture. So far, 26.09 crore Soil Health Cards have been generated and issued to farmers . 130627 farmer’s trainings, 7.17 lakh demonstrations, 7425 farmer’s Melas/ campaigns on soil health card recommendations have been organized across the country. National Mission on Natural Farming (NMNF) was approved by the Union Cabinet on 25 November 2024.  NMNF promotes chemical-free, nature-based farming practices using on-farm inputs. Under the scheme, 23.13 lakh farmers have been registered and 11.44 lakh hectares area have been covered, Government has adopted Integrated Pest Management (IPM) as cardinal principle and main plank of plant protection in the overall Crop Production Programme since 1985. IPM is an eco-friendly approach which encompasses cultural, mechanical, biological and need based chemical control measures. The Integrated Pest Management-cum-Locust Division of Directorate of Plant Protection, Quarantine and Storage ( DPPQ&S) promotes Integrated Pest Management (IPM) through its 48 Central Integrated Pest Management Centres (CIPMCs) and Locust-cum-CIPMCs located across 28 States and 2 UTs. Farmers are trained through Farmer Field Schools (FFS), 2-day HRD programmes, and safe & judicious use of pesticides awareness programmes. These programmes enable farmers to integrate cultural, mechanical and biological control measures. Special awareness Campaign and Khet Bachao Abhiyan  on balanced use of fertilizers have been conducted by Department of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare (DA&FW) and ICAR during the current Kharif Season 2026 wherein total  2,94,554 programs covering 1,36,73,465 farmers have been achieved. During the campaign, farmers have also been made aware on Natural/Organic Farming, bio-inputs, alternative fertilizers etc. Paramparagat Krishi Vikas Yojana (PKVY) is implemented since 2015-16.  PKVY promotes organic farming by providing end-to-end support covering production, processing, certification, and marketing. So far, 18.93 lakh hectares have been brought under organic farming and 33.63 lakh farmers have been benefited. Mission Organic Value Chain Development for North Eastern Region (MOVCDNER) is implemented since 2015-16 to promote organic farming in North Eastern States.  So far, 2.36 lakh hectares have been brought under organic farming and 2.74 lakh farmers have been benefited. The Government also promotes Soil Organic Carbon Enhancer namely, Fermented Organic Manure (FOM) /Liquid Fermented Organic Manure (LFOM) as a part of judicious use of fertilizers. During 2024-25, the annual consumption of FOM/LFOM was 3.36 LMT. During the current Kharif Season (1.4.2026 to 16.7.2026), the consumption of FOM/LFOM is 11.86 LMT. Indian Council of Agriculture Research (ICAR) through Directorate of Weed Research, Jabalpur is promoting sustainable Integrated Weed Management (IWM) for judicious use of herbicides in different crops and cropping systems through research, demonstrations, capacity building and extension programmes. The Directorate disseminates scientific advisories through mobile-based services, social media, printed literature and village-level extension programmes to promote the efficient and environmentally safe use of herbicides. The Directorate is also analyzing the herbicide residues in soil and food chain, and accordingly suggesting farmers for crop management practices. These interventions have significantly contributed in reducing the indiscriminate use of herbicides thereby improving soil health and crop productivity. title: RISKS AND CALAMITIES COVERED UNDER PMFBY
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Agriculture &
Farmers Welfare RISKS AND CALAMITIES COVERED UNDER PMFBY प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                04 AUG 2026 6:15PM by PIB Delhi The Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana ( PMFBY), introduced in the country from 2016-17,  is voluntary for the States as well as farmers.  The scheme  provides for comprehensive risk insurance against crop damage due to non-preventable natural risks from pre-sowing to post-harvest for the crops/areas notified by the concerned State Government.   The losses to crops due to wild animals, being preventable in nature, were therefore not covered earlier.  However, at the request of Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change and State Governments, States have been allowed to notify the losses by wild animals on individual assessment as add on cover at the cost of State Government.  Detailed protocol for such coverage has been provided in the Operational Guidelines of the scheme. Inundation as a risk cover is available to all notified crops under (PMFBY).  However, for hydrophilic crops like paddy, jute, mesta, sugarcane, such cover is available except in case of localized claims. This information was given by the Minister of State for Agriculture and Farmers Welfare SHRI RAMNATH THAKUR in a written reply in Lok Sabha today. ***** RC/MS (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2294455) आगंतुक पटल  : 134 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: Urdu , हिन्दी Ministry of Agriculture &

title: OILSEED AND PALM OIL PRODUCTION
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Agriculture &
Farmers Welfare OILSEED AND PALM OIL PRODUCTION प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                04 AUG 2026 6:12PM by PIB Delhi The National Mission on Edible Oils-Oilseeds (NMEO-OS) was approved on 3 rd October, 2024 to boost domestic oilseed production and to strive towards self-reliance (Atmanirbhar Bharat) in edible oils. The mission aims to increase primary oilseed production from 39 million tonnes (2022-23) to 69.7 million tonnes by 2030-31. The NMEO-OS is implemented through a cluster-based approach. Over 600 Value Chain Cluster have been identified across the country which is managed by Value Chain Partners such as Farmer Producer Organizations (FPOs), cooperatives and other agencies. Under these clusters, farmers are provided free high-quality seeds of latest high yielding varieties and training on good agricultural practices. T he mission supports the establishment and upgradation of post-harvest infrastructure (oil mills) to improve oil recovery from primary and secondary sources. The mission strengthens availability of certified seeds through 100% support for purchase of breeder seeds, establishment of new seed hubs and specialised seed storage units in the public sector to enhance production and storage capacity. The mission focuses on improving productivity through Frontline Demonstrations (FLDs), Cluster Frontline Demonstrations (CFLDs) and Block-Level Demonstrations (BLDs) to help farmers adopt latest varieties and good agricultural practices. Oilseed production has increased from 39.67 million tonnes in 2023-24 to 43.06 million tonnes in 2025-26 (3 rd Advance Estimate, DA&FW). Under the mission, 13.52 lakh hectares were covered under free seed distribution in Value Chain Clusters during 2025-26, against the annual target of 10.00 lakh hectares. 60 Seed Hubs & 50 specialized seed storage units have been sanctioned for production of Breeder Seed of recently released varieties. As reported by the Directorate of Sugar & Vegetable Oils, Department of Food and Public Distribution, India imported 160.72 lakh tonnes of edible oils during 2024–25. Of this, 75.17 lakh tonnes comprised palm oil, accounting for 46.77% of the total edible oil imports. The Government of India launched the National Mission on Edible Oils–Oil Palm (NMEO-OP) in August 2021 to promote oil palm cultivation, with special focus on North Eastern States. The Mission is being implemented in 15 States. The mission provides comprehensive support to farmers, including assistance for high quality planting materials, inputs for intercropping and maintenance during the four year gestation period. There is also a provision for replanting of old and unproductive plantations. The mission supports farm machinery, irrigation facilities, seed gardens, nurseries and Custom Hiring Centres. The North Eastern States are provided financial assistance for setting up oil palm processing mills. From 2021-22 to 2025-26, 2.73 lakh hectares was brought under oil palm cultivation, taking the cumulative area to 6.40 lakh hectares as on 31.03.2026. During this period, 114.66 lakh tonnes of Fresh Fruit Bunches (FFBs) were harvested, resulting in the production of 20.10 lakh tonnes of Crude Palm Oil (CPO). At present, 27 oil palm processing mills are operational across the country. The Mission provides Viability Gap Payment (VGP) to support oil palm growers. As on date, ₹18.90 crore has been disbursed to 9,244 oil palm farmers in Goa, Tamil Nadu, Gujarat, Karnataka, Odisha, Arunachal Pradesh, Assam, and Mizoram under this provision. This information was given by the Minister of State for Agriculture and Farmers Welfare SHRI RAMNATH THAKUR in a written reply in Lok Sabha today. ***** RC/MS (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2294450) आगंतुक पटल  : 158 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: हिन्दी Ministry of Agriculture &

title: MINIMUM SUPPORT PRICES (MSPs) FOR ALL CROPS
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Agriculture &
Farmers Welfare MINIMUM SUPPORT PRICES (MSPs) FOR ALL CROPS प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                04 AUG 2026 6:10PM by PIB Delhi Every year, Government fixes Minimum Support Prices (MSPs) for 22 mandated agricultural crops for the country as a whole, based on the recommendations of the Commission for Agricultural Costs & Prices (CACP), after considering the views of the State Governments and Central Ministries / Departments concerned. The Union Budget for  2018-19 had announced the pre-determined principle to keep MSPs at levels of at least one and half times of the cost of production. Accordingly, Government had increased MSPs for all mandated Kharif, Rabi and other commercial crops with a minimum margin of 50 percent over all India weighted average cost of production from year 2018-19 onwards. Out of the total production, only marketable surplus is available for procurement by Government agencies when market price of these produce fall below the MSP. Government procures cereals and coarse cereals through Food Corporation of India (FCI) and other designated State Agencies to provide price support to the farmers. Procurement of pulses, oilseeds and copra is done under Price Support Scheme under umbrella scheme of Pradhan Mantri Annadata Aay Sanrakshan Abhiyan (PM-AASHA), on the request of the concerned State Government as per the guidelines as and when market price of these produce fall below the MSP. Procurement agencies under PM-AASHA Scheme are National Agricultural Cooperative Marketing Federation of India Ltd (NAFED) and National Co-operative Consumers' Federation of India Ltd. (NCCF). Cotton and Jute are also procured by Government at MSP through Cotton Corporation of India (CCI) and Jute Corporation of India (JCI), respectively. In addition, Adequate number of procurement centres are opened by respective State Government Agencies, taking into account the production, marketable surplus, convenience of farmers and availability of other logistics / infrastructure such as storage and transportation etc. Temporary purchase centres, in addition to the existing mandis and depots/godowns are also established at key points. The procurement operation is a continuously evolving process and during the last few years, procurement processes under MSP have improved to ensure payment of MSP to farmer’s bank account directly and linkage of Aadhaar and land records with the States’ procurement portals ensure that the farmers directly get the benefits of the MSP purchase. Government has launched Mission for Aatmanirbharta in Pulses till 2030-31, to reduce import dependence and achieve self-sufficiency in pulses. To encourage domestic production of  pulses, the Government is undertaking procurement of Tur, Urad and Masur under the PM-AASHA Scheme on the request of State Government from pre-registered farmers as much as offered by them through Central Nodal Agencies, namely the National Agricultural Cooperative Marketing Federation of India Ltd. (NAFED) and the National Cooperative Consumers' Federation of India Limited (NCCF). Government also implements Market Intervention Scheme (MIS), a component under PM-AASHA, for procurement of agricultural and horticultural commodities, which are perishable in nature and are not covered under the Price Support Scheme (PSS). The objective of intervention is to protect the growers of these commodities from making distress sale in the event of a bumper crop during the peak arrival period when the prices tend to fall below economic levels and the cost of production. There should be at least a 10 percent decrease in the ruling market prices over the previous normal year. The scheme is implemented at the request of a State/UT government. Government has introduced a new component of Price Differential Payment (PDP) under Market intervention scheme (MIS) from 2024-25 season for direct payment of the price difference between the Market Intervention Price (MIP) and the selling price to the farmers of perishable crops. States/UTs have an option to choose either to do physical procurement of the crop or to make the differential payment between the MIP & Sale Price to the farmers. Further, from 2024-25 season, Government added another component under Market intervention scheme (MIS) for reimbursing the Storage and Transportation cost of TOP crops (Tomato, Onion and Potato) to central nodal agencies & State designated agencies for transporting them from the producing State to consuming states in the interest of the farmers. Increased MSP has benefited farmers of the country which are evident from data of procurement and MSP amount paid to the farmers. The details of procurement and MSP amount paid to farmers during 2021-22 to 2025-26 (upto June, 2026) are given as under: Procurement and MSP amount paid to farmers during last five years 2021-22 to 2025-26 Total Procurement (In LMT) Total MSP Value (In lakh Crore) 5781 14.58 The total procurement of all 22 MSP crops has increased from 6,987 Lakh Metric Tonne (LMT) during 2004-14 to 12,819 LMT during 2014-26(upto June 2026). The MSP amount paid to farmers has increased from Rs. 7.41 Lakh Crores during 2004-14 to Rs. 27.80 Lakh crores during 2014-26 (upto June 2026). The Government is implementing several policies, reforms, developmental programmes to increase agricultural productivity, reduce the cost of cultivation, promote crop diversification, ensure remunerative returns and provide income support to farmers. These various schemes / programmes cover the entire spectrum of agriculture including credit, insurance,income support, infrastructure, crops including horticulture, seeds, mechanization,marketing, organic and natural farming, farmer collectives, irrigation, extension activities,procurement of crops, digital agriculture etc. This information was given by the Minister of State for Agriculture and Farmers Welfare SHRI RAMNATH THAKUR in a written reply in Lok Sabha today. ***** RC/MS (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2294446) आगंतुक पटल  : 267 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: Urdu , हिन्दी , Telugu Ministry of Agriculture &

title: SUPPORT FOR FARMER PRODUCER ORGANISATION
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Agriculture &
Farmers Welfare SUPPORT FOR FARMER PRODUCER ORGANISATION प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                04 AUG 2026 6:07PM by PIB Delhi The Government is implementing the Central Sector Scheme for "Formation and Promotion of 10,000 Farmer Producer Organizations (FPOs). 10,000 FPOs have been formed under the scheme since 2020-21. FPOs undertake a wide range of business activities including agri-input supply, aggregation and trading of agricultural produce, value addition and processing, seed production, digital commerce through e-market places, custom hiring services & export promotion. From the audited financial statements 2024-25 of the scheme FPOs, 6964 FPOs had a turnover of up to Rs.50 Lakh, 862 FPOs had a turnover of Rs.50 Lakh to Rs.1 Crore and 1135 FPOs had a turnover of over Rs.1 Crore. The National Academy of Agricultural Sciences, in Policy Paper No. 144, covers all FPOs registered in the country. title: ICAR's Genome Breakthrough Paves Way for Better Pigeonpea Varieties
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Agriculture &
Farmers Welfare ICAR's Genome Breakthrough Paves Way for Better Pigeonpea Varieties ICAR-developed sequence approved as the global reference genome of pigeonpea, making it India's first fully annotated telomere-to-telomere (T2T) reference genome High-quality genetic blueprint expected to accelerate development of climate-resilient, high-yielding and nutritious pigeonpea varieties, strengthening India's self-reliance in pulses Latest milestone builds on ICAR-NIPB's pioneering work that produced the world's first draft genome of a pulse crop in 2011 प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                04 AUG 2026 6:02PM by PIB Delhi In a major scientific breakthrough Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR) has developed India's first fully annotated telomere-to-telomere (T2T) reference genome of pigeonpea ( Cajanus cajan L. Millsp.) variety 'Asha'. Popularly known as ‘Arhar’ or ‘Tur’, pigeonpea is one of India's most important pulse crops and a major source of dietary protein. It plays a vital role in ensuring the country's food and nutritional security. The breakthrough builds on the pioneering work of ICAR–National Institute for Plant Biotechnology, New Delhi in pigeonpea genomics. In 2011, the institute published the world's first draft genome of a pulse crop, pigeonpea variety 'Asha', which was also the first crop genome to be sequenced entirely in India. An improved version of the draft genome was published in 2017, and the latest achievement represents its complete telomere-to-telomere (T2T) genome sequence, providing the most comprehensive genetic blueprint of the crop to date. The newly developed T2T genome sequence contains 752.65 million base pairs of DNA assembled into 92 contigs, providing a complete representation of all 11 chromosomes of pigeonpea. The genome assembly, designated NIPB_CcT2T_4, has been deposited in the global database (NCBI) under accession number GCF_000230855.1 and was released on 20 April 2026. The genome assembly comprises all 11 chromosomes, including all 11 centromeres and 22 telomeres, demonstrating chromosome-level completeness. A comprehensive genome annotation identified 36,557 genes, producing 48,008 mRNAs (coding sequences). Transcriptome (RNA sequence) mapping recorded more than 99.9% read alignment, confirming the high accuracy and completeness of the genome. The fully annotated T2T reference genome marks a significant milestone in India's pulse research ecosystem. It will serve as a valuable national genomic resource for advanced gene and pangenome analyses, discovery of genes associated with important agronomic and nutritional traits, and the application of molecular breeding and genome-editing technologies. The development is expected to accelerate the breeding of climate-resilient, high-yielding and nutritionally enriched pigeonpea varieties, thereby strengthening the country's pulse improvement programme. The achievement will provide a major impetus to research and innovation, benefit scientists, breeders and farmers, and contribute to enhanced productivity, improved farmer livelihoods, and India's food and nutritional security. The ICAR plays a pivotal role by developing high-yielding, pest-resistant, and climate-resilient pulse varieties, supervising breeder seed production, conducting multi-location trials, demonstrating improved production technologies through its institutes and Krishi Vigyan Kendras (KVKs), and providing scientific support for capacity building and technology dissemination to farmers across the country. The Government of India launched the Mission for ‘Aatmanirbharta in Pulses’ (2025-26 to 2030-31) to achieve self-sufficiency in pulse production, reduce import dependence, and enhance farmers' income through improved seeds, area expansion, technology adoption, assured procurement, and strengthened post-harvest infrastructure. The mission aims to increase pulse production to about 35 million tonnes by 2030–31 through a comprehensive strategy involving research, seed systems, and extension services. ➡️ NCBI URL link for the Reference Genome of the Pigeonpea (Arhar/Tur Dal) https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/datasets/genome/GCF_000230855.2/ ➡️ REVIEW PAPER Genetic and genomic resources for accelerating marker-assisted ideotype breeding in pigeonpea (Cajanus cajan L.
