title: CROP DIVERSIFICATION AND MICRO IRRIGATION
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Agriculture &
Farmers Welfare CROP DIVERSIFICATION AND MICRO IRRIGATION प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                04 AUG 2026 4:18PM by PIB Delhi The Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR), Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers’ Welfare has studied the prevailing cropping pattern and hydrological realities in different regions of India.  ICAR study using Central Ground Water Board (CGWB) data and monthly gridded GRACE satellite data indicated the mismatch between the water demand of existed cropping patterns and water availability in groundwater depleted states particularly in Punjab, Haryana, Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Maharashtra, Karnataka, and Tamil Nadu, encompassing the arid and semi-arid climates of the Country.  ICAR has also prepared ‘Atlas of cropping systems in India’ and also identified alternative cropping systems as sustainable alternatives to cereal-dominated systems considering the prevailing agro-climatic conditions, resource availability including water availability and market opportunities. Further, ICAR has prepared the agro-ecological and district specific crop plan for 14 major crops namely rice, wheat, maize, pearl millet, sorghum, pigeon pea, chickpea, soybean, mustard, groundnut, cotton, sugarcane, potato and onion by combining the Relative Spread Index (RSI), Relative Yield Index (RYI), Sustainable Yield Index (SYI) and Soil-climate suitability index (SCSI). Rice, sugarcane, cotton and jute are among the major water-intensive crops grown in India and together occupy about 62.7 million hectares, representing nearly one-third of the country's gross cropped area. Recognizing the need to align cropping patterns with local water availability, ICAR assessed the cultivation of major water-intensive crops in relation to rainfall and water availability. The assessment identified that about 2.89 million hectares of rice are cultivated in 68 districts receiving less than 650 mm annual rainfall, accounting for about 5.67% of the total rice area (51 million hectares).   Similarly, about 0.721 million hectares of sugarcane are cultivated in 91 districts receiving less than 700 mm annual rainfall, representing about 10.76% of the total sugarcane cultivated area (6.7 million hectares). These assessments provide the scientific basis for promoting location-specific crop diversification, particularly in water-scarce regions experiencing recurring water stress and declining groundwater levels, while balancing water security, farmer livelihoods and agricultural productivity. The Government is promoting crop diversification from water-intensive crops to relatively low water-requiring crops such as pulses, oilseeds, millets and horticultural crops, taking into account local water availability, soil characteristics, agro-climatic suitability and sustainable use of natural resources. Under the Pilot Project on Crop Diversification, ICAR has implemented location-specific crop diversification interventions in 47 identified districts based on these criteria. To support diversified cropping systems, ICAR has also standardized and promoted optimum irrigation scheduling and drip fertigation for different crops to enhance water-use efficiency and productivity. Further, during 2023–24 to 2025–26, ICAR organized 457 training programmes, benefiting 8,749 farmers and 4,592 extension functionaries, to promote scientific crop diversification and sustainable crop management practices. The Government is implementing several schemes and programmes to promote sustainable agriculture, micro-irrigation, soil health management and efficient utilisation of natural resources. The Prime Minister Dhan-Dhaanya Krishi Yojana (PM-DDKY) promotes sustainable agriculture in 100 aspirational agricultural districts through convergence of interventions such as crop diversification, irrigation development, post-harvest infrastructure, natural and organic farming, Integrated Pest Management (IPM) and Integrated Nutrient Management (INM). The Per Drop More Crop (PDMC) component of the Pradhan Mantri Krishi Sinchayee Yojana (PMKSY) promotes efficient use of irrigation water through adoption of drip and sprinkler irrigation systems. The Soil Health Card Programme promotes soil test-based balanced and integrated nutrient management by providing farmers with crop-specific fertilizer recommendations for improving soil fertility and nutrient use efficiency. Further, the Watershed Development Component of PMKSY (WDC–PMKSY 2.0) promotes integrated watershed management through soil and water conservation, rainwater harvesting, groundwater recharge, restoration of degraded lands and sustainable management of natural resources. In addition, ICAR promotes soil health management through soil test-based balanced and Integrated Nutrient Management (INM), Soil Test Crop Response (STCR)-based general fertilizer recommendations, and micronutrient mapping with location-specific nutrient recommendations. The Council has developed rapid and efficient soil testing kits and digital decision-support tools to facilitate timely soil fertility assessment and site-specific nutrient management. These technologies are disseminated through Krishi Vigyan Kendras (KVKs), frontline demonstrations and farmer capacity-building programmes to promote balanced fertilization, improve nutrient use efficiency and sustain soil health. The Government is promoting long-term water security and climate-resilient agriculture through research, technology development and field demonstrations led by the Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR). The initiatives include rainwater harvesting, creation of farm ponds and other surface water storage structures, groundwater recharge, conjunctive use of surface and groundwater, multiple use of harvested water, in-situ moisture conservation, conservation agriculture, in-situ moisture conservation, protective irrigation, micro-irrigation, and AI-, sensor- and weather-based irrigation scheduling, and advisory systems to improve water-use efficiency and climate resilience,  and crop diversification from water-intensive crops to pulses, oilseeds, maize and agroforestry. ICAR also promotes micro-irrigation, Direct Seeded Rice (DSR), System of Rice Intensification (SRI), Alternate Wetting and Drying (AWD), raised-bed planting, laser land levelling, mulching, sprinkler and drip irrigation, and climate-resilient, water-efficient crop varieties through farmer training, frontline demonstrations, through Krishi Vigyan Kendras (KVKs) and State extension agencies. The Government is strengthening the resilience of Indian agriculture to climate variability through research, technology development and field-level interventions complemented by flagship Government schemes. Under the National Innovations in Climate Resilient Agriculture (NICRA), ICAR promotes climate-resilient crop varieties tolerant to drought, flood, salinity and heat stress, Climate Resilient Villages (CRVs) in 151 vulnerable districts, District Agriculture Contingency Plans prepared for 651 districts, along with weather-based agro-advisories and farmer capacity building through Krishi Vigyan Kendras (KVKs). These initiatives are supported through Government schemes such as the National Mission for Sustainable Agriculture (NMSA), Pradhan Mantri Krishi Sinchayee Yojana (PMKSY) – Per Drop More Crop (PDMC), Watershed Development Component of PMKSY (WDC-PMKSY 2.0) and the Prime Minister Dhan-Dhaanya Krishi Yojana (PM-DDKY), which improve resilience to climate variability and support environmentally sustainable agricultural practices. This information was given by Minister of State for Agriculture and Farmers Welfare, Shri Bhagirath Choudhary in a written reply in Lok Sabha today. * **** RC/MS (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2294287) आगंतुक पटल  : 286 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: हिन्दी , Bengali Ministry of Agriculture &

title: Indigenous African Swine Fever (ASF) Vaccine Developed by ICAR Bolsters India's Biosecurity
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Agriculture &
Farmers Welfare Indigenous African Swine Fever (ASF) Vaccine Developed by ICAR Bolsters India's Biosecurity Union Agriculture Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan, in the Presence of Union Minister Rajiv Ranjan Singh, dedicates Vaccine to the Nation at this Year’s ICAR Foundation Day A major step towards Atmanirbhar Bharat in veterinary vaccine development, with the potential to position India as a global supplier of affordable ASF vaccines प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                04 AUG 2026 4:14PM by PIB Delhi African Swine Fever (ASF), caused by the African Swine Fever Virus (ASFV), is one of the most devastating trans-boundary animal disease affecting domestic and wild pigs worldwide. Characterised by high fever, haemorrhages and mortality rates that may approach 100 per cent, the disease has caused severe socio-economic losses to the global pig farming sector. Since its first detection in India in 2020, ASF has spread to several States and Union Territories, resulting in massive pig mortality, disruption of pig production, restrictions on animal movement and trade, and significant livelihood losses for smallholder pig farmers, particularly in the North-Eastern region. In the absence of an effective treatment or a commercially approved vaccine in India, disease control has largely relied on rapid diagnosis, culling of infected animals and strict biosecurity measures. The economic impact of ASF outbreaks in India has been significant. During the initial outbreaks in Assam in 2020 and 2021, pig mortality and culling resulted in estimated losses of approximately ₹276 crore. In Mizoram, ASF outbreaks have reportedly affected more than 11,382 households up to 2025, resulting in an estimated financial loss of approximately ₹982 crore. These outbreaks have highlighted the urgent need for an effective indigenous soultion to strengthen disease preparedness, protect farmers' livelihoods and build resilience in the country's pig farming sector. Addressing this critical challenge, scientists at ICAR–National Institute of High Security Animal Diseases (ICAR-NIHSAD), Bhopal, have developed India's first indigenous MA-104_Cell_Line-Based Live Attenuated African Swine Fever (ASF) Vaccine for pigs. Developed using a novel attenuated ASFV Genotype II virus with unique gene deletions in the MA-104 cell line, the vaccine is a major breakthrough in veterinary research and is well suited for large-scale production. The vaccine has successfully undergone comprehensive laboratory evaluation, including sterility, purity, safety, genetic stability, immunogenicity, protective efficacy and virulence reversion studies. It was also field validated in collaboration with the Department of Animal Husbandry & Dairying (DAHD), Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying, Government of India, further establishing its safety and efficacy under field conditions. The vaccine is recommended for healthy pigs above eight weeks of age and is administered as a 1 mL intramuscular injection, followed by a booster dose 14 days after the primary vaccination. The indigenous vaccine is expected to substantially reduce pig mortality, minimise economic losses and improve the livelihoods of pig farmers across the country. By providing an effective preventive tool against one of the world's most destructive livestock diseases, it will significantly strengthen India's animal health security and support the sustainable growth of the pig farming sector. Dr. M.L. Jat, Secretary, DARE and Director General, ICAR said that this breakthrough marks the dawn of a new era in veterinary science. It reflects India's growing scientific capability to develop world-class animal health solutions and paves the way for a new generation of indigenously developed vaccines and innovative technologies that will strengthen livestock health, enhance disease preparedness, and support the nation's food and biosecurity. At present, only a couple of commercially licensed ASF vaccines are available in Vietnam. These vaccines are produced using patented proprietary cell lines. In contrast, the indigenous vaccine developed by ICAR-NIHSAD uses the widely available MA-104 cell line, making it a major technological breakthrough. This eliminates dependence on proprietary manufacturing platforms, enables large-scale vaccine production and significantly brings down manufacturing costs. **** RC/MS (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2294280) आगंतुक पटल  : 346 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: Gujarati , Urdu , हिन्दी , Marathi , Tamil , Telugu , Malayalam Ministry of Agriculture &

Addressing this critical challenge, scientists at ICAR–National Institute of High Security Animal Diseases (ICAR-NIHSAD), Bhopal, have developed India's first indigenous MA-104_Cell_Line-Based Live Attenuated African Swine Fever (ASF) Vaccine for pigs. Developed using a novel attenuated ASFV Genotype II virus with unique gene deletions in the MA-104 cell line, the vaccine is a major breakthrough in veterinary research and is well suited for large-scale production. The vaccine has successfully undergone comprehensive laboratory evaluation, including sterility, purity, safety, genetic stability, immunogenicity, protective efficacy and virulence reversion studies. It was also field validated in collaboration with the Department of Animal Husbandry & Dairying (DAHD), Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying, Government of India, further establishing its safety and efficacy under field conditions. The vaccine is recommended for healthy pigs above eight weeks of age and is administered as a 1 mL intramuscular injection, followed by a booster dose 14 days after the primary vaccination. The indigenous vaccine is expected to substantially reduce pig mortality, minimise economic losses and improve the livelihoods of pig farmers across the country. By providing an effective preventive tool against one of the world's most destructive livestock diseases, it will significantly strengthen India's animal health security and support the sustainable growth of the pig farming sector. Dr. M.L. Jat, Secretary, DARE and Director General, ICAR said that this breakthrough marks the dawn of a new era in veterinary science. It reflects India's growing scientific capability to develop world-class animal health solutions and paves the way for a new generation of indigenously developed vaccines and innovative technologies that will strengthen livestock health, enhance disease preparedness, and support the nation's food and biosecurity. At present, only a couple of commercially licensed ASF vaccines are available in Vietnam. These vaccines are produced using patented proprietary cell lines. In contrast, the indigenous vaccine developed by ICAR-NIHSAD uses the widely available MA-104 cell line, making it a major technological breakthrough. This eliminates dependence on proprietary manufacturing platforms, enables large-scale vaccine production and significantly brings down manufacturing costs. **** RC/MS (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2294280)

title: Incident involving Air India Flight AI2379 (Phuket–Delhi) on 04.08.2026
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Civil Aviation Incident involving Air India Flight AI2379 (Phuket–Delhi) on 04.08.2026 प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                04 AUG 2026 7:56PM by PIB Delhi On 04.08.2026, Air India Flight AI2379, operated by an Airbus A320 aircraft (VT-EXO) from Phuket to Delhi, experienced a momentary altitude variation during flight. The aircraft subsequently stabilised and landed safely at Indira Gandhi International Airport, Delhi. The flight was carrying 137 passengers, including 3 infants, and 8 crew members (2 pilots and 6 cabin crew). Immediately upon landing, medical teams attended to all passengers and crew as a precautionary measure. Eight passengers and four cabin crew members have been admitted to hospitals for detailed medical evaluation and treatment. All admitted passengers and crew members are stable and are being provided with adequate medical care and attention. The remaining passengers were provided the necessary assistance and support. Hon’ble Minister of Civil Aviation personally visited Fortis Hospital, accompanied by the Secretary, Ministry of Civil Aviation and DG DGCA to enquire about the condition of the injured passengers and assure them of all necessary assistance. Senior officers of the Ministry have also visited Fortis and Medanta Hospitals and are closely coordinating with the hospital authorities and the airline to ensure the best possible medical care and all necessary support to the injured. The aircraft has been moved to the hangar and the Flight Data Recorder and Cockpit Voice Recorder have been secured for detailed examination. DGCA has initiated a detailed investigation into the occurrence. The Ministry of Civil Aviation and DGCA are closely monitoring the situation. Passenger safety remains the highest priority, and all necessary measures are being taken. ***** Divyanshu Kumar (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2294547) आगंतुक पटल  : 344 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: Gujarati Ministry of Civil Aviation Incident involving Air India Flight AI2379 (Phuket–Delhi) on 04.08.2026 प्रविष्टि तिथि:

title: Six Coal Blocks Successfully Auctioned in the 15th Round and 2nd attempt of 13th Round of Commercial Auctions
content:

                04 AUG 2026 7:20PM by PIB Delhi The Ministry of Coal have successfully auctioned six coal blocks under the 15 th round and 2 nd Attempt of 13 th Round of commercial coal mine auctions. The ministry launched the said rounds of commercial coal block auctions on April 17, 2026. title: Dipka OC: Powering India's Growth through Scale, Efficiency and Sustainable Mining
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Coal Dipka OC: Powering India's Growth through Scale, Efficiency and Sustainable Mining प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                04 AUG 2026 12:53PM by PIB Delhi Dipka OCP of South Eastern Coalfields Limited (SECL) stands out as one of the most vivid reflections of the remarkable transformation of India's coal mining sector. From producing barely 1 million tonne of coal in 1992, Dipka OC has evolved into one of the largest coal-producing complexes in the country, recording an all-time high production of 37.5 million tonnes and despatch of 39.43 million tonnes during FY 2025-26. With the recent enhancement of Environmental Clearance to 40 MTPA and a well-defined roadmap towards 60 MTPA, Dipka OC today stands as a strategic national asset, combining scale, efficiency and sustainability in equal measure. A Strong Start to FY 2026-27 Building upon last year's record performance, Dipka OC has begun the current financial year with equally impressive momentum. Up to 25 July 2026, the mine has produced 12.66 million tonnes of coal, achieving 104% of the progressive production target. Even more encouraging is the 30.5% year-on-year growth in coal production compared to the corresponding period of the previous year, reflecting substantial improvement in mine productivity and equipment utilisation. Coal dispatch has been equally robust, touching 13.87 million tonnes, exceeding the progressive target by achieving 109%, thereby ensuring uninterrupted fuel supply to thermal power stations and industrial consumers. The seamless synchronization between coal production and despatch demonstrates Dipka's operational maturity, where mining, transportation and logistics function as an integrated value chain rather than as isolated activities. Creating Value Beyond Production While production remains the principal indicator of mining performance, Dipka's success is equally reflected in its financial contribution. During FY 2025-26, the mine generated an overall profit of ₹3,230.91 crore, making it one of the strongest profit centres within SECL. Profitability has improved not merely because of higher production but also due to better cost management and enhanced operational efficiency. With profit per tonne increasing to ₹827, the mine has demonstrated that large-scale production can be achieved without proportionate escalation in operating costs. These financial outcomes underline Dipka's growing contribution to Coal India Limited's overall profitability. Strengthening the Foundation for Future Growth Behind Dipka's impressive production performance lies a series of strategic initiatives that have strengthened the mine's long-term production capability. Among these, land acquisition and rehabilitation have emerged as the most significant enablers for sustained capacity expansion. Following the successful possession of Malgaon village, the Area has made substantial progress towards rehabilitation and resettlement of Hardi Bazar, one of the largest and most complex R&R initiatives in the region. Rather than viewing rehabilitation merely as a statutory obligation, Dipka has adopted a development-oriented approach by initiating development of a well-planned rehabilitation township equipped with essential civic infrastructure, including roads, schools, healthcare facilities, community amenities and public utilities. This participative and transparent approach has facilitated progressive land availability for mining while strengthening stakeholder confidence and social acceptance of the project. Infrastructure that Supports High Production Large-scale mining demands equally robust evacuation infrastructure. Dipka possesses one of the most diversified coal evacuation systems in Coal India Limited, comprising MGR-connected silos, First Mile Connectivity (FMC) silos, railway loading facilities and road transport systems. This integrated network provides operational flexibility and enables uninterrupted dispatch to major consumers, including NTPC Sipat and several thermal power stations across western and central India. Efficient evacuation has ensured that increasing production is promptly translated into higher consumer supplies without creating stock accumulation at the pithead. Technology Driving Productivity Dipka's remarkable production journey has been powered by sustained investment in technology and modernization. The mine has progressively upgraded its mining systems with 42-cubic metre electric rope shovels, high-capacity surface miners, long in-pit belt conveyor systems, advanced silo loading facilities, drone-based mine monitoring and digital mine management platforms. These technologies have significantly improved equipment productivity, optimized mine planning, reduced operational delays and strengthened monitoring of mining activities. As production volumes continue to grow, technology remains one of the strongest differentiators enabling Dipka to maintain high operational efficiency. Responsible Mining for Sustainable Growth Dipka has demonstrated that high production and environmental stewardship can progress together. The Area has implemented an array of initiatives including Continuous Ambient Air Quality Monitoring Systems (CAAQMS), fog cannon-based dust suppression, wheel washing systems, plantation drives, deployment of electric vehicles and plastic waste recycling facilities. These measures have substantially strengthened environmental management while improving the overall sustainability of mining operations. Digital environmental monitoring through integrated online platforms has further enhanced regulatory compliance and operational transparency. At the same time, systematic rehabilitation and development of modern resettlement infrastructure have enabled timely land availability for future mining while maintaining constructive engagement with project-affected families. This balanced approach has significantly strengthened the long-term production outlook of the Area. Looking Beyond 40 Million Tonnes The recent enhancement of Environmental Clearance to 40 MTPA represents not the culmination but the beginning of Dipka's next growth phase. With progressive land acquisition, ongoing rehabilitation, infrastructure augmentation and a clear vision for expansion to 60 MTPA, the mine possesses all the essential ingredients for sustained high performance. Dipka's journey is a compelling example of how scientific mine planning, technological innovation, financial discipline and responsible mining can collectively create a world-class mining operation. As one of Coal India Limited's flagship producing mines, Dipka continues to set new benchmarks in production, profitability, operational efficiency and environmental responsibility while making an ever-growing contribution to India's energy security. **** Shuhaib T (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2294174) आगंतुक पटल  : 439 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: Urdu , हिन्दी , Tamil , Telugu Ministry of Coal Dipka OC: Powering India's Growth through Scale, Efficiency and Sustainable Mining प्रविष्टि तिथि:

title: Government Develops Industrial Townships Under NICDP Through Centre-State Partnership Model
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Commerce & Industry Government Develops Industrial Townships Under NICDP Through Centre-State Partnership Model Government Approves 20 Industrial Nodes Under NICDP; ₹16,172.95 Crore Sanctioned for Industrial Corridor Development Four Industrial Corridor Projects Completed with World-Class Infrastructure; Government Fast-Tracks Remaining Nodes प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                04 AUG 2026 3:20PM by PIB Delhi Government of India has undertaken development of industrial townships under the National Industrial Corridor Development Programme (NICDP), through Special Purpose Vehicles formed jointly with the State Government. The project development activities include identification of industrial nodes as per the prioritisation of the State government, followed by preparation and approval of concept master plan and development plan, environmental clearance and detailed design plan by the State government, prior to consideration of the project for approval. The State Government contribution is in the form of land and Govt of India’s contribution is in the form of equity and/or debt. Government of India has approved a total of 20 industrial nodes under NICDP. Out of these, 12 projects were approved during the last 5 years. The State wise details of these projects is at Annexure I. Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT) has sanctioned and released funds amounting to Rs.16,172.95 Crore to National Industrial Corridor Development and Implementation Trust (NICDIT) for development of Industrial Corridor Projects. NICDIT has further released funds to the extent of Rs.14,569.97 Crore to the project SPVs to carry out project development for various industrial nodes/projects under NICDP. Details regarding the funds released to the project SPVs by NICDIT for the approved projects, State and project-wise is at Annexure II. Out of the 20 projects approved under NICDP, four projects have been completed. The current status of ongoing projects (16 no.) under NICDP is at Annexure III. The total construction timeline for project completion is 36-48 months from the actual date of appointment of EPC contractor. The internal trunk infrastructure, including roads, water supply, sewerage and power distribution within the industrial city/node, are executed through EPC contractors engaged by the respective project SPVs. External connectivity infrastructure such as bulk water supply, power, telecom and roads—have been comprehensively mapped and examined on the PM Gati Shakti National Master Plan (NMP) portal and undertaken by concerned state SPVs as per SHA/SSA conditions in consultation with State department/Central agencies. The following components have been developed in the 04 completed projects: S. No. State Node Infrastructure components developed i. All necessary regulatory as well as statutory clearances are obtained on time through coordination with stakeholders and line agencies to reduce risk. Regular monitoring at various levels is carried out and necessary policy interventions are made wherever required. The PRAGATI and PMG portals are leveraged to fast-track project implementation and ensure timely completion to remove bottlenecks wherever required. Government of India has approved a total of 20 industrial nodes under NICDP. Out of these, 12 projects were approved during the last 5 years. The State wise details of these projects is at Annexure I. Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT) has sanctioned and released funds amounting to Rs.16,172.95 Crore to National Industrial Corridor Development and Implementation Trust (NICDIT) for development of Industrial Corridor Projects. NICDIT has further released funds to the extent of Rs.14,569.97 Crore to the project SPVs to carry out project development for various industrial nodes/projects under NICDP. Details regarding the funds released to the project SPVs by NICDIT for the approved projects, State and project-wise is at Annexure II. Out of the 20 projects approved under NICDP, four projects have been completed. The current status of ongoing projects (16 no.) under NICDP is at Annexure III. The total construction timeline for project completion is 36-48 months from the actual date of appointment of EPC contractor. The internal trunk infrastructure, including roads, water supply, sewerage and power distribution within the industrial city/node, are executed through EPC contractors engaged by the respective project SPVs. External connectivity infrastructure such as bulk water supply, power, telecom and roads—have been comprehensively mapped and examined on the PM Gati Shakti National Master Plan (NMP) portal and undertaken by concerned state SPVs as per SHA/SSA conditions in consultation with State department/Central agencies. Maharashtra Shendra-Bidkin Industrial Area (SBIA) iii Uttar Pradesh Integrated Industrial Township – Greater Noida (IIT-GN) iv Madhya Pradesh Integrated Industrial Township – Vikram Udyogpuri (IIT-VUL) The following steps are taken to expedite implementation and ensure timely completion of projects: An Apex Monitoring Authority periodically reviews the activities of NICDIT and the progress of the Industrial Corridor projects DPIIT through NICDIT periodically monitors the development of these projects with the officials of State Govt(s)/respective agencies/stakeholders. All necessary regulatory as well as statutory clearances are obtained on time through coordination with stakeholders and line agencies to reduce risk. Regular monitoring at various levels is carried out and necessary policy interventions are made wherever required. The PRAGATI and PMG portals are leveraged to fast-track project implementation and ensure timely completion to remove bottlenecks wherever required. title: Union Minister Scindia, MP CM Mohan Yadav Secure Cumulative ₹5,500 Crore Investment Commitments for India’s first Telecom Manufacturing Zone
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Communications Union Minister Scindia, MP CM Mohan Yadav Secure Cumulative ₹5,500 Crore Investment Commitments for India’s first Telecom Manufacturing Zone Mumbai Investors’ Meet Attracts Fresh ₹2,000 Crore Commitments; Telecom Manufacturing Zone Set to Generate over 18,000  Employment Opportunities India Advancing Towards a Global Standard, Best-in-Class Manufacturing Ecosystem Led By PM Modi: Scindia प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                04 AUG 2026 8:20PM by PIB Mumbai Mumbai : 4 August 2026 Union Minister for Communications and Development of North Eastern Region Jyotiraditya M. Scindia, along with Madhya Pradesh Chief Minister Dr. Mohan Yadav, today co-chaired the second Investors’ Meet in Mumbai for India’s first and only Telecom Manufacturing Zone (TMZ) in Gwalior, securing fresh investment commitments worth ₹2,000 crore for the initiative. The meeting witnessed participation from nearly 18 leading industry players from across the telecom ecosystem, with the latest commitments expected to generate close to 4,000 employment opportunities. With the Mumbai commitments, the Telecom Manufacturing Zone has now attracted cumulative investment commitments worth ₹5,500 crore and is expected to create over 18,000 employment opportunities. This builds upon the ₹3,500 crore investment commitments and 14,000 jobs announced during the inaugural Investors’ Roundtable in New Delhi held last week, marking another significant milestone towards the TMZ’s vision of attracting over ₹10,000 crore in investments. Addressing industry leaders, Minister Scindia said that under the leadership of Prime Minister Narendra Modi, India has witnessed a transformational revolution in telecommunications and digitalisation over the last twelve years. He noted that India has evolved from a nation driven by telecom services into one preparing to become a global leader in telecom products and manufacturing. Emphasising the vision of “Make in India, Make for the World” and “Local for Global”, the Minister said India must now transition from being a services-led nation to a product-led nation. He outlined a three-pronged strategy to achieve this transformation: increasing domestic value addition, creating intellectual property in India, and enabling Indian-designed and Indian-manufactured telecom products to reach every corner of the world. Drawing parallels with India’s remarkable success in mobile manufacturing and digital public infrastructure, Minister Scindia said that the same model can now be replicated in telecom manufacturing. He noted that India has transformed from importing the vast majority of its mobile phones to becoming one of the world’s largest mobile manufacturing hubs, while digital platforms such as UPI have demonstrated India’s ability to create globally scalable technology solutions. He expressed confidence that the TMZ in Gwalior would emerge as another global success story that countries around the world could look to replicate. The Minister described the Telecom Manufacturing Zone as a first-of-its-kind initiative inspired by the success of Special Economic Zones but designed exclusively for the telecommunications sector. The integrated ecosystem will bring together the complete telecom value chain, including design, research and development, testing, manufacturing, components, semiconductors, optical fibre, telecom equipment and allied industries, supported by common plug-and-play testing infrastructure and world-class facilities. Highlighting Gwalior’s strategic advantages, Minister Scindia said its central location, excellent connectivity, established industrial ecosystem, availability of plug-and-play infrastructure, strong talent pipeline from premier educational institutions, and competitive operating costs make it an ideal destination for telecom manufacturing investments. Highlighting Gwalior’s rapidly evolving infrastructure, Minister Scindia noted that enhanced connectivity is significantly strengthening the city’s investment proposition. He said that with the upcoming high-speed Agra-Gwalior Greenfield Expressway and improved highway connectivity to the NCR, travel between Delhi-NCR and Gwalior will be completed in less than 3 hours. He invited companies across every telecom vertical to establish operations in the Zone, creating a complete end-to-end manufacturing ecosystem. The Minister also praised Chief Minister Dr. Mohan Yadav and the Government of Madhya Pradesh for their proactive partnership in making the Telecom Manufacturing Zone a reality. He highlighted the State’s industry-friendly incentives, including land availability, capital support, employment-linked incentives, skill development assistance and logistics advantages, which together make the project globally competitive. Reaffirming the Government’s long-term commitment, Minister Scindia announced that a Special Purpose Vehicle (SPV) comprising representatives from both the Department of Telecommunications and the Government of Madhya Pradesh will jointly steer the implementation of the project. Calling it an unprecedented Centre-State partnership, he assured investors that both governments would work together continuously to resolve issues, facilitate investments and ensure the long-term success of the Telecom Manufacturing Zone. The Investors’ Meet was attended by Secretary, Department of Telecommunications Amit Agarwal, Additional Chief Secretary, Government of Madhya Pradesh Neeraj Mandloi, senior government officials, industry leaders and investors from across the telecommunications ecosystem. title: TRAI Assesses Mobile Network Quality Across Srinagar City, Gulmarg City, Anantnag City, Pahalgam City, Srinagar to Pahalgam Highway and Srinagar to Gulmarg Highway Route under J&K LSA
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Communications TRAI Assesses Mobile Network Quality Across Srinagar City, Gulmarg City, Anantnag City, Pahalgam City, Srinagar to Pahalgam Highway and Srinagar to Gulmarg Highway Route under J&K LSA प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                04 AUG 2026 5:21PM by PIB Delhi The Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (TRAI) has released findings of Independent Drive Test (IDT) conducted across Srinagar City, Gulmarg City, Anantnag City, Pahalgam City, Srinagar to Pahalgam Highway and Srinagar to Gulmarg Highway Route under J&K LSA, during the month of June 2026, for information of general telecom consumers. The purpose of this drive test is to assess and verify real time quality of mobile network services (both voice & data) provided by Telecom Service Providers (TSPs). During the IDT, TRAI captures performance of TSPs for key Quality of Service (QoS) parameters like Coverage, Call Drop Rate (CDR), Call Setup Success Rate (CSSR), data Download (DL) and Upload (UL) throughput etc., which are then published to inform Consumers and encourage TSPs to improve their services. These IDTs have been designed to capture on ground mobile network performance of all TSPs across diverse usages environment like cities, hotspots, public transport hubs, etc. In this type of drive testing, live data and voice sessions are established using SIM cards from all TSPs over 2G, 3G, 4G and 5G networks. Multiple advanced test handsets are used, and the sessions are monitored and analyzed in real-time using advanced Software Systems. TRAI, through its appointed agency, conducted drive tests across City drive – 373.6 Km, Highway Drive-111.5 Km, Hotspot locations - 06, Walk Test – 4.9 Km and Inter Operator Calling at 01 location during 08 th June 2026 to 12 th June 2026 in J&K LSA . These tests were conducted under the supervision of the TRAI Regional Office Delhi. The observations presented in drive test reports represent the performance of the TSPs on the area / route under test on the day / time of conducting the drive test. Drive Test Route Map : The following map provides overview of drive test routes indicating Railway Drive, Highway Drive, City drive, Hotspots, Walk tests & Inter-operator calling, as per the legends shown on the map: - Figure-1: Drive test routes Key Parameters Assessed Coverage Gap: Percentage of samples, for which signal strength observed less than the minimum prescribed signal strength for respective technology (2G/ 3G/ 4G/ 5G). Voice Services: Call Setup Success Rate (CSSR), Drop Call Rate (DCR), Call Setup Time, Call Silence Rate, Speech Quality (MOS). Call Silence Instance : Number of call silence instances occurred during the calls. Data Services: Download / Upload Throughput, Latency, Jitter, Packet Drop Rate. The overall mobile network performance in Srinagar and Gulmarg City route for the key parameters has been summarized below: - Coverage Gap - The signal strength observed during voice testing on the drive test route in auto-selection mode (5G/4G/3G/2G), measured as the number of samples having poor signal strength out of the total samples collected, was 194/40350 for Airtel, 1380/40020 for BSNL, 167/37548 for RJIL and 4500/39609 for VIL. Details of the coverage gaps have been provided in the map of Annexure -I . Dropped Calls - Dropped calls in auto-selection mode (5G/ 4G/ 3G/ 2G), measured as the number of dropped calls out of the number of successfully established calls, were 0/360 for Airtel, 07/340 for BSNL, 0/361 for RJIL and 3/360 for VIL. Details of the dropped call locations have been provided in the map of Annexure -I . Call Silence Instance - Call silence instances in Auto-selection mode (5G/4G), measured as the total number of silence instances observed for > 3 seconds out of the total calls established, were 0/350 for Airtel, 39/332 for BSNL, 2/348 for RJIL and 9/344 for VIL. Details of the call silence instance locations have been provided in the map of Annexure -I . Data Download and Upload Throughput: Data Download performance (Overall): Average download speed was observed as 188.64 Mbps for Airtel (5G), 10.77 Mbps for BSNL (4G), 276.92 Mbps for RJIL (5G) and 24.14 Mbps for VIL (4G). Detail of Download throughput has been provided in the map of Annexure -I . Data Upload performance (Overall): Average upload speed was observed as 33.69 Mbps for Airtel (5G), 6.34 Mbps for BSNL (4G), 35.90 Mbps for RJIL (5G) and 10.79 Mbps for VIL (4G). Details of Upload throughput have been provided in the map of Annexure -I . Locations of Dropped Calls and Call Silence instances can be seen by clicking red dot on the map of Annexure -I . The overall mobile network performance in Anantnag and Pahalgam City route for the key parameters has been summarized below: - Coverage Gap - The signal strength observed during voice testing on the drive test route in auto-selection mode (5G/4G/3G/2G), measured as the number of samples having poor signal strength out of the total samples collected, was 226/17997 for Airtel, 3242/16735 for BSNL, 365/17914 for RJIL and 6947/15634 for VIL. Details of the coverage gaps have been provided in the map of Annexure -II . Dropped Calls - Dropped calls in auto-selection mode (5G/ 4G/ 3G/ 2G), measured as the number of dropped calls out of the number of successfully established calls, were 0/161 for Airtel, 4/142 for BSNL, 0/161 for RJIL and 5/145 for VIL. Details of the dropped call locations have been provided in the map of Annexure -II . Call Silence Instance - Call silence instances in Auto-selection mode (5G/4G), measured as the total number of silence instances observed for > 3 seconds out of the total calls established, were 01/156 for Airtel, 17/133 for BSNL, 2/155 for RJIL and 10/111 for VIL. Details of the call silence instance locations have been provided in the map of Annexure -II . Data Download and Upload Throughput: Data Download performance (Overall): Average download speed was observed as 183.84 Mbps for Airtel (5G), 6.86 Mbps for BSNL (4G), 163.53 Mbps for RJIL (5G) and 12.92 Mbps for VIL (4G). Details of Upload throughput have been provided in the map of Annexure -IV . Locations of Dropped Calls and Call Silence instances can be seen by clicking red dot on the map of Annexure -IV . Details of drive test route and area covered during the IDT are as below: - a) City - The areas covered in the city drive are Srinagar, Rajbagh, Nowgam, Chanpora, Hyderpora, Ranbirgarh, Shadi Pora, Dab Sadat, Seh Pora, Ganderbal, Rangil, New Theed, Dani Hama, Rainawari, Soura, Hardu Aboora , Gulmarg, Anantnag, Hakura Badas Gam, Qazigund, Qaimoh, Bijbehara, Mattan, Seer Hamdan, Srigufwara, Sallar Pahalgam and nearby areas. b) Highway - The area covered in the Highway route are Srinagar to Pahalgam Highway passing through Pampore, Lethipora, Barsoo, Awantipora, Chersoo Awantipora,Bijbehara, Mattan,Seer Hamdan, Aishmuqam, Yanier and Srinagar to Gulmarg Highway passing through Narbal, Kawoosa Khalisa, Magam, Kunzer, Cahandilora, Tungmarg and Gulmarg etc. c) Hotspot - The hotspot locations, capturing stationary user experience are Accounts General Office, Betaab Valley Viewpoint, Hari Singh High St., SMHS Hospital, Srinagar Railway Station and University of Kashmir Srinagar. d) Walk Test - The walk test conducted on 12 th June 2026, covered Lal Chowk to Ghanta Ghar capturing mobile network behaviors in crowded pedestrian environments . The findings of this IDT report have been shared with respective TSPs for taking further necessary action at their end. Detailed reports of IDT are made available on the TRAI website at www.trai.gov.in . title: Quarterly Highlights of Action Against Unsolicited Commercial Communications (UCC) For the period 1st April, 2026 to 30th June, 2026 (Q1 of FY 2026-27)
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Communications Quarterly Highlights of Action Against Unsolicited Commercial Communications (UCC)  For the period 1st April, 2026 to 30th June, 2026 (Q1 of FY 2026-27) प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                04 AUG 2026 3:21PM by PIB Delhi Particulars Key Statistics (rounded off) Total Subscriber Base in the country as on 30 th June, 2026 1.348 billion Total Calls Originated in the Telecom Network during Apr’26 to Jun’26 730.82 billion Total SMS Originated in the Telecom Network during Apr’26 to Jun’26 691.09 billion Total UCC Complaints Registered during Apr’26 to Jun’26 1.085 million Total Actionable Complaints during Apr’26 to Jun’26 0.553 million Enforcement Actions Against Actionable Complaints during Q1 of FY 2026-27 Telecom Resources Barred for 15 Days for 1st violation of regulations 1,37,053 Telecom Resources Disconnected for 1 Year for repeated violation of regulations 46,786 Total No. of Senders* Blacklisted for 1 Year 263 Total SMS Headers Blocked 2,873 * A Sender is a Principal Entity or Telemarketer who owns one or more telephone numbers or the SMS headers used for communication. Key Insights: ❖ Overall , action was taken against 183 thousand telecom resources along with blacklisting of 263 senders in Q1 / FY 2026-27. ❖ Enforcement targeted multiple layers – outgoing barring, long-term disconnection, sender blacklisting across all operators and SMS header blocking – to curb repeat violations. ❖ Against 730.82 billion total calls originated in the telecom network in the country in Q1 of FY 2026-27, total UCC complaints stood at 1.085 million i.e. approximately 1.5 complaints per million calls . TRAI DND App Consumer participation through the TRAI DND App continued to play a critical role in strengthening enforcement against spam communications. The App is a tool for consumers to register and modify their preferences for blocking or receiving promotional communications with ease. Item Key Statistics (rounded off) Total App Downloads as on 30.06.26 3.316 million Total UCC Complaints Received during Apr’26 to Jun’26 through all means. 1.085 million Total Complaints Received via TRAI DND App during Apr’26 to Jun’26 0.966 million % of Complaints Received through TRAI DND App 89% Key Insights: ❖ The TRAI DND App accounts for 89% of all UCC complaints received by the Access Providers. DND Preference Registrations Consumers can use the TRAI DND App, their telecom service provider’s App/ Website, or call/ send SMS to 1909 to register and modify their Do Not Disturb (DND) preferences for blocking or receiving promotional communications from the senders from any or all the sectors. Parameter Key Statistics (rounded off)) Total Preferences Registered at DND Registry as on 30.06.2026. 224 million Total Subscriber Base in the country as on 30.06.2026 1.348 billion Pecentage of Registered Preferences. 16% Key Insights: ❖ More than 1.12 billion subscribers have not registered any preference, and, hence, are accessible for all commercial communications from registered telemarketers and senders. The consumers desirous of controlling commercial communications can register their preferences on DND registry. TRAI Designated Series: 140xx and 1600xx TRAI introduced the designated 140 series for promotional calls to ensure that such calls originate from a dedicated numbering series, enabling consumers to easily identify and manage such calls. The calls originating from 140 series numbers are pre-verified against the preferences of the customers before delivery. The designated series enables the consumer to exercise the choice of accepting or declining the call. The 1600 series was introduced for service and transactional calls by the entities in Banking, Financial services & Insurance sector, and for Government to citizen communication. This designated series  provides trusted calling numbers for such important communications. Together, these dedicated numbering series improve transparency, consumer trust, and the effectiveness of regulatory enforcement against spam and fraudulent communications. Item Key Statistics (rounded off) (During Q1, FY 2026-27) Total Promotional calls originated using 140 Series numbers. 13.16 billion 140 Series calls blocked after verification with registered DND preferences of the customers. 1.48 billion Commercial SMS originated by the Registered Senders/ Telemarketers. 248.06 billion Promotional SMS Blocked after verification with registered DND preferences of the customers. 7.30 billion Total Calls originated from 1600 Series numbers. 1.15 billion Key Insights: ❖ Registered DND preferences enabled blocking of about 1.48 billion promotional calls and 7.30 billion promotional SMSs, demonstrating effective consumer preference enforcement. ❖ 13.16 billion promotional calls and 248.06 billion commercial SMS were routed through registered communication channels. AI-Based Suspected Spam Flagging on Incoming Calls In order to alert the consumers from suspected spam calls and SMS from entities using normal 10-digit numbers that bypass the regulated system, AI-based systems have been deployed by the Telecom Service providers (TSPs) to flag such suspected spam on the basis of calling pattern analysis. Further, the telecom service providers have started sending warning notifications to entities suspected with high probability of sending such spam. An entity could be using multiple numbers for sending spam. These notifications warn the suspected senders of regulatory action so as to refrain from sending further spam. Item Key Statistics (rounded off) (During Q1, FY 2026-27) Total Incoming Calls 721.79 billion Total Incoming Calls Flagged by AI based Systems as Suspected Spam 22.99 billion Total Incoming SMS 836.31 billion Total Incoming SMS Flagged by AI based Systems as Suspected Spam 1.44 billion Warning Notifications issued to suspected high probability spam sending entities * 243 thousand * Warning Notifications have been sent starting from 23 rd June, 2026. Key Insights: ❖ AI-based spam detection flagged 24.43 billion suspected spam calls/SMSs, enabling consumers to exercise choice of either ignoring such communication or picking such communications with caution. ❖ Over 243 thousand warning notifications were issued to the suspected senders within one week of commencement of the sending warning notifications. ***** NJ/AR (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2294234) आगंतुक पटल  : 183 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: हिन्दी , Gujarati Ministry of Communications Quarterly Highlights of Action Against Unsolicited Commercial Communications (UCC)  For the period 1st April, 2026 to 30th June, 2026 (Q1 of FY 2026-27) प्रविष्टि तिथि:

title: Cooperative based Organic Farming
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Cooperation Cooperative based Organic Farming प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                04 AUG 2026 5:15PM by PIB Delhi Organic farming is promoted through Paramparagat Krishi Vikas Yojana (PKVY) in the States/UTs including Assam and Mission Organic Value Chain Development for North Eastern Region (MOVCDNER) for the North Eastern States including Assam since 2015-16 by the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare, Government of India. Both schemes stress on end-to-end support to farmers engaged in organic farming i.e. from production to processing, certification and marketing. Primary focus of the schemes is to form organic clusters, with preference to small and marginal farmers, to create a supply chain. Both the schemes are implemented through States /UT Governments. Under PKVY, assistance of Rs. 31,500 per hectare is provided over 3 years for promotion of organic farming. Out of this, assistance of Rs. 15,000 per ha is provided to farmers through Direct Benefit Transfer for on- farm /off –farm organic inputs. Under MOVCDNER, assistance of Rs. 46,500/ha is provided over 3 years for creation of Farmers Producer Organization, support to farmers for organic inputs etc. Out of this, assistance @ Rs. 32,500/ ha is provided to farmers for off -farm /on –farm organic inputs under the scheme including Rs. 15,000 as Direct Benefit Transfer to the farmers. This information was given by Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation, Shri Amit Shah in a written reply in Lok Sabha. ***** AK/AP (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2294368) आगंतुक पटल  : 153 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: Urdu , हिन्दी Ministry of Cooperation Cooperative based Organic Farming प्रविष्टि तिथि:

title: Bhartiya Beej Sahakari Samiti Limited
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Cooperation Bhartiya Beej Sahakari Samiti Limited प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                04 AUG 2026 5:14PM by PIB Delhi Bhartiya Beej Sahakari Samiti Limited (BBSSL) has so far introduced seeds of 18 crops and 124 varieties in the market under the ‘Bharat Beej’ brand for distribution across the country. BBSSL distributes its seeds through its nationwide network of member cooperative societies, private distributors and dealers, as well as through State Seed Federations and Seed Corporations under various government schemes. For the effective implementation of its seed distribution programme, BBSSL has designated region-wise Zonal Managers and Coordinators, including officials responsible for Maharashtra and Dadra and Nagar Haveli, at its Head Office. In Maharashtra, seeds of fodder crops, cotton, sorghum and groundnut have been supplied by BBSSL through the State Government under Centrally Sponsored Schemes, namely NMEO-OS, NFSNM and the Kapas Kranti Mission, while wheat and gram seeds have been distributed through private distribution channels. In Dadra and Nagar Haveli, the Department of Agriculture has been designated as BBSSL’s Nodal Agency for coordinating seed distribution and related activities. The BBSSL has been set up to act as an apex organization for production, procurement, processing, branding, labelling, packaging, storage, marketing and distribution of quality seeds; strategic research & development; and to develop a system for preservation and promotion of indigenous natural seeds. title: Financial Health of Cooperative Societies
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Cooperation Financial Health of Cooperative Societies प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                04 AUG 2026 5:10PM by PIB Delhi As per the National Cooperative Database (NCD), as on 15.07.2026, there are 41,501 cooperative societies in Mumbai, including housing, consumer, credit and labour cooperatives. Of these, 40,853 are functional. Among the functional cooperative societies, 19,911 are profit-making and 14,877 are loss-making, while financial information is not available for 6,065 societies. The Government approved the Centrally Sponsored Project for Computerisation of functional Primary Agricultural Credit Societies (PACS), including those in Maharashtra, in 2022. The objective of the project is to bring all functional PACS on a common ERP (Enterprise Resource Planning)-based National Software. Initially, 63,000 PACS were approved under the Project for Computerization of PACS with a financial outlay of ₹2,516 crore. The project has since been expanded to cover 79,630 PACS with a revised outlay of ₹2,925.39 crore. Additionally, the National Cooperative Development Corporation (NCDC) provides financial assistance for infrastructure development, business diversification, value chain development, and capacity building of cooperative institutions across the country, including Maharashtra. As on 30.06.2026, NCDC has cumulatively disbursed ₹5,74,090.48 crore, including ₹3,96,763 crore during the last five years, for the development of cooperative institutions. The Ministry of Cooperation, since its inception on 06.07.2021, has undertaken several initiatives to realize the vision of “Sahakar-se-Samriddhi” and to strengthen cooperative sector across the country including Mumbai. Key areas of initiatives include: Computerization of PACS: The Government has approved the Centrally Sponsored Project for Computerization of 79,630 PACS with a financial outlay of ₹2,925.39 crore, along with provision of IT infrastructure and implementation guidelines (Margdarshika), to promote digitalization, transparency and efficient service delivery. Model Bye-laws for PACS: Enabled PACS to undertake more than 25 business activities, improve governance, transparency and accountability in their operations. Now, PACS can operate as PM-Kisan Samridhi Kendras (PMKSKs), Pradhan Mantri Bhartiya Janaushadhi Kendras (PMBJKs), Common Service Centres (CSC) etc. Capacity Building and Training : Training programmes and workshops are organized for PACS officials to strengthen governance, financial management and operational capacity. Strengthening of the Three-Tier Cooperative Credit Structure: Measures have been taken to strengthen coordination among PACS, District Central Cooperative Banks (DCCBs) and State Cooperative Banks (StCBs) to improve liquidity management and credit flow. World's Largest Decentralized Grain Storage Plan : The Government is implementing the World's Largest Decentralized Grain Storage Plan in the Cooperative Sector to enhance storage capacity at the grassroots level. National Cooperative Database (NCD): The NCD has been developed to identify gaps in cooperative coverage, facilitate formation of new cooperative societies, support evidence-based policymaking, and enable performance assessment of cooperative societies through the Cooperative Ranking Framework. Tribhuvan Sahkari University : The Government has established Tribhuvan Sahkari University to strengthen cooperative education, training, research and capacity building. This information was given by Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation, Shri Amit Shah in a written reply in Lok Sabha. ***** AK/AP (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2294362) आगंतुक पटल  : 91 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: Urdu , हिन्दी Ministry of Cooperation Financial Health of Cooperative Societies प्रविष्टि तिथि:

title: Bharat Taxi
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Cooperation Bharat Taxi प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                04 AUG 2026 5:07PM by PIB Delhi Bharat Taxi, country’s first cooperative-led ride-hailing platform, operated by Sahakar Taxi Cooperative Limited (STCL) has been launched. The objective of Bharat Taxi is not to replace any private app-based taxi aggregators, rather, it aims to provide an alternative driver-centric and people-centric mobility platform based on the cooperative model wherein drivers are associated as members and stakeholders to promote their economic and social well-being, while providing consumers with safe, reliable and affordable transportation services. The principal objectives of Bharat Taxi are to provide reliable, affordable and transparent mobility services, promote employment and self-employment opportunities for Sarathis(drivers), strengthen their economic welfare and develop a technology-driven mobility ecosystem based on cooperative principles. Bharat Taxi is operated by Sahakar Taxi Cooperative Limited (STCL), a Multi-State Cooperative Society registered under the Multi-State Cooperative Societies Act, 2002. The registered Head Office of the Society is located in New Delhi. The governance and management structure of the Society comprises the Chairman, Vice-Chairman, Chief Executive Officer (CEO), Chief Operating Officer (COO), Departmental Heads, Regional Offices and city-level operational teams, which collectively oversee policy implementation, operational management and service delivery across the platform. The Society is governed in accordance with the provisions of the Multi-State Cooperative Societies Act, 2002 and its registered bye-laws. The platform is supported by eight leading national cooperative institutions, namely NCDC, IFFCO, AMUL (GCMMF), KRIBHCO, NAFED, NABARD, NDDB and NCEL. These institutions support the implementation of the cooperative model through institutional cooperation, outreach and member mobilisation. As on 28.07.2026, a total of 8.27 lakh Sarathis (drivers) have been registered on the platform. The details of enabled drivers are as under: State Cab Auto Bike Total Sarathis Delhi- NCR 1,35,554 37,850 87,641 2,61,045 Gujarat 32,192 49,764 22,207 1,04,163 Uttar Pradesh 7,687 6,181 7,753 21,621 Chandigarh 7,810 982 1,903 10,695 Maharashtra 53,139 23,329 7,864 84,332 Rajasthan 7,749 5,265 7,585 20,599 No financial assistance, equity support or incentive has been provided by the Government for establishing or expanding the Bharat Taxi platform. The platform is being operated by Sahakar Taxi Cooperative Limited (STCL) under the cooperative framework. The rollout of services of Bharat Taxi in other cities and States is taken by Sahakar Taxi Cooperative Limited (STCL) subject to operational requirements and necessary approvals. Expansion is undertaken based on factors such as operational preparedness, availability of Sarathis, completion of statutory requirements, and coordination with the concerned State Governments, cooperative institutions, and other stakeholders. The expansion strategy includes partnerships with airports, railway stations, metro systems and other public transport facilities, wherever feasible, to facilitate seamless last-mile connectivity through appropriate arrangements with the concerned authorities. Passenger safety is supported through verification of Sarathis and vehicles prior to onboarding, maintenance of trip records and coordination with the concerned authorities, wherever required. The platform provides safety features such as an SOS facility and enables passengers to share journey details with family members or other trusted contacts. Institutional arrangements are also established with Police Departments in various States to strengthen passenger safety and facilitate coordination during emergencies. Customer data is stored in encrypted form in accordance with the provisions of the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 and the Information Technology Act, 2000. Fare determination is based on a transparent framework developed after considering the views of the concerned State Transport Authorities, representatives of Sarathis and other stakeholders. Any revision in fares is undertaken after taking into account operational costs, local transport conditions and stakeholder consultations, thereby ensuring appropriate representation of Sarathis in the fare determination process. A structured grievance redressal mechanism has been established through the Call Centre, Customer Support Team and Grievance Redressal Team for receiving and resolving grievances of both passengers and Sarathis in accordance with the prescribed procedures. This information was given by Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation, Shri Amit Shah in a written reply in Lok Sabha. ***** AK/AP (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2294356) आगंतुक पटल  : 201 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: Urdu , हिन्दी , Telugu Ministry of Cooperation Bharat Taxi प्रविष्टि तिथि:

title: Cooperative Godowns
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Cooperation Cooperative Godowns प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                04 AUG 2026 5:02PM by PIB Delhi Since the implementation of decentralized grain storage plan in Cooperative Sector from 31.05.2023, no such report has been received from the State of Uttar Pradesh. In order to ensure proper utilization of the godowns the employees of the PACS/Cooperative Societies have been imparted training in modern warehouse management organized by NABARD and WDRA in the state of Uttar Pradesh. However, no specific training request on modern warehouse management has been received so far from Jaunpur. The state can raise request for conduct of such training for their PACS/Cooperative Societies to NABARD and WDRA. In this regard, no such information/complaint has been received from the state of Uttar Pradesh. Decentralized storage plan in cooperative sector entails creation of various agri infrastructure including godowns, custom hiring centers, processing units, Fair Price Shops, cold storage etc., at Primary Agricultural Credit Societies (PACS)/other cooperative societies level through convergence of various existing schemes of the Government of India (GoI), such as, Agriculture Infrastructure Fund (AIF), Agricultural Marketing Infrastructure Scheme (AMI), Sub Mission on Agricultural Mechanization (SMAM), Pradhan Mantri Formalization of Micro Food Processing Enterprises Scheme (PMFME). Unnao, Sonbhadra in Purvanchal and Jaunpur, Mahoba, Hamirpur, Banda, Jalaun, and Jhansi in Bundelkhand region are listed under Pradhan Mantri Dhan-Dhaanya Krishi Yojana (PMDDKY). The decentralised grain storage plan in Cooperative Sector is one of the components of Pradhan Mantri Dhan-Dhaanya Krishi Yojana (PMDDKY), complements promoting integrated agricultural infrastructure and value addition in rural areas. Under the plan the creation of storage infrastructure at PACS/other cooperative societies, coupled with primary processing and allied facilities, is expected to generate substantial employment opportunities. Jaunpur district can also participate and avail the benefit under the decentralized grain storage plan in cooperative sector with the approval of District Cooperative Development Committee (DCDC). Under the plan the detailed project report is sanctioned by the respective DCCB after scrutinizing all the requisite document and for availing the advance subsidy claim the DPR is verified by NABARD through their dedicated portal. After completion of the project, physical verification is conducted by respective bank and NABARD. This information was given by Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation, Shri Amit Shah in a written reply in Lok Sabha. ****** AK/AP (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2294350) आगंतुक पटल  : 73 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: Urdu , हिन्दी Ministry of Cooperation Cooperative Godowns प्रविष्टि तिथि:

title: Department of Consumer Affairs Invites Applications for Government Approved Test Centres (GATCs) from 17–31 August 2026
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food & Public Distribution Department of Consumer Affairs Invites Applications for Government Approved Test Centres (GATCs) from 17–31 August 2026 51 GATC recognised so far. More Verification Capacity • Faster Services • Better Consumer Protection The initiative envisions to enhance the country's verification capacity, improve accessibility of verification services and facilitate faster compliance for industry while ensuring accurate measurements for consumers. प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                04 AUG 2026 2:18PM by PIB Delhi The Department of Consumer Affairs, Food & Public Distribution, has invited online applications from eligible industries, laboratories, engineering colleges, polytechnics, ITIs and testing facilities for recognition as Government Approved Test Centres (GATCs) under the Legal Metrology (Government Approved Test Centre) Rules, 2013 . Applications can be submitted online through the Department's official portal emaap.gov.in/gatc from 17 August 2026 to 31 August 2026 . The portal provides a fully digital application process, including online submission, fee payment, application tracking and communication with applicants, making the process transparent, efficient and business-friendly. The initiative is aimed at expanding India's verification ecosystem for weights and measures by increasing the participation of technically competent private institutions. A larger network of GATCs will strengthen the country's verification capacity, improve access to verification services and enable faster compliance for industries, while ensuring accurate measurements for consumers. Government Approved Test Centres are authorised to carry out the verification and re-verification of specified weighing and measuring instruments used in trade and commerce. Expanding the network of these centres will help make verification services more accessible, reduce turnaround time and improve the delivery of Legal Metrology services across the country. Following recent amendments to the Legal Metrology (Government Approved Test Centre) Rules, 2013, recognised GATCs are now authorised to verify 23 categories of weighing and measuring instruments used across sectors such as healthcare, energy, transport, retail, manufacturing and infrastructure. The authorised categories include: Water meters Sphygmomanometers (blood pressure monitors) Clinical thermometers Automatic rail weighbridges Tape measures Non-automatic weighing instruments of Accuracy Class III (up to 150 kg) Non-automatic weighing instruments of Accuracy Class IIII Load cells Beam scales Counter machines Weights of all categories Gas meters Energy meters Moisture meters Speed meters for vehicles Breath analysers Multi-dimensional measuring instruments Flow meters Petrol and diesel dispensers CNG dispensers LPG dispensers LNG dispensers Hydrogen dispensers Eligible applicants include industries, manufacturers, laboratories, engineering colleges, polytechnics, ITIs and testing facilities that possess: Prescribed testing and calibration equipment traceable to national standards; Qualified technical personnel with experience in Legal Metrology; and The infrastructure required under the GATC Rules. The expanded network of GATCs will complement the work of State Legal Metrology Departments by increasing verification capacity across the country. This will enable faster verification and re-verification of weighing and measuring instruments, while allowing State Legal Metrology Officers to focus more on market surveillance, enforcement activities and consumer grievance redressal. The initiative reflects the Government's continued commitment to Ease of Doing Business, Digital Governance, Atmanirbhar Bharat and consumer protection by creating a modern, technology-driven and transparent Legal Metrology ecosystem. As India continues to strengthen its position as an OIML Certification Authority , the expanded GATC framework is also expected to enhance the country's quality infrastructure, promote internationally accepted measurement practices and support Indian industry in meeting global standards. Interested organisations may visit emaap.gov.in/gatc for detailed eligibility conditions and to submit their applications. *** RT/ SB / ARC (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2294205) आगंतुक पटल  : 476 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: Kannada , Urdu , हिन्दी , Marathi , Gujarati , Tamil Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food & Public Distribution Department of Consumer Affairs Invites Applications for Government Approved Test Centres (GATCs) from 17–31 August 2026 51 GATC recognised so far. title: Online Registrations for Yuva Sangam Phase VII Commence from 4 August 2026
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Education Online Registrations for Yuva Sangam Phase VII Commence from 4 August 2026 Ministry of Education opens online registrations for Yuva Sangam Phase VII 20 Higher Education Institutions to lead youth exchange programmes under Ek Bharat Shreshtha Bharat प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                04 AUG 2026 7:15PM by PIB Delhi The Ministry of Education today opened the online registration portal for Yuva Sangam Phase VII under the Ek Bharat Shreshtha Bharat (EBSB) initiative. Interested youth aged 18–30 years, including students of Higher Education Institutions, NSS/NYKS volunteers, and young professionals, are eligible to register through the official portal at https://ebsb.aicte-india.org The last date of registration for Yuva Sangam Phase VII is Aug 18, 2026. For Yuva Sangam Phase VII, 20 Higher Education Institutions (HEIs), that is, IITs, IIMs, Central Universities and NITs have been identified as nodal institutions to host and facilitate the exchange programme. Selected participants will undertake five to seven day educational and cultural tours (excluding travel days) to their paired States/UTs, where they will gain firsthand exposure to local traditions, educational institutions, governance initiatives, innovation ecosystems, industries, heritage sites, and community life. Pairing of States/UTs for Yuva Sangam Phase VII: S. No. State Proposed paired HEIs Paired State Proposed paired HEIs 1 Uttar Pradesh BHU Varanasi Keralam IIT Palakkad 2 Madhya Pradesh SPA Bhopal Karnataka CU Karnataka 3 Assam IIT Guwahati Telengana CU Hyderabad 4 Goa NIT Goa Mizoram CU Mizoram 5 Rajasthan IIT Jodhpur Sikkim Sikkim University 6 J&K, Ladakh NIT Srinagar Maharashtra IIT Bombay 7 West Bengal IIT Kharagpur Uttarakhand HBNU, Srinagar 8 Chandigarh IISER Mohali Gujarat CU Gujarat 9 Himachal Pradesh NIT Hamirpur Odisha IIM Sambalpur 10 Delhi Delhi University Tamil Nadu CU Tamil Nadu Yuva Sangam is a flagship Youth Exchange Programme of the Department of Higher Education, Ministry of Education, aimed at strengthening emotional bonds and fostering mutual understanding among young citizens from different States and Union Territories. The initiative promotes the spirit of "Unity in Diversity" by facilitating structured exposure visits between paired States and Union Territories, enabling participants to experience India's rich cultural, linguistic, educational and developmental diversity firsthand. The programme is structured around the five thematic pillars (5 Ps) of Paryatan (Tourism), Parampara (Traditions & Culture), Pragati (Development & Governance), Paraspar Sampark (People-to-People Connect), and Prodyogiki (Technology & Innovation). Through these thematic engagements, participants develop a deeper appreciation of India's cultural diversity while fostering mutual understanding and national unity, in alignment with the vision of the National Education Policy (NEP) 2020. Yuva Sangam is implemented through a collaborative "Whole of Government" approach with active support from participating Ministries, Departments, State Governments and partner Higher Education Institutions. The previous editions of the programme have witnessed overwhelming participation from youth across the country. The Ministry of Education encourages youth from across the country to seize this unique opportunity to experience India's vibrant diversity, interact with peers from different regions, and become ambassadors of the Ek Bharat Shreshtha Bharat vision. ***** RRTN (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2294518) आगंतुक पटल  : 139 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: Marathi Ministry of Education Online Registrations for Yuva Sangam Phase VII Commence from 4 August 2026 Ministry of Education opens online registrations for Yuva Sangam Phase VII 20 Higher Education Institutions to lead youth exchange programmes under Ek Bharat Shreshtha Bharat प्रविष्टि तिथि:

title: Union Education Minister Shri Pralhad Joshi to Participate in the 13th BRICS Education Ministers’ Meeting to be Held in Odisha
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Education Union Education Minister Shri Pralhad Joshi to Participate in the 13th BRICS Education Ministers’ Meeting to be Held in Odisha Meeting to Deliberate on Key Priorities Including ECCE, Skill Development, Research and Innovation, Mutual Recognition of Qualifications and Academic Leadership Posted On:
                04 AUG 2026 6:52PM by PIB Delhi The Ministry of Education, under India’s BRICS chairship 2026, is scheduled to host the 13th BRICS Education Ministers’ Meeting and the 3rd BRICS Senior Officials’ Meeting from August 5–7, 2026 in Bhubaneswar, Odisha. These meetings would bring together education ministers, senior officials and delegates from BRICS member countries to discuss topics of collaboration, including the following priority areas: (a) Strengthening Early Childhood Care and Education (ECCE); (b) Strengthening skill development and enhanced cooperation under the BRICS TVET Cooperation Alliance (TCA); (c) Promoting collaborative research, innovation and start-ups; (d) Strengthening Mutual Recognition of Qualifications (MRQ); and (e) Capacity building for academic leadership. India’s BRICS chairship is guided by the theme “Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability”, reflecting the people-centric and humanity-first approach articulated by the Prime Minister of India, Shri Narendra Modi, at the 2025 BRICS Summit in Rio de Janeiro. The 13th Education Ministers’ Meeting and the 3rd Senior Officials’ Meetings would build upon a series of engagements held under the BRICS Education Track during India’s chairship. The 1st and 2nd BRICS Senior Officials’ Meetings were held earlier on 7th and 28th April 2026, respectively, followed by the BRICS Network University Conference and International Governing Board Meeting on July 20 –21, 2026. The previous engagements have helped shaped discussions and build consensus on the priority areas and proposed outcomes for the Ministerial Meeting. Ahead of the 13th Education Ministers’ Meeting, the BRICS TVET Symposium and the Joint Management Committee (JMC) meeting of the BRICS TVET Cooperation Alliance were also held in New Delhi on August 3–4, 2026, led by the Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship. These engagements seek to deepen cooperation among BRICS countries in technical and vocational education and training, skills development and workforce preparedness and to consolidate and exchange research and best practices across the priority themes. Alongside these high-level inter-governmental engagements, India’s BRICS chairship is placing strong emphasis on youth participation and people-to-people exchanges. In this spirit, Model BRICS has been conceptualised as a student-focused initiative to be organised on the sidelines of BRICS Ministerial Meetings across India. The initiative seeks to familiarise young citizens with BRICS processes while strengthening their understanding of diplomacy, multilateral cooperation and consensus-building. ***** RRTN (Release ID: 2294492) Visitor Counter : 232 Read this release in: Urdu , हिन्दी , Gujarati Ministry of Education Union Education Minister Shri Pralhad Joshi to Participate in the 13th BRICS Education Ministers’ Meeting to be Held in Odisha Meeting to Deliberate on Key Priorities Including ECCE, Skill Development, Research and Innovation, Mutual Recognition of Qualifications and Academic Leadership Posted On:
