title: C-DAC and Geological Survey of India sign Umbrella MoU to Strengthen Geoscience, Mineral Exploration and Disaster Management through Next-Generation Technologies
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Electronics & IT C-DAC and Geological Survey of India sign Umbrella MoU to Strengthen Geoscience, Mineral Exploration and Disaster Management through Next-Generation Technologies Partnership to leverage AI, High-Performance Computing and Advanced Digital Technologies for Earth Science Applications प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                04 AUG 2026 4:55PM by PIB Delhi The Centre for Development of Advanced Computing (C-DAC), Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) and the Geological Survey of India (GSI) signed an Umbrella Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) to strengthen collaboration in geoscience, mineral exploration and disaster management through advanced next-generation technologies. The MoU was signed at Electronics Niketan, New Delhi, in the presence of Shri S. Krishnan, IAS, Secretary, MeitY by Shri E. Magesh, Director General, C-DAC and Shri Pradeep Singh, Additional Director General, Geological Survey of India (GSI). The collaboration aims to combine C-DAC's High-Performance Computing (HPC) capabilities with GSI's geological expertise to address complex sub-surface exploration challenges through advanced digital technologies. The partnership envisages the use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and HPC for processing large geophysical datasets, enabling high-resolution 3D subsurface mapping, predictive modelling for mineral targeting and cognitive processing of decades of unstructured geological records into a domain Large Language Model (LLM). The collaboration will also support disaster mitigation through slope-scale landslide monitoring using Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR), development of early warning systems and studies on Glacier Lake Outburst Floods (GLOF). In addition, it aims to accelerate the discovery of critical minerals and Rare Earth Elements (REE), thereby contributing to India's economic security, supply chain resilience and technological self-reliance. The ceremony was attended by Shri Sudeep Srivastava, Joint Secretary, MeitY; Shri Maneesh Khar, Deputy Director General, DGCO, GSI; Dr. Praveer Pankaj, Director, DGCO, GSI; Dr. Mukesh Verma, Director, DGCO, GSI; Shri Manoj Jain, Group Coordinator (R&D in IT), MeitY; Cmde Sandeep Wadhwa, Executive Director (Corporate & Govt. Business), C-DAC; Dr. Ch. A. S.                         04 AUG 2026 4:55PM by PIB Delhi The Centre for Development of Advanced Computing (C-DAC), Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) and the Geological Survey of India (GSI) signed an Umbrella Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) to strengthen collaboration in geoscience, mineral exploration and disaster management through advanced next-generation technologies. The MoU was signed at Electronics Niketan, New Delhi, in the presence of Shri S. Krishnan, IAS, Secretary, MeitY by Shri E. Magesh, Director General, C-DAC and Shri Pradeep Singh, Additional Director General, Geological Survey of India (GSI). The collaboration aims to combine C-DAC's High-Performance Computing (HPC) capabilities with GSI's geological expertise to address complex sub-surface exploration challenges through advanced digital technologies. The partnership envisages the use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and HPC for processing large geophysical datasets, enabling high-resolution 3D subsurface mapping, predictive modelling for mineral targeting and cognitive processing of decades of unstructured geological records into a domain Large Language Model (LLM). The collaboration will also support disaster mitigation through slope-scale landslide monitoring using Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR), development of early warning systems and studies on Glacier Lake Outburst Floods (GLOF). In addition, it aims to accelerate the discovery of critical minerals and Rare Earth Elements (REE), thereby contributing to India's economic security, supply chain resilience and technological self-reliance. ministry: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
title: CAQM extends Monitoring and Enforcement of Dust Mitigation measures across NCR; More ULBs empowered to Prosecute Gross Violators at C&D Sites
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change CAQM extends Monitoring and Enforcement of Dust Mitigation measures across NCR; More ULBs empowered to Prosecute Gross Violators at C&D Sites प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                04 AUG 2026 7:18PM by PIB Delhi The Commission for Air Quality Management in NCR and Adjoining Areas (CAQM) has issued an amendment dated 03.08.2026 to its Statutory Direction No. 86 to further strengthen enforcement against violations of dust mitigation measures at Construction and Demolition (C&D) sites with plot area less than 500 sqm. across the National Capital Region (NCR). The amendment widens the ambit of enforcement by extending the powers to initiate prosecution against gross violators to additional Municipal Corporations, Development Authorities, Municipal Councils, Municipal Boards and Urban Local Bodies (ULBs) in the NCR. Statutory Direction No. 86, issued on 02.01.2025 and amended on 24.06.2025, had authorised the Commissioner/Zonal Deputy Commissioners of the Municipal Corporation of Delhi (MCD), Secretary, New Delhi Municipal Council (NDMC), and Commissioners/Chief Executives/Deputy Commissioners of various ULBs in Gurugram, Faridabad, NOIDA, Greater NOIDA, Ghaziabad and Sonipat to file a complaint/prosecution before the jurisdictional Judicial Magistrate in cases of gross violations of directions/orders relating to dust and air pollution control and mitigation measures at such sites within their respective jurisdictions. The Direction also empowered these authorities to order closure of such sites and impose or realise Environmental Compensation (EC) in cases of gross violations, including those relating to the GRAP Schedule in respect of C&D activities. Recognising that a significant number of construction projects on plots having an area of less than 500 sqm. are also ongoing in several other Municipal Corporations and bigger cities/towns in the NCR, which contribute significantly to the overall PM10 and PM2.5 load attributed to the C&D sector, the Commission has expanded the enforcement framework to ensure more effective implementation of dust mitigation measures across the region. Accordingly, the powers to initiate prosecution against gross violators of dust mitigation measures at C&D sites have now been extended to additional Municipal Corporations, Development Authorities and Urban Local Bodies across the NCR, including Manesar, Karnal, Panipat, Rohtak, Meerut, Alwar, Bharatpur, Bhiwadi and Neemrana, besides strengthening the existing enforcement mechanism in the NCR. The amended Direction also requires all concerned agencies to submit a monthly status report to the Commission on complaints and prosecutions filed, along with the monthly progress reports already being submitted. This reporting mechanism is expected to strengthen accountability and facilitate closer monitoring of enforcement actions across the NCR. During the last quarter, April–June 2026, 16,195 inspections were undertaken by DPCC/SPCBs at C&D sites in Delhi, 909 sites in Haryana (NCR), 230 sites in Uttar Pradesh (NCR) and 160 sites in the NCR districts of Rajasthan. Considering the large number of C&D activities being undertaken across the NCR, particularly smaller construction projects on plots measuring less than 500 sqm., expanding the enforcement framework to additional Municipal Corporations, Development Authorities, Municipal Councils, Municipal Boards and ULBs assumes considerable significance for ensuring effective implementation of dust mitigation measures and strengthening compliance across the region. The Commission has reiterated that effective enforcement of dust control measures at C&D sites remains a vital component of improving the overall air quality of the region. The expanded enforcement mechanism shall ensure stricter compliance, strengthen deterrence against violations and contribute significantly towards reduction of dust emissions across the NCR. ***** VM/GS (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2294520) आगंतुक पटल  : 59 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: Urdu Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change CAQM extends Monitoring and Enforcement of Dust Mitigation measures across NCR; More ULBs empowered to Prosecute Gross Violators at C&D Sites प्रविष्टि तिथि:

ministry: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
title: On International Clouded Leopard Day, India Strengthens Conservation through Dedicated Conservation Action Plan for the Wild Cat
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change On International Clouded Leopard Day, India Strengthens Conservation through Dedicated Conservation Action Plan for the Wild Cat The Action Plan focuses on Habitat Protection, Scientific Monitoring, Landscape Connectivity and Community Participation across Northeast India प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                04 AUG 2026 12:41PM by PIB Delhi On the occasion of International Clouded Leopard Day, India has reaffirmed its commitment to the conservation of one of Asia’s most elusive wild cats through the newly launched Clouded Leopard Conservation Action Plan (CAP). Prepared under the Government of India–GEF–UNDP initiative, the Action Plan CAP was released during the 91st meeting of the Standing Committee of the National Board of Wild Life (SCNBWL), held in the second week of July 2026, at Coimbatore. The action plan provides a comprehensive framework for securing habitats, restoring forest connectivity, strengthening scientific monitoring and empowering local communities for conservation of the species. The CAP marks an important step towards strengthening long-term conservation of the Clouded Leopard across Northeast India. The approach focuses on landscape-level conservation, scientific assessment, community participation and technology-driven interventions to protect the species and its habitats. A key component of the Action Plan is the identification of 14 priority conservation landscapes across Northeast India, along with landscape-scale habitat restoration and corridor conservation to strengthen connectivity between forest habitats. The Government has also strengthened the institutional framework for Clouded Leopard conservation through the inclusion of the species under the Species Recovery Programme of the Integrated Development of Wildlife Habitats (IDWH) scheme. The CAP provides for standardised scientific monitoring through camera traps, occupancy surveys, genetics and environmental DNA (eDNA), enabling improved understanding of the species and its habitat requirements. It also emphasises strengthening anti-poaching measures and wildlife crime prevention. Capacity building of frontline staff is another important component, including the use of the M-STrIPES smart application to strengthen field-level conservation efforts. Recognising the critical role of local communities in wildlife conservation, the Action Plan promotes community-based conservation and sustainable livelihood support . It also encourages transboundary cooperation with neighbouring range countries for coordinated conservation of the species across its range. The CAP further integrates climate resilience and adaptive management into conservation planning, strengthening the long-term resilience of Clouded Leopard habitats and landscapes. The conservation of the Clouded Leopard is intrinsically linked with the conservation of the forests and natural heritage of Northeast India. Through the Conservation Action Plan, India is advancing a coordinated approach that combines habitat protection, scientific monitoring, landscape restoration, involving technology, community participation and international cooperation to secure the future of this remarkable wild cat. title: Government Boosts MSME Financing Through SIDBI and ECLGS 5.0
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Finance Government Boosts MSME Financing Through SIDBI and ECLGS 5.0 SIDBI Expands Nationwide Presence with 71 New Branches; Direct Credit Portfolio Grows 36.8% Y-oY ECLGS 5.0 Envisages ₹2.55 Lakh Crore Additional Credit With up to 100% Guarantee Coverage for Eligible MSMEs प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                04 AUG 2026 3:51PM by PIB Delhi Some major initiatives have been undertaken by Small Industries Development Bank of India (SIDBI) during the last five years to improve the flow of credit to Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) across the country. These include the following initiatives: Subsequent to Union Budget Announcement FY 2024-25, SIDBI has opened 71 new branches across India from 01.04.2024 to 29.07.2026 to expand its reach to serve major MSME clusters and provide direct credit to MSMEs. As on March 31, 2026, SIDBI’s direct credit outstanding portfolio stands at ₹ 51,687 crores, as against ₹ 37,781 crores as on 31 March, 2025, registering a Y-o-Y growth of 36.8%. The Bank also provides refinance assistance to augment resources of Primary Lending Institutions (PLIs) to increase their flow of credit to MSMEs. As on March 31, 2026, SIDBI’s refinance outstanding portfolio stands at ₹ 4,50,571 crore, as against ₹ 3,85,327 crore as on 31 March, 2025, registering a Y-o-Y growth of 16.9%. SIDBI has launched a product on co-lending arrangement with Non-Banking Financial Companies (NBFCs) to provide affordable credit to smaller MSMEs, especially new borrowers, as part of its effort to reach underserved/ unserved MSMEs. During FY 202526, the Bank initiated co-lending arrangements with Regional Rural Banks (RRBs) to strengthen credit delivery and broaden financial access in underserved and untapped areas. Prayaas Scheme has been launched by SIDBI to facilitate access to affordable credit to informal micro-entrepreneurs/ micro-enterprises (IMEs), especially women and poor. SIDBI has launched a GST Sahay app for ‘on tap’ invoice-based (cash flow based) small value credit to micro enterprises using trade data and digital frameworks. The Government has introduced Emergency Credit Line Guarantee Scheme (ECLGS) 5.0 in May, 2026. Under the scheme, MSMEs are eligible for additional credit up to 20% of the peak fund-based working capital outstanding during the fourth quarter of FY 2025–26. The scheme provides 100% guarantee coverage to Member Lending Institutions (MLIs) towards the amount in default for such additional credit facility extended to the eligible MSME borrowers. For the scheduled passenger airlines, the guarantee coverage is 90%. However, the scheduled passenger airlines are eligible for additional credit up to 100% of the total peak credit outstanding (both fund-based and non-fund-based) during the fourth quarter of FY 2025-26. Under the scheme, additional credit flow of ₹ 2,55,000 crore is envisaged for MSMEs, non-MSMEs and scheduled passenger airlines. This information was given by Minister of State in the Ministry of Finance Shri Pankaj Chaudhary in Rajya Sabha today. ****** SR/AD (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2294261) आगंतुक पटल  : 354 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: Urdu , हिन्दी , Gujarati , Kannada Ministry of Finance Government Boosts MSME Financing Through SIDBI and ECLGS 5.0 SIDBI Expands Nationwide Presence with 71 New Branches; Direct Credit Portfolio Grows 36.8% Y-oY ECLGS 5.0 Envisages ₹2.55 Lakh Crore Additional Credit With up to 100% Guarantee Coverage for Eligible MSMEs प्रविष्टि तिथि:

ministry: Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying
title: Government Strengthens Dairy Development, Livestock Infrastructure and Animal Health Preparedness Across India
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying Government Strengthens Dairy Development, Livestock Infrastructure and Animal Health Preparedness Across India Strengthening Dairy Cooperatives and Breed Improvement Enhancing Preparedness Against Animal Disease Outbreaks प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                04 AUG 2026 1:02PM by PIB Delhi Union Minister for Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying, Shri Rajiv Ranjan Singh alias Lalan Singh , informed the Lok Sabha that the Government continues to strengthen the dairy and livestock sectors through focused interventions in dairy infrastructure, breed improvement, entrepreneurship promotion and animal health preparedness. The Government informed that milk procurement prices are determined by dairy cooperatives and private dairies based on prevailing market conditions, and no report has been received by the Department indicating that dairy farmers are not receiving remunerative prices due to the gap between procurement and retail prices. To strengthen the dairy sector, the National Programme for Dairy Development (NPDD) has facilitated the organisation of 36,611 new Dairy Cooperative Societies and strengthened 34,557 village-level dairy cooperative societies as of June 2026. Around 168 lakh litres per day of milk chilling capacity has been created, while 76,748 milk quality testing devices have been distributed. Under the Animal Husbandry Infrastructure Development Fund (AHIDF), projects with a total milk processing and value addition capacity of 418 lakh litres per day have been approved. The Milk Supply Review Dashboard Portal, integrated with the National Cooperative Database, currently reflects three active dairy cooperative societies in Delhi. Under the Rashtriya Gokul Mission (RGM), substantial progress has been achieved in indigenous breed development, genetic improvement and productivity enhancement. Tamil Nadu received Central assistance of ₹12,521.83 lakh during the last three years, fully utilised by the State. The support enabled 36.13 lakh artificial inseminations, strengthening of four semen stations, training and equipping of 475 MAITRIs, establishment of two IVF laboratories, creation of sex-sorted semen facilities, establishment of three Breed Multiplication Farms and assistance for Heifer Rearing Centres. The Government also highlighted nationwide achievements under the Rashtriya Gokul Mission, National Livestock Mission (NLM) and Livestock Health and Disease Control Programme (LHDCP). During the last five years, over 17.27 crore artificial inseminations have been carried out under the Nationwide Artificial Insemination Programme, benefiting nearly 5.98 crore farmers. A total of 47,687 MAITRIs (Multi-Purpose Artificial Insemination Technicians in Rural India) have been trained, 24 IVF laboratories established, 48 semen stations sanctioned and 28 heifer rearing centres approved. Under the National Livestock Mission, 4,084 breed multiplication farms have been approved, 1.61 lakh metric tonnes of quality fodder seed produced, and 204 silage and Total Mixed Ration units sanctioned. Large-scale vaccination against Foot and Mouth Disease, Brucellosis, Peste des Petits Ruminants and Classical Swine Fever continues under LHDCP. The Entrepreneurship Development Programme under the National Livestock Mission has sanctioned 4,291 projects involving a total project cost of ₹2,956.79 crore with approved subsidies of ₹1,356.53 crore. These projects are expected to generate around 21,000 direct employment opportunities and indirectly benefit approximately 91,000 farmers. The programme is implemented through a fully digitised portal with subsidy disbursement through the Public Finance Management System. The Government also informed the House that the national mock exercise, Pashujanya Yudh Abhyas (PYA), conducted in Madhya Pradesh from 29 June to 3 July 2026, has been successfully evaluated. The exercise strengthened preparedness for zoonotic disease outbreaks by improving coordination, surveillance, biosafety, laboratory protocols, infection prevention, emergency response and inter-agency communication. The Department continues to support States through disease surveillance, vaccination, laboratory strengthening, standard operating procedures, crisis management plans and capacity building under the Livestock Health and Disease Control Programme. ****** SM/ (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2294181) आगंतुक पटल  : 298 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: Urdu , हिन्दी , Gujarati , Tamil Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying Government Strengthens Dairy Development, Livestock Infrastructure and Animal Health Preparedness Across India Strengthening Dairy Cooperatives and Breed Improvement Enhancing Preparedness Against Animal Disease Outbreaks प्रविष्टि तिथि:

ministry: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
title: Update on AB PM-JAY
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Health and Family Welfare Update on AB PM-JAY As on 30 June 2026, AB-PMJAY Enables 12.69 Crore Cashless Hospital Admissions Worth ₹1.92 Lakh Crore, Reducing Out-of-Pocket Expenditure प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                04 AUG 2026 4:12PM by PIB Delhi Ayushman Bharat - Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (AB-PMJAY) provides health coverage of Rs. 5 lakh per family per year for secondary and tertiary care hospitalization to 12 crore economically vulnerable families, constituting the bottom 40% of India's population. In March 2024, the scheme was expanded to include approximately 37 lakh families of Accredited Social Health Activists, Anganwadi Workers, and Anganwadi Helpers. The scheme was further expanded in October 2024 to cover 6 crore senior citizens of age 70 years and above belonging to 4.5 crore families irrespective of their socio-economic status. The State/UT-wise details of Ayushman cards created can be accessed at https://dashboard.nha.gov.in/public/card AB-PMJAY has significantly contributed in reducing out-of-pocket expenditure. As on 30.06.2026, a total of 12.69 crore hospital admissions amounting to Rs.1.92 lakh crore have been authorized under the scheme through a network of 37,413 public and private hospitals. According to the National Health Accounts Estimates 2022-23, out of pocket expenditure as a proportion of total health expenditure declined from 62.6% in 2014-15 to 43.4% in 2022-23. This substantial reduction indicates that households are incurring a considerably lower share of healthcare costs directly from their own pockets, owing to increased public investment in health and the expansion of publicly financed health insurance schemes such as AB-PMJAY. ministry: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
title: Update on NFHS-6
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Health and Family Welfare Update on NFHS-6 NFHS-6 Fact Sheet Indicators Finalised by Technical Advisory Committee in Line with Government's Data Harmonisation Initiative NFHS-6 Fact Sheets Focused on Harmonised Key Indicators; Anaemia Estimates to Be Released Based on ICMR's Gold Standard Survey प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                04 AUG 2026 4:11PM by PIB Delhi The Ministry of Health and Family Welfare (MoH&FW) conducts an integrated survey namely National Family Health Survey (NFHS). The survey provides data on health and family welfare and associated domains like characteristics of the population; fertility and fertility preferences; family planning; maternal and child health; nutrition; morbidity and healthcare; women’s empowerment, etc. The National and State/UT Fact Sheets of sixth round of NFHS (2023-24) were released on 29.05.2026. The indicators to be included in the NFHS-6 National and State/UT Fact Sheets were ﬁnalized on the recommendations of the Technical Advisory Committee (TAC) constituted for NFHS-6, comprising representatives from concerned Ministries/Departments including Department of Drinking Water and Sanitation (DDWS), Ministry of Women & Child Development (MoWCD), Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI), Office of the Registrar General & Census Commissioner of India (ORGI), NITI Aayog, Department of Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities (DEPwD) etc. The TAC recommended ﬁnalizing the list of indicators for the Fact Sheets in line with the Data Harmonization initiatives of the Government of India (GoI), so as to avoid inconsistencies arising from fragmented and unharmonized data available across diﬀerent oﬃcial data sources. The TAC further recommended that the Fact Sheets are intended to present only key indicators, particularly those related to health and family welfare, so as to better highlight the key takeaways of the survey. Additionally, the Ministry of Health & Family Welfare, after due deliberations, decided to adopt the prevalence figures of anaemia to be arrived from an independent survey conducted by Indian Council of Medical Research utilizing the gold standard intravenous method for haemoglobin testing. The Union Minister of State for Health and Family Welfare, Smt. Anupriya Patel stated this in a written reply in the Rajya Sabha today. ******* SR HFW/PQ- Update on NFHS-6 /4 August 2026/5 (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2294277) आगंतुक पटल  : 222 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: Urdu , हिन्दी Ministry of Health and Family Welfare Update on NFHS-6 NFHS-6 Fact Sheet Indicators Finalised by Technical Advisory Committee in Line with Government's Data Harmonisation Initiative NFHS-6 Fact Sheets Focused on Harmonised Key Indicators; Anaemia Estimates to Be Released Based on ICMR's Gold Standard Survey प्रविष्टि तिथि:

ministry: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
title: Measures taken to strengthen 24×7 emergency services
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Health and Family Welfare Measures taken to strengthen 24×7 emergency services As on 26 June 2026, 100% of Public Healthcare Facilities Assessed Through IPHS Digital Toolkit; 64% Score Above 50% प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                04 AUG 2026 4:10PM by PIB Delhi Public health and Hospitals are a state subject. The primary responsibility of strengthening public healthcare system lies with the respective States/Union Territories. The Ministry of Health and Family Welfare provides technical and financial support to the States/ Union Territories to strengthen the public healthcare system in rural and underserved areas as per Indian Public Health Standards (IPHS), based on the proposals received in the form of Programme Implementation Plans (PIPs) under National Health Mission. Government of India provides approval for the proposal in the form of Record of Proceedings (RoPs) as per norms & available resources. States/ Union Territories are expected to ensure Primary Health Centres (PHCs) and Community Health Centres (CHCs) are functional with adequate staff, equipment, medicines and diagnostic facilities as per Indian Public Health Standards. The details regarding doctors, specialists and paramedical staff in rural health facilities across States/Union Territories can be accessed at the following link of HDI 2023-24: https://www.mohfwdohfw.gov.in/static/uploads/2026/05/57202cf30629539e4d0fb0a2f700ac62.pdf The Ministry has developed an open-source toolkit and a web-based dashboard (www.iphs.mohfw.gov.in) launched under IPHS on 28 th June 2024 to facilitate self- assessment by all levels of facilities including Ayushman Arogya Mandirs. The IPHS Dashboard is designed to monitor public health facilities' compliance with the IPHS 2022 standards and offers real-time updates, enabling oversight and data-driven decision-making to identify gaps and facilitate timely interventions. As on 26th June, 2026, 100% of public healthcare facilities have been assessed through IPHS ODK toolkit. Out of total assessed facilities 64% of Health facilities have scored above 50% score. Further, for strengthening 24x7 emergency services, obstetric care and diagnostic facilities in underserved rural areas, the Ministry’s support includes engagement of human resources, provision of essential drugs, diagnostics and medical equipment, infrastructure strengthening, establishment of Ayushman Arogya Mandirs (AAMs), ensuring 24×7 services and First Referral Units (FRUs), implementation of the Free Diagnostics Service Initiative, Free Drugs Service Initiative, Biomedical Equipment Maintenance & Management Programme, National Quality Assurance Standards (NQAS) and other quality improvement initiatives. This Ministry also supports ‘Free Diagnostics Service Initiative’ programme under NHM with the aim to provide accessible and affordable pathological and radiological diagnostics services closer to the community, which in turn reduces the Out-of-Pocket Expenditure (OOPE). Diagnostics services are provided free of cost at all levels of public health facilities (14 tests at Sub Centers, 63 at Primary Health Centers, 97 at Community Health Centres, 111 test at Sub District Hospitals and 134 tests at District Hospitals). For strengthening of Obstetric Care, comprehensive maternal healthcare services are supported under the National Health Mission (NHM), including antenatal care, institutional deliveries, skilled birth attendance, basic and comprehensive emergency obstetric care (including Caesarean section where indicated), postnatal care, referral transport, management of obstetric complications, and free maternal healthcare services under the Janani Shishu Suraksha Karyakram (JSSK) and Janani Suraksha Yojana (JSY), with the objective of ensuring safe motherhood and reducing maternal and neonatal mortality. The Union Minister of State for Health and Family Welfare, Shri. Prataprao Jadhav stated this in a written reply in the Rajya Sabha today. ******* SR HFW/PQ- Measures taken to strengthen 24×7 emergency services /4 August 2026/3 (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2294276) आगंतुक पटल  : 103 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: Urdu , हिन्दी Ministry of Health and Family Welfare Measures taken to strengthen 24×7 emergency services As on 26 June 2026, 100% of Public Healthcare Facilities Assessed Through IPHS Digital Toolkit; 64% Score Above 50% प्रविष्टि तिथि:

ministry: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
title: Measure undertaken to strengthen Health Research
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Health and Family Welfare Measure undertaken to strengthen Health Research Government Enhances Health Research Funding; ICMR Budget Rises from ₹2,732.13 Crore in 2024-25 to ₹4,000 Crore in 2026-27 Government Strengthened Health Research Ecosystem Through New ICMR Funding Framework and Strategic Research Programmes प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                04 AUG 2026 4:09PM by PIB Delhi Government has increased the budget in health research along with new schemes/initiatives to make research grants more competitive and accessible. The budgetary allocation for the Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR) has increased from ₹2,732.13 crore in Budget Estimates 2024–25 to ₹3,125.50 crore in Budget Estimates 2025–26 and ₹4,000.00 crore in Budget Estimates 2026–27. The allocation for 2026–27 represents an increase of approximately 21 per cent over the Revised Estimates for 2025–26 of ₹3,150.00 crore. The Government has also undertaken measures to broaden and strengthen the health-research funding ecosystem. ICMR has informed that it has rationalised and expanded its intramural and extramural grants architecture so that funding support is calibrated to the scale, maturity, risk and translational stage of a research proposal. ICMR has initiated new follow-on grants to utilize the leads from the initial research grants. The current structure includes Small or ANVESHAN Grants of up to ₹2 crore, Intermediate or NISCHAYAK ANVESHAN Grants ranging from ₹2 crore to ₹8 crore, the First-in-the-World Challenge with stage-linked support of up to ₹8 crore, and Centres for Advanced Research with support of up to ₹15 crore. These instruments support investigator-initiated research, proof-of-concept studies, validation of interventions, high-risk and high-reward innovation, multidisciplinary research and advanced research programmes. ICMR has further informed that it has initiated the following Strategic research funding grants to augment and supplement the research budget for public medical colleges and hospitals. i) Top-Tier Global Leadership Funding Scheme: A flagship initiative to elevate global ranking of top-ten NIRF-ranked medical institutions as research leaders. ii) ICMR–National Medical Commission (NMC) Joint Call: Research for Strengthening and Enhancing Quality of Medical Education by the top-100 NIRF-ranked medical institutions to support innovation and implementation research to enhance quality and outcomes of medical education with a focus on competency-based education, digital learning, and assessment reforms. iii) ICMR Initiative for Strengthening Intramural Research in three Central Government Medical Colleges, Delhi. iv) Anusandhan National Research Foundation (ANRF), in collaboration with ICMR and Gates Foundation, has launched the Mission for Advancement in High-Impact Areas (MAHA)-Medical Technology (महा MedTech). This landmark initiative aims to accelerate innovation in India’s medical technology sector, reduce reliance on high-cost imports, and promote equitable access to affordable and high-quality medical technologies. v) ICMR Clinical Care Excellence Initiative: Multi-centre Clinical Trials addressing Non-Communicable Diseases vi) Special Call for Proposals for Establishment of ICMR Centre for Advanced Research (CAR) for the Development of Priority Medical Devices and Diagnostic Technologies addressing unmet clinical needs identified by ICMR through extensive stakeholder consultations. The initiative seeks to promote the development of affordable, accessible, and indigenous healthcare technologies of national public health relevance for wider public benefit and long-term self-reliance in the MedTech sector. The priority medical devices and diagnostic technologies have been identified through a rigorous exercise involving eminent clinicians in different clinical settings across the country including clinicians from tier-1, tier-2 & tier-3 cities, resulting in a curated list of ~100 priority unmet clinical need based medical device/diagnostic technologies. vii) ICMR’s Multistate Implementation Research Study to improve coverage of high-quality Palliative Care Interventions to develop, implement, and evaluate a scalable palliative care model integrated with healthcare services in India and to evaluate cost-effectiveness and feasibility of the model and generate evidence for national scale-up for palliative care. ICMR supports several extramural research projects for frontier technologies including development of recombinant vaccines, biologics, cell and gene therapies, Robotics and AI-tools. 22 projects of frontier technology have been undertaken including CAR-T cell therapy & Robotics-based targeted therapy for cancer, cardiac massaging, root canal treatment. ICMR has further supported indigenous development of 97 medical devices/ diagnostic technologies and cost reduction for 11 technologies. Over 60 innovative projects have been supported in First in the World challenge. With a view to strengthen the domestic biopharmaceutical sector and enhance global competitiveness in biologics and biosimilars, the Government has announced the Biopharma SHAKTI scheme with an outlay of ₹10,000 crore over five years with an objective to build a globally competitive domestic ecosystem for biologics and biosimilars to support affordable healthcare in India and enable India to emerge as a global biopharma manufacturing and innovation hub. Further by supporting research and development, strengthening clinical trial infrastructure and promoting collaboration between academia, research institutions and industry, the Scheme seeks to encourage domestic innovation and manufacturing capabilities in the biopharmaceutical sector. Such initiatives are expected to contribute towards reducing import dependence over time and enhance India’s participation in the global biopharmaceutical market. The long-term goal is to move toward innovation leadership, including AI-designed biologics and advanced therapies and precision medicine to make these more affordable and accessible. The Union Minister of State for Health and Family Welfare, Shri. Prataprao Jadhav stated this in a written reply in the Rajya Sabha today. ******* SR HFW/PQ- Measure undertaken to strengthen Health Research/4 August 2026/2 (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2294275) आगंतुक पटल  : 92 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: हिन्दी Ministry of Health and Family Welfare Measure undertaken to strengthen Health Research Government Enhances Health Research Funding; ICMR Budget Rises from ₹2,732.13 Crore in 2024-25 to ₹4,000 Crore in 2026-27 Government Strengthened Health Research Ecosystem Through New ICMR Funding Framework and Strategic Research Programmes प्रविष्टि तिथि:

ministry: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
title: Update on NTEP
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Health and Family Welfare Update on NTEP ICMR Study Finds Drone-Assisted TB Sample Transport Reduces Diagnosis Time from 15 Days to 5 Days and Patient Expenditure from ₹9,451 to ₹91 ICMR's i-DRONE Initiative Cuts TB Diagnosis Time by Two-Thirds and Reduces Patient Costs by Over 99% प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                04 AUG 2026 4:08PM by PIB Delhi As per the latest study conducted by the Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR) under its i-DRONE initiative, drone-assisted transport of tuberculosis (TB) sputum samples has been found to significantly reduce the time and cost of TB diagnosis in remote and hard-to-reach areas. The study, conducted in Yadadri-Bhuvanagiri district of Telangana in collaboration with AIIMS Bibinagar and the National TB Elimination Programme (NTEP), demonstrated that the median turnaround time for TB diagnosis was reduced from 15 days to 5 days, while the mean out-of-pocket expenditure incurred by patients decreased from approximately Rs 9,451/- to Rs 91/-, thereby improving timely access to TB diagnostic services. The Union Minister of State for Health and Family Welfare, Smt. Anupriya Patel stated this in a written reply in the Rajya Sabha today. ******* SR HFW/PQ- Update on NTEP /4 August 2026/4 (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2294274) आगंतुक पटल  : 118 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: Urdu , हिन्दी Ministry of Health and Family Welfare Update on NTEP ICMR Study Finds Drone-Assisted TB Sample Transport Reduces Diagnosis Time from 15 Days to 5 Days and Patient Expenditure from ₹9,451 to ₹91 ICMR's i-DRONE Initiative Cuts TB Diagnosis Time by Two-Thirds and Reduces Patient Costs by Over 99% प्रविष्टि तिथि:

title: The Ministry of Heavy Industries (MHI) has not formulated any separate phased national policy to incentivize flex-fuel vehicles operating on fuel blended with more than 20% ethanol
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Heavy Industries The Ministry of Heavy Industries (MHI) has not formulated any separate phased national policy to incentivize flex-fuel vehicles operating on fuel blended with more than 20% ethanol प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                04 AUG 2026 6:35PM by PIB Delhi Production Linked Incentive scheme for Automobile & Auto Components (PLI-Auto scheme) is implemented on an all-India basis. The current status of implementation of PLI-Auto scheme is as below:- Parameter Cumulative till 31.03.2026 Investment (Rs. cr) 44,326 Incremental Sales (Base Year FY2019-20) (Rs. cr) 52,414 Employment generated (Nos.) 67,820 Incentive disbursed (Rs. cr) 2,386.36 To boost domestic manufacturing and localisation of AAT products, PLI-Auto scheme mandates minimum Domestic Value Addition (DVA) of 50% for availing incentives. As on 28.07.2026, 18 applicants have received DVA certificates for 155 AAT products/variants. The Ministry of Heavy Industries (MHI) has not formulated any separate phased national policy to incentivize flex-fuel vehicles operating on fuel blended with more than 20% ethanol. content:

title: An allocation of ₹2,000 crore has been made under the PM E-DRIVE Scheme for deployment of Electric Vehicle Public Charging Stations (EVPCS) on pan India basis
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Heavy Industries An allocation of ₹2,000 crore has been made under the PM E-DRIVE Scheme for deployment of Electric Vehicle Public Charging Stations (EVPCS) on pan India basis Posted On:
                04 AUG 2026 6:34PM by PIB Delhi The PM E-DRIVE Scheme is being implemented on a pan-India basis, and no State-wise allocation of funds has been made. As on 22.07.2026, a total of 42,035 EVs have been sold in Assam, under this Scheme which includes 8,003 EVs sold in Cachar district. Further, a total of 40,009 EVs have been incentivised in Assam with a total reimbursement of  ₹ 99.10 crore to OEMs. An allocation of ₹2,000 crore has been made under the PM E-DRIVE Scheme for deployment of Electric Vehicle Public Charging Stations (EVPCS) on pan India basis including the state of Assam.  Assam has not yet submitted any proposal for deployment of EVPCS under the PM E-DRIVE scheme. No such assessment has been done by the Ministry of Heavy Industries (MHI) for Cachar district of Assam. The MHI is implementing following schemes to promote electric mobility, strengthen charging infrastructure and encourage the adoption of electric public transport and commercial vehicles across the country including Cachar district and other parts of Assam: Faster Adoption and Manufacturing of (Hybrid &) Electric Vehicles in India (FAME India) Scheme Phase-II : The Government implemented this scheme for a period of five years from 01.04.2019 to 31.03.2024 with a total budgetary support of ₹11,500 crore. The scheme provided demand incentive for e-2Ws, e-3Ws, e-4Ws and grant for e-buses and setting up of EV public charging stations (EV PCS). FAME-II has supported the sale of approximately 16.72 lakh electric vehicles, including e-2Ws, e-3Ws, and e-4Ws. In addition, 5,297 electric buses (e-buses) have been deployed under the Scheme as on 30.06.2026. Further, an amount of ₹912.50 crore was allocated under the Scheme for the establishment of EVPCS across the country. Production Linked Incentive (PLI) Scheme for Automobile and Auto Component Industry in India (PLI-Auto): The Government notified this scheme for Automobile and Auto Component Industry in India, on 23.09.2021, for enhancing India's manufacturing capabilities for Advanced Automotive Technology (AAT) products, including EVs, with a budgetary outlay of ₹25,938 crore. Production Linked Incentive (PLI) Scheme for National Programme on Advanced Chemistry Cell (ACC) Battery Storage : The Government on 09.06.2021 notified the PLI  Scheme for manufacturing of ACC in the country with a budgetary outlay of ₹18,100 crore. The scheme aims to establish a competitive domestic manufacturing ecosystem for 50 GWh of ACC batteries. PM Electric Drive Revolution in Innovative Vehicle Enhancement (PM EDRIVE) Scheme: This scheme with an outlay of ₹10,900 crore is implemented from 01.04.2024. This scheme supports incentivization of approximately 28.30 lakh electric vehicles (EVs) including e-2W, e-3W, e-Trucks, e-buses and e-Ambulances. Further, grant for EV public charging stations (EV PCS) and upgradation of testing agencies is also available under this scheme. An allocation of ₹4,391 crore has been made under the scheme for deployment of 14,028 e-buses out of which 13,800 e-buses have been allocated in seven cities having four million plus population viz. Delhi, Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Mumbai, Ahmedabad, Pune and Surat. Further, 200 e-buses have been approved for Union Territory of Jammu & Kashmir. ₹2,000 crore has been allocated for deployment of EV Public Charging Stations on pan India basis. PM e-Bus Sewa-Payment Security Mechanism (PSM) Scheme : This Scheme notified on 28.10.2024, has an outlay of ₹3,435.33 crore and aims to support deployment of more than 38,000 electric buses. The objective of this scheme is to provide payment security to e-bus operators in case of default by Public Transport Authorities (PTAs). Following initiatives have also been taken up by the Government of India to increase the use  of electric vehicles in the country: – i.          GST on electric vehicles and chargers/ charging stations for electric vehicles has been reduced to 5%. ii.         The Ministry of Road Transport & Highways (MoRTH) announced that battery-operated vehicles will be given green license plates and be exempted from permit requirements. iii. MoRTH issued an advisory to states to waive road tax on EVs, which in turn will help reduce the initial cost of EVs. ******* TPJ (Release ID: 2294482) Visitor Counter : 77 Read this release in: हिन्दी Ministry of Heavy Industries An allocation of ₹2,000 crore has been made under the PM E-DRIVE Scheme for deployment of Electric Vehicle Public Charging Stations (EVPCS) on pan India basis Posted On:

title: ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT IN UT
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Home Affairs ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT IN UT प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                04 AUG 2026 3:32PM by PIB Delhi The Government has made sustained efforts to ensure the economic development of Union Territories (UTs) through a series of focused interventions, including development of world-class infrastructure, enhancement of road, sea and air connectivity, augmentation of digital connectivity, promotion of tourism, strengthening of education, healthcare, industrial development, improving urban services, bringing in governance reforms, ease of doing business, and livelihood generation, etc. The details are given at Annexure-I. The Government has taken various measures to promote renewable and green energy in the UTs through effective implementation of schemes, PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana, PM-KUSUM, etc., development of utility-scale solar projects, augmentation of rooftop solar installations, promotion of household solar adoption; and other interventions.  The details of measures taken in this regard, and the benefits arising out of those are given at Annexure-II. Annexure -I (i) Landmark MICE (Meetings, Incentives, Conferences and Exhibitions) infrastructure projects like the Yasho Bhoomi Convention Centre and Bharat Mandapam in Delhi have been completed. (ii) Strategic infrastructure projects in Jammu & Kashmir (J&K), like the Chenani-Nashri Tunnel, Z-Morh Tunnel, and the Udhampur-Srinagar-Baramulla Rail Link including the iconic Chenab Rail Bridge have been completed. (iii) Road infrastructure has been augmented, such as the development of the Urban Extension Road-II (UER-II) and the Dwarka Expressway in Delhi, the Delhi-Dehradun and Delhi-Meerut Expressways; and construction of new motorable bridges in Ladakh, etc., which have significantly improved regional connectivity. (iv) Construction of helipads and hangars has been completed in Ladakh to ensure connectivity to difficult terrains and for medical emergencies, even during the winter months. Air connectivity in Lakshadweep has improved with daily scheduled flights and successful trial seaplane landings. New airport terminals have been constructed at Sri Vijaya Puram in Andaman & Nicobar Islands (A&NI) and at NAMO airport, Daman. (v) Digital connectivity has expanded significantly in UTs, especially in island UTs of Andaman & Nicobar Islands (A&NI) and Lakshadweep. The Chennai Andaman Nicobar Islands (CANI) Optical Fibre Cable (OFC) project in the UT of A&NI and the Kochi Lakshadweep Island (KLI) Submarine OFC Project have revolutionised the digital connectivity between the islands and the mainland, enabling online education, tele-medicine,  e-governance, digital  banking  and  e-commerce.  These initiatives have led to  reduced data costs, increased mobile and internet/broadband penetration, and enhanced internet tele-density and speeds across the island UTs. In A&NI bandwidth has increased from 4.12 Gbps to 243 Gbps and in Lakshadweep from 1.7 Gbps to 200 Gbps. (vi) Tourism has been identified as a key sector due to its multiplier effect on economic growth and livelihood opportunities, leading to improved standards and quality of living. The Government is actively working towards transforming UTs into global hubs of tourism. Schemes such as the Swadesh Darshan and PRASHAD have been effectively leveraged to develop tourism infrastructure in UTs. Letter of award has been issued for development of 04 eco-tourism projects in A&NI. 50 tents at Bangaram and 100 tents at Thinnakara have commenced operation in Lakshadweep; and world class seafronts and premier river fronts, and tent cities have been developed in DNH&DD. (x)       UTs are undertaking solar and hydro power projects to achieve power self-sufficiency with cleaner, cheaper sources of power. (xi)      Measures have also been taken towards industrial development in UTs. Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Home Affairs FINANCIAL ASSISTANCE FOR NATURAL DISASTERS प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                04 AUG 2026 3:29PM by PIB Delhi As per the National Policy on Disaster Management (NPDM), the primary responsibility for disaster management, including disbursal of relief assistance on ground level, rests with the State Governments concerned. The State Governments undertake relief measures in the wake of natural calamities, from the State Disaster Response Fund (SDRF) already placed at their disposal as well as other available resources, in accordance with Government of India approved items and norms. The Central Government supplements the efforts of the State Governments and provides requisite logistics and financial support. In the case of disaster of a 'severe nature', additional financial assistance is provided from the National Disaster Response Fund (NDRF) on the basis of the recommendations of the Inter-Ministerial Central Team (IMCT), in accordance with the prescribed procedure. This Ministry does not centrally maintain data regarding the loss of lives and property due to any disaster in the country.  However, the details of damages reported by State Governments/ UTs due to various hydro-meteorological disasters in the country including Himachal Pradesh during last three years i.e. 2023-24 to 2025-26 are as per Annexure-I. Further, the details of State-wise allocation and releases of funds under State Disaster Response Fund (SDRF) and National Disaster Response Fund (NDRF) during last three years i.e. 2023-24 to 2025-26 are as per Annexure-II. The Central Government has taken several initiatives to strengthen disaster risk reduction and enhance resilience in hilly States, including Himachal Pradesh, under the existing institutional and policy framework; as per the details provided below : - The National Disaster Management Plan (NDMP) and the guidelines issued by the National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA) cover disasters such as landslides, cloudbursts, Glacial Lake Outburst Floods (GLOFs), forest fires and earthquakes, to which the Himalayan region is particularly vulnerable. The Government has approved the National Landslide Risk Mitigation Project (NLRMP) for implementation in 15 States, including Himachal Pradesh, with the objective of reducing mortality and economic losses by reducing the vulnerability of communities and their assets to landslides. Under the project, a Central share of ₹125.00 crore and State share of ₹14.00 crore have been approved for Himachal Pradesh. To adopt various structural and non-structural mitigation measures for addressing the risk of Glacial Lake Outburst Floods (GLOFs), the National Glacial Lake Outburst Flood Risk Mitigation Programme (NGRMP) was approved for the States of Arunachal Pradesh, Himachal Pradesh, Sikkim and Uttarakhand. Mitigation Scheme for Forest Fire Risk Management has also been approved, under which central share of ₹ 7.34 crore and state share of ₹ 0.82 crore has been approved for Himachal Pradesh. Under the National Project for Strengthening Community Based Disaster Risk Reduction Initiatives in Panchayati Raj Institutions, a total budget of ₹14.84 crore has been allocated for Himachal Pradesh to integrate Disaster Risk Reduction (DRR) practices into the Panchayati Raj governance structure through a bottom-up approach. An integrated warning system (SACHET) based on the Common Alerting Protocol (CAP) has also been operationalized; under this system, geo-targeted early warnings are disseminated by integrating alerts issued by the India Meteorological Department (IMD), Central Water Commission (CWC), Geological Survey of India (GSI), Indian National Centre for Ocean Information Services (INCOIS), Defence Geo-informatics Research Establishment (DGRE), and Forest Survey of India (FSI). Apart from this, it is continuously strengthening multi-disaster early warning systems, disaster-resistant infrastructure, community preparedness and capacity building through initiatives like Aapda Mitra (Aapda Mitra) and Yuva Aapda Mitra Scheme (Yuva Aapda Mitra Scheme). title: MODERNISATION OF CAPF
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Home Affairs MODERNISATION OF CAPF प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                04 AUG 2026 3:27PM by PIB Delhi The major measures undertaken for the modernization of Central Armed Police Forces (CAPFs) include induction of modern weapons, surveillance and communication systems, mobility platforms, force protection equipment, operational infrastructure and advanced technologies, through a Central Sector  Scheme, namely Modernization Plan-IV for CAPFs. The major items provided to CAPFs through this Scheme during the last three years include: (i)      Modern weapon systems and combat equipment: Assault rifles, Glock pistols with Corner Shot systems, modern arms and ammunition and weapon accessories. (ii)     Surveillance and intelligence systems: Thermal imagers, passive night vision goggles, UAVs/drones, Automatic Fire Detection and Suppression Systems and other electronic surveillance equipment. (iii)    Communication and Information Technology: Secure communication equipment, Hyper-Converged Infrastructure (HCI) servers/nodes, networking infrastructure, command-and-control systems and digital operational platforms. (iv)    Mobility and specialized vehicles: Medium Bullet Proof Vehicles, Light Bullet Proof Vehicles, Mine Protected Vehicles, Wheel Armoured Platforms, Emergency Rescue Fire Tenders and Rubberized Inflatable Boats. (v)     Force protection equipment: Bullet-resistant jackets, ballistic helmets, protective shields and other personal protective equipment. (vi)    Specialized operational equipment: Counter-IED/bomb disposal equipment, rescue and disaster response equipment and specialized tactical gear. (vii)   Infrastructure: Modern training facilities, communication infrastructure, logistics support systems, ICT infrastructure, maintenance facilities and other operational infrastructure to support border guarding and internal security operations. Force-wise and year-wise funds allotted to CAPFs and expenditure incurred under Modernization Plan-IV are given in Annexure-A. As a result of the modernization measures, the operational capability of CAPFs has improved significantly and these interventions have enhanced operational preparedness, mobility, situational awareness, surveillance,  force protection, intelligence gathering and response capability, thereby strengthening border guarding, counter-insurgency, anti-Naxal and other internal security operations and to effectively address emerging security challenges. title: PROVISIONS IN BNS TO DEAL CRIMES
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Home Affairs PROVISIONS IN BNS TO DEAL CRIMES प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                04 AUG 2026 3:26PM by PIB Delhi The Government is committed to prevention and countering of the crime against women and children. In the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, for the first time, the provisions relating to crime against woman and child have been given precedence and placed under one Chapter. Strict punishments up to death sentence have been provided for the offences against women. Punishment for gang rape of a woman below the age of 18 years is life imprisonment till remainder of the convict’s natural life or death. A new offence for having sexual intercourse on false promise of marriage, employment, promotion or by concealing identity, etc. has also been incorporated in Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023. Main provisions related to protection of women and children in the new sanhitas are given in Annexure. PROVISIONS FOR PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN Offences against woman and child have been given precedence over all other offences in a new chapter-V of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023. In Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, the age differential for minor victims of gang rape has been done away with. Earlier different punishments were prescribed for gang rape on a girl below the age of 16 years and 12 years. This provision has been modified and now gang rape on a woman below the age of eighteen years is punishable with imprisonment of life or death. Women have been recognized as an adult member of family who can receive summons on behalf of the person summoned. The earlier reference to ‘some adult male member’ has been replaced with ‘some adult member’. In order to provide more protection to the victim and enforce transparency in investigation related to an offence of rape, the statement of the victim shall be recorded through audio video means by police. For certain offences against woman, statement of the victim is to be recorded, as far as practicable, by a woman Magistrate and in her absence a male Magistrate in the presence of a woman to ensure sensitivity and fairness, creating a supportive environment for victims. Medical practitioners are mandated to send the medical report of a victim of rape to the investigating officer within 7 days. It is provided that no male person under the age of fifteen years or above the age of 60 years (65 years earlier) or a woman or a mentally or physically disabled person or a person with acute illness shall be required to attend at any place other than the place in which such male person or woman resides. In cases where such a person is willing to attend the police station, they may be allowed to do so. The new laws provide for free first-aid or medical treatment to victims of crimes against women and children at all hospitals. This provision ensures immediate access to essential medical care, prioritizing the well-being and recovery of victims during challenging times. ix. The act of hiring, employing or engaging a child to commit an offence, is made a punishable offence under section 95 of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023, which entails punishment of imprisonment of minimum seven years, extendable to ten years. This provision aims to deter gangs or groups from employing/hiring children for committing offence. This was stated by the Minister of State in the Ministry of Home Affairs Shri Bandi Sanjay Kumar in a written reply to a question in the Lok Sabha. ***** RK/RR/PR/PS/SC (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2294238) आगंतुक पटल  : 128 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: Urdu , हिन्दी Ministry of Home Affairs PROVISIONS IN BNS TO DEAL CRIMES प्रविष्टि तिथि:

title: ZERO TOLERANCE FOR DRUG TRAFFICKERS
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Home Affairs ZERO TOLERANCE FOR DRUG TRAFFICKERS प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                04 AUG 2026 3:25PM by PIB Delhi In view of the increasing challenges of illegal narcotics trade and drug abuse, Narcotics Control Bureau (NCB), in coordination with concerned State and Union Territory Police, continues to undertake intelligence-led operations and preventive measures to protect youth from the menace of drugs. Various stringent actions taken under a ‘Zero Tolerance’ policy to deter drug traffickers are as under: - (i)      To address the challenge of illicit drug trafficking & abuse of drugs, Vision Document on Narcotics Control (2026-2029) has been released on 26.06.2026, which lays down a 3-year road map with clear priorities and time bound targets to be achieved by various stakeholders to control drugs with ‘Whole-of-Government’ & ‘Whole-of-Society’ approach. (ii)     NCB, Drug Law Enforcement Agencies (DLEAs) and State Police are actively engaged in enforcement activity under the Narcotics Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (NDPS) Act, 1985. These concerted efforts have resulted in significant achievements in term of drug seizures, registration of cases, arrests, disposal of seized drugs, destruction of illicit cultivation, financial investigations and preventive detention under Prevention of Illicit Traffic in Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (PITNDPS) Act, 1988. (iii)    Established a 4-tier Narco-Coordination Centre (NCORD) mechanism for ensuring better coordination between Central & State Drug Law Enforcement Agencies and other stake holders in the field of controlling drug trafficking and drug abuse in India. (iv)    An NCORD portal has been developed by NCB. It is an all in one portal for information related to drug law enforcement. Topics like NCORD, Training & Capacity Building, Narco-offenders data, legal information, exemplary initiatives taken by states etc are covered on the NCORD portal. (v)     To monitor the investigation of significant and important drug cases including cases of narco-terrorism, a Joint Coordination Committee (JCC ) with DG, NCB as its Chairman has been set up. So far, 11 JCC meetings at the Central level and 75 JCC meetings at the State level have been conducted. (vi)    All Director General of Police (DGPs) of States/UTs have been requested for sensitization of beat constables, field officers and SHOs regarding Red Flag Indicators (RFI) and emerging threats relating to clandestine manufacturing of synthetic drugs, particularly Mephedrone and Amphetamine-type Stimulants (ATS). (vii)   NCB has been regularly coordinating with other agencies like Excise, Border Security Force (BSF), State ANTF etc. to conduct joint operations to control the drug trafficking. (viii)  Financial investigations and effective implementation of the PITNDPS is being regularly emphasized at forums viz. NCORD, JCC, Regional Conference for dismantling and weakening of organized synthetic drug trafficking networks. (ix)    Comprehensive guideline on financial investigation, facilitating systematic identification, tracing and attachment of proceeds of crime have been issued. (x)     For the capacity building of Drug Law Enforcement Officers and Agencies, NCB organizes workshops/ seminars/ training programmes. NCB is regularly conducting specialised training programmes on investigation of clandestine laboratories and precursor chemical diversion in collaboration with the United States-Drug Enforcement Administration (US-DEA), with participation of officers from Central Agencies and State DLEAs. (xi)    India holds regular Director General (DG) Level/Bilateral talks on drug related matters with countries such as Myanmar, Nepal, Thailand, Sri Lanka, Indonesia, Singapore, United States of America (USA). (xii)   NCB has strengthened international cooperation in drug control through bilateral agreements with 27 countries and Memorandum of Understanding (MoUs) with 19 countries. (xiii)  A National Narcotics Helpline " मादक - पदार्थ निषेध आसूचना केंद्र " ( MANAS) was launched as a 24x7, toll-free National Narcotics Call Centre. MANAS has been envisioned as an integrated system providing a single platform for citizens to log, register and resolve drug related issues/problems through various mode of communications like call (1933), e-mail, web portal & UMANG mobile app. (xiv)  Launched "Mission Drug Free Campus" in various educational institutions, universities all over India, in which special focus is being given to the youth and they are being sensitized about the importance of drug free campuses. As domain specific initiatives, Government through NCB has adopted an intelligence-led and technology driven approach to identify and dismantle drug trafficking networks operating through online platforms, encrypted communication applications and the Darknet. The steps taken in this regard are as under: Strengthened capabilities to counter technology enabled drug trafficking by engaging cyber experts to investigate darknet enabled drug trafficking and cryptocurrency-based transactions. To enhance the technical expertise of enforcement personnel, NCB, in  collaboration  with  the  US-DEA  and Rashtriya  Raksha  University (RRU), Gandhinagar, has conducted several capacity building programmes for officers of NCB and other Drug Law Enforcement Agencies (DLEAs) on cyber enabled narcotics investigations, digital forensics, darknet monitoring, cryptocurrency investigations and other emerging technologies used in drug trafficking. Furthermore, the Vision Document on Narcotics Control (2026–2029) has been released on 26.06.2026 envisages the establishment of dedicated Darknet and Cryptocurrency Cells in all Anti-Narcotics Task Forces (ANTFs), adoption of advanced technologies and AI-enabled analytics, research, capacity building of agencies and enhanced inter-agency coordination to dismantle organized cyber enabled drug trafficking networks. The administration of the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (NDPS) Act, 1985 lies with the Department of Revenue. The Government undertakes periodic reviews of the provisions of the NDPS Act, taking into account judicial pronouncements, implementation experience, and gaps identified by enforcement agencies and stakeholders. Based on such reviews and keeping in view emerging challenges, amendments to the Act are proposed wherever considered necessary. This forms part of the Government’s continuous legislative review process to ensure that the statutory framework remains effective, contemporary and responsive to evolving requirements. The Vision Document on Narcotics Control (2026-2029) inter-alia has focused on creating Drug Free Campus (+500 meter) around educational institutions. Further, consent-based screening Test for students as part of student wellness programme is also proposed in the Vision Document at Centrally Funded Higher Educational Institutions. The initiative forms part of the three-year, time bound roadmap under the Vision Document, which also promotes Drug Free Campuses, preventive education, awareness programmes, counselling and community participation to create a safe and drug-free environment in educational institutions. This was stated by the Minister of State in the Ministry of Home Affairs Shri Nityanand Rai in a written reply to a question in the Lok Sabha. ***** RK/RR/PS/SC (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2294237) आगंतुक पटल  : 150 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: Urdu , हिन्दी , Bengali Ministry of Home Affairs ZERO TOLERANCE FOR DRUG TRAFFICKERS प्रविष्टि तिथि:
