title: EMPLOYMENT UNDER VB-GRAM-G
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Rural Development EMPLOYMENT UNDER VB-GRAM-G प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                04 AUG 2026 4:25PM by PIB Delhi Consequent upon commencement of the Viksit Bharat– Guarantee for Rozgar and Aajeevika Mission (Gramin) (VB-G RAM G) Act, 2025, the scheme has successfully been implemented in rural areas of the entire country w.e.f 01.07.2026. The VB-G RAM G provides for a statutory guarantee of one hundred and twenty five days of wage employment in a financial year to every rural household whose adult members volunteer to undertake unskilled manual work against one hundred day of guaranteed wage employment available under Mahatma Gandhi NREGS. The new scheme has been successfully implemented in the State of Maharashtra and Madhya Pradesh also w.e.f 0.1.07.2026. In case of Maharashtra interim allocation Rs.4420.32 crore has been made for the State. Subsequently, Mother Sanctions amounting to Rs.1459.92 Crore have been issued to the State of Maharashtra as first installment of Central Share under various components based on the proposal received from the State. Further in case of Madhya Pradesh an interim allocation Rs.6252.03 crore has been made for the State. Subsequently, Mother Sanctions amounting to Rs.630.76 Crore have been issued to the State of Madhya Pradesh as first installment of Central Share under various components based on the proposal received from the State. It is also stated that under Section 5(4) of the Act, the State Governments may make provision for providing additional days of employment beyond the period guaranteed under the Act from their own resources. The Act also aims to strengthen sustainable rural livelihoods through the creation of durable assets and implementation of the permissible works specified in Schedule I of the Act, namely Water-related Works, Core Rural Infrastructure, Livelihood-related Infrastructure and Special Works to Mitigate Extreme Weather Events. These provisions are intended to enhance livelihood security, strengthen rural infrastructure and promote sustainable rural development. Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana–National Rural Livelihoods Mission (DAY-NRLM), a flagship poverty alleviation programme of the Ministry of Rural Development, is being implemented through the State Rural Livelihoods Missions (SRLMs) across 760 districts and 7,246 blocks in 34 States and Union Territories including Maharashtra and Madhya Pradesh. As of June 2026, the Mission has mobilized about 10.08 crore rural households into nearly 92 lakh Self Help Groups (SHGs). Under the existing provisions of DAY-NRLM, capitalization support is provided to eligible SHGs in the form of Revolving Fund (RF) of ₹20,000–₹30,000 per SHG and Community Investment Fund (CIF) of up to ₹2.50 lakh per SHG to support income-generating and livelihood activities, including entrepreneurial ventures. In addition, interest subvention is available on bank loans to eligible SHGs. For loans up to ₹3 lakh, banks provide credit at a concessional interest rate of 7% per annum. For loans above ₹3 lakh and up to ₹5 lakh, banks extend credit at an interest rate equivalent to their one-year MCLR or any other external benchmark-based lending rate or 10% per annum, whichever is lower. Cumulatively, loans amounting to ₹13.41 lakh crore have been disbursed to SHGs under the Mission. These benefits are available to eligible SHGs, including those in Maharashtra and Madhya Pradesh, in accordance with the scheme guidelines. This information was given by the Minister of State for Rural Development SHRI KAMLESH PASWAN in a written reply in Lok Sabha today. ***** RC/PU (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2294301) आगंतुक पटल  : 148 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: Urdu , हिन्दी , Telugu Ministry of Rural Development EMPLOYMENT UNDER VB-GRAM-G प्रविष्टि तिथि:

title: SOCIO-ECONOMIC UPLIFTMENT OF RURAL WOMEN
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Rural Development SOCIO-ECONOMIC UPLIFTMENT OF RURAL WOMEN प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                04 AUG 2026 4:20PM by PIB Delhi The Ministry of Rural Development is implementing Deendayal AntyodayaYojana – National Rural Livelihoods Mission (DAY – NRLM) across the country (except Delhi & Chandigarh) with the objective of organizing the rural households into Self Help Groups (SHGs) and continuously nurturing and supporting them till they attain appreciable increase in income over a period of time and improve their quality of life. Cumulatively, 10.08 crore women have been mobilized into 92 lakh SHGs. The mission seeks to achieve its objective through investing in four core components, viz., social mobilization, promotion and strengthening of self-managed and financially sustainable community institutions of the rural poor; financial inclusion of the rural poor; sustainable livelihoods; and social inclusion, social development through its following sub-schemes. i) National Rural Livelihoods Mission (NRLM): A sub-scheme to promote sustainable institutions of the poor, their capacity building, livelihoods, ensuring access to financial services, strengthening social development outcomes such as Food, Nutrition, Health, WASH(FNHW) and gender inclusion ii) Start-up Village Entrepreneurship Programme (SVEP): SVEP is a sub-scheme under the DAY-NRLM , supports Self-Help Group (SHG) members and their family members in establishing small non-farm enterprises. The programme is implemented at the block level and as on May 2026, more than 6.5 lakh enterprises have been supported under SVEP. iii) MahilaKisanSashakthikaranPariyojana (MKSP)-Under MahilaKisanSashaktikaranPariyojana (MKSP), which is another sub-scheme of DAY-NRLM aims at meeting the specific needs of women farmers to enable them to achieve socio-economic empowerment. The primary objective of the MKSP is to empower women in agriculture by making systematic investments to enhance their participation and productivity, as also create and sustain their agriculture-based livelihoods. The scheme also supports development of a pool of community resource persons to enable the community institutions to manage their activities. iv) DeenDayalUpadhyayaGrameenKaushalyaYojana (DDU-GKY): DDU-GKY provides placement-linked skill training and employment opportunities in diverse sectors. Since inception (2014-15), it has trained 18.45 lakh rural youth including women and facilitated placement of 12.35 lakh candidates. Social inclusion remains at the core of the programme, with participation of 9.69 lakh women, 5.94 lakh SCs, 3.24 lakh STs, 3.12 lakh minorities and 0.14 lakh Persons with Disabilities. v) Rural Self Employment Training Institutes (RSETI): RSETIs promote entrepreneurship and self-employment among rural households through short-term, demand-driven training and handholding support. RSETIs have trained 62.45 lakh candidates and successfully settled 45.25 lakh rural youth, largely through self-employment and micro-enterprises. Women constitute a significant share of beneficiaries, with 43.71 lakh (over 70%) women trained, alongside substantial participation from SC, ST, OBC, minority and PwD communities. The programme is supported by a robust network of 647 RSETIs across 634 districts. The details of funds allocated, released/utilised under NRLM during the last five years, State wise, including Karnataka is given at Annexure-I. District-wise funds are not allocated under DAY-NRLM scheme. The number of beneficiaries under DAY-NRLM scheme during the last five years, State wise and district wise including Chitradurga districts are given at Annexure-II and Annexure-III. DAY-NRLM has undertaken focused initiatives for the inclusion and economic empowerment of Scheduled Castes (SCs), Scheduled Tribes (STs), and Other Backward Classes (OBCs). The Mission prioritizes mobilization of vulnerable households into Self‑Help Groups (SHGs), strengthening of Village Organisations and Cluster Level Federations, and ensuring access to community investment funds, bank credit, livelihood promotion, skill development, and social security schemes. Emphasis is placed on tribal and socially excluded communities through targeted outreach in aspirational and tribal districts, dedicated capacity building, convergence with departments such as Social Welfare, and support for agriculture, livestock, non‑farm enterprises, and traditional livelihoods. These interventions have enhanced financial inclusion, women’s leadership, income generation, and access to entitlements among SC, ST, and OBC households, contributing significantly to poverty reduction and social inclusion across the country. DDU-GKY is a placement-linked skilling programme for rural poor youth, and it explicitly prioritizes marginalized groups. The scheme mandates coverage norms of 50% for SC/ST, 15% for minorities, and 33% for women, and also gives special attention to women-headed households, persons with disabilities, and manual scavengers. For women from SC/ST/OBC/EWS backgrounds can access free skill training, boarding and lodging, post-placement support, and employment-linked pathways without upfront training cost. DDU-GKY therefore serves as the main route for wage employment and career mobility for disadvantaged rural women with participation of 9.69 lakh women, 5.94 lakh SCs, 3.24 lakh STs, 3.12 lakh minorities and 0.14 lakh Persons with Disabilities. Under RSETI, Women constitute a significant share of beneficiaries, with 43.71 lakh (over 70%) women trained, alongside substantial participation from SC, ST, OBC, minority and PwD communities. The programme is supported by a robust network of 647 RSETIs across 634 districts. Annexure I State- wise funds allocated, released/utilised under NRLM during the last five years (inRs. Lakhs) Sl. ministry: Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways
title: PRIVATE INVESTMENT AND EXPANSION OF NATIONAL WATERWAYS
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways PRIVATE INVESTMENT AND EXPANSION OF NATIONAL WATERWAYS प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                04 AUG 2026 3:41PM by PIB Delhi To encourage private investment and expand the operational network of National Waterways (NWs) for cargo and passenger traffic, the Government has notified the National Waterways (Construction of Jetties/Terminals) Regulations, 2025 to facilitate the construction and operation of terminals by private entities. Further, the Jalvahak Scheme has been launched for providing incentives up to 35% to promote cargo movement on inland waterways. The Government is also encouraging private sector participation through Public-Private Partnership (PPP) models duly assigning the O&M of terminals on long concession period. The Jalyan & Navic portal, a One Nation One Registration single window system developed to serve as a centralized national registry for inland vessels and crew, is fully operational. Eighteen States/UTs have been onboarded on the portal and 9,953 inland vessels and 1,215 crew are registered on this portal as on 30 th July, 2026. The major challenges in increasing cargo and passenger movement on NWs include limited industrial zone along the NWs; limited availability of suitable inland vessels; inadequate first and last-mile connectivity; limited multimodal logistics infrastructure; low awareness among cargo owners and operators regarding the benefits of Inland Water Transport (IWT). To address these challenges, the Government has undertaken a number of measures which are given at Annexure. Annexure Measures taken to address the challenges in increasing cargo and passenger movement on National Waterways: Development of Multi-Modal Terminals, Inter-Modal Terminals, community jetties, floating terminals and cargo aggregation hubs to strengthen multimodal connectivity and facilitate seamless cargo movement. Implementation of the Jalvahak Scheme to incentivise movement of cargo through inland waterways and promote modal shift from road and rail. Notification of the National Waterways (Construction of Jetties/Terminals) Regulations, 2025 to facilitate private sector investment in terminal and jetty infrastructure. Development of an enabling ecosystem for deployment of inland vessels by improving fairway conditions and encouraging private participation in vessel operations. Operationalization of additional routes under the Indo-Bangladesh Protocol (IBP) to improve regional connectivity and expand cargo movement. Development of passenger and cruise infrastructure on suitable National Waterways to promote tourism and regional passenger transport. Engagement with Central Ministries, State Governments, Public Sector Undertakings and private stakeholders to promote modal shift of suitable cargo to inland waterways and enhance utilization of the NWs. Development of Multi Modal Logistic Parks (MMLPs) along the NWs. Fairway maintenance through river training works, fairway maintenance, channel marking and hydrographic surveys. ministry: Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways
title: SHIPBUILDING PROMOTION AND MARITIME FINANCING
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways SHIPBUILDING PROMOTION AND MARITIME FINANCING प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                04 AUG 2026 3:40PM by PIB Delhi The Government has approved Shipbuilding Financial Assistance Scheme (SBFAS), which is an extension of Shipbuilding Financial Assistance Policy (SBFAP), with an outlay of ₹ 24,736 crore to address cost disadvantages of Indian shipyards vis-a-vis global shipyards. The scheme guidelines to operationalize SBFAS have been issued on 26.12.2025. Maritime Development Fund (MDF), with a corpus of ₹ 25,000 crore has been established for providing long term financing support to the shipbuilding and maritime sector. It comprises of a Maritime Investment Fund (MIF) of ₹ 20,000 crore with 49% participation from the Government of India to support equity financing for maritime sector, and an Interest Incentivization Fund (IIF) of ₹ 5,000 crore to reduce the effective cost of debt for shipyards. The guidelines for MDF have been issued on 20.02.2026. SBI Ventures Limited has been appointed as the Fund Manager for MIF on 26.05.2026. National Shipbuilding Mission (NSbM), an inter-ministerial body, has been established as the nodal agency to oversee the implementation of Shipbuilding schemes viz. Shipbuilding Financial Assistance Scheme (SBFAS) and Shipbuilding Development Scheme (SBDS) launched by Government of India. Under the Shipbuilding Development Scheme, proposals for the development of greenfield shipbuilding clusters in Andhra Pradesh, Gujarat and Tamil Nadu, as well as three brownfield capacity expansion projects of various existing shipyards have been given in-principle approval, after appraisal by NSbM. The objective of these initiatives is to position India as a global hub in the shipbuilding and maritime sector in line with Maritime India Vision 2030 and Maritime Amrit Kaal Vision, 2047. This information was given by the Union Minister of Ports, Shipping and Waterways, Sarbananda Sonowal, in a written reply to the Rajya Sabha. *** MI/Indu (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2294248) आगंतुक पटल  : 132 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: Urdu , हिन्दी Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways SHIPBUILDING PROMOTION AND MARITIME FINANCING प्रविष्टि तिथि:

ministry: Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways
title: ‘SEAFARER-FIRST’ INITIATIVE
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways ‘SEAFARER-FIRST’ INITIATIVE प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                04 AUG 2026 3:39PM by PIB Delhi The Government accords the highest priority to the safety, security and welfare of Indian seafarers, who form a significant part of the global maritime workforce. In view of the escalation of the security situation in Iran, the Strait of Hormuz, the Persian Gulf and adjacent waters, the Directorate General of Maritime Administration (DGMA), a subordinate office under this Ministry has instituted a comprehensive and graded 'Seafarer-First' framework of measures. As part of this a real-time reporting, tracking and monitoring mechanism for vessels and seafarers operating in the said region is in place and operational. The details of steps/ measures taken by the Government are placed at Annexure . ANNEXURE Advisories to Ensure the Safety and Security of Indian Seafarers: Following advisories operate alongside the standing maritime security architecture established under DGS Circular No. 08 of 2024 dated 10.04.2024 and are supported by a 24-hour Control Room, continuous real-time monitoring through the DG Communication Centre under DGMA, and the issue of a Situation Report every 24 hours. DGS Circular No. 01 of 2026 dated 14.01.2026 – issued pursuant to the advisory of the Ministry of External Affairs and the Embassy of India, Tehran, advising all Recruitment and Placement Services Licence (RPSL) companies and shipping companies not to deploy Indian seafarers to Iran until further orders, and advising vessels calling at Iranian ports or transiting the Strait of Hormuz to exercise utmost caution. DGS Circular No. 08 of 2026 dated 28.02.2026 – mandating comprehensive ship-shore security drills covering loitering munitions, unmanned surface vessels and similar threats, testing of the Ship Security Alert System prior to transit, voyage-specific risk assessment by owners, operators and charterers, full implementation of Ship Security Plans, and immediate reporting of any suspicious activity, interception, electronic interference or GNSS disruption to the DG Communication Centre. DGS Circular No. 09 of 2026 dated 28.02.2026 – Urgent Advisory to Indian Seafarers and Shipping Stakeholders in view of Escalating Situation in Iran, requiring Indian seafarers in Iran to remain vigilant, register with the Embassy of India, coordinate for safe departure where feasible, and directing stakeholders to immediately provide details of Indian seafarers in affected areas. DGS Circular No. 21 of 2026 dated 07.04.2026 - issued a safety advisory for Indian seafarers ashore in Iran and onboard vessels operating in or around Iranian waters, directing them to remain vigilant, restrict unnecessary movement, follow advisories issued by the Embassy of India in Tehran, maintain contact with company representatives, and utilize DGS emergency support channels for assistance as required. DGS Circular No. 31 of 2026 dated 13.06.2026 – Precautionary Measures for Indian Seafarers in view of the Heightened Security Situation in the Gulf Region, reiterating heightened security vigilance, directing shipping companies and RPSL companies to restrict deployment of Indian seafarers to conflict areas until further orders (except emergency crew changes with consent), monitoring and reporting requirements, and dissemination of verified security information. DGS Circular No. 33 of 2026 dated 26.06.2026 – issued upon improvement in the situation, superseding the earlier restriction and permitting normal operations subject to caution and applicable coastal-State security protocols, and providing for a coordinated evacuation mechanism involving the International Maritime Organization (IMO), the United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO), the MICA Centre and coastal States. DGS Circular No. 36 of 2026 dated 15.07.2026 – issued upon renewed escalation, advising ship owners, ship managers and RPSL companies to avoid deploying Indian seafarers on vessels undertaking voyages involving passage through the Strait of Hormuz until further orders, together with heightened security vigilance and full compliance with the International Ship and Port Facility Security (ISPS) Code. Details of real-time reporting, tracking and monitoring mechanism for vessels and seafarers operating in the said region: The eNavik Portal, operationalised on 01.07.2026, provides an integrated digital platform with dedicated 24x7 Marine Casualty Reporting, Crisis Management and Seafarer Grievance Redressal modules, enabling digital reporting of marine casualties, security incidents and distress situations, automated routing of incident reports to the concerned authorities, and real-time tracking of response measures and case progression. An online Ship Reporting Form, has been instituted under DGS Circular No. 08 of 2024, through this all vessels transiting the Persian Gulf, the Strait of Hormuz, the Gulf of Oman, the Gulf of Aden, the Red Sea and adjacent waters submit their details, thereby maintaining a comprehensive and up-to-date vessel database which facilitates tracking and coordination and enables a swift response by the Indian Navy in the event of an incident. A requirement, under DGS Circular No. 08 of 2026, for the Company Security Officer to furnish to the DG Communication Centre the full particulars of the vessel together with the crew list. Continuous real-time monitoring is undertaken through the DG Communication Centre, which is manned round the clock, in close coordination with the Indian Navy, the Information Fusion Centre – Indian Ocean Region (IFC-IOR) and other competent authorities. A Situation Report is compiled and issued every 24 hours, which records, inter alia, the vessel-wise position and the number of Indian seafarers onboard each vessel in the region. The measures taken to ensure the safety, communication, evacuation and repatriation of Indian seafarers operating in the region are as follows: Communication: A dedicated 24-hour Control Room and the DG Communication Centre (MMDAC) function round the clock. A defined incident-communication protocol requires contact with the nearest Indian Naval or coalition warship on VHF Channel 16 and immediate intimation to the DG Communication Centre, the IFC-IOR and the UKMTO. Since activation, the Control Room has handled 15,771 telephone calls and 36,499 e-mails from seafarers, their families and maritime stakeholders. Navigational warnings and maritime security advisories are disseminated to stakeholders on a continuing basis. Evacuation and Repatriation: A total of 60 vessels have safely transited SoH carrying cargo for India. Further, 3,972 Indian seafarers have been repatriated from the Gulf region. Close and continuing contact is maintained with the families of seafarers, and dedicated welfare counsellor access has been provided wherever required. In cases of fatality, immediate financial support is facilitated, including release of Rs. 10,00,000 (Rupees Ten Lakh) through the Seafarers Welfare Fund Society. Steps taken to ensure no Indian Seafarer is compelled to sail without adequate information, protection and support: Regulated engagement. Every Indian seafarer is engaged through a licensed RPSL agency, and no seafarer can complete emigration clearance or sign-on formalities without formal and verified approvals. This provides an effective single point of control for the enforcement of deployment restrictions and for compliance monitoring. Consent in crew changes. Where a crew change in the conflict-affected area was permitted in a genuine emergency under DGS Circular No. 31 of 2026, it was expressly made subject to the consent of the seafarer concerned. Genuine emergency cases are considered only within the applicable legal and safety framework. Removal of compulsion at the systemic level. By advising against deployment on voyages through the Strait of Hormuz, the advisory removes, at the level of the system, any pressure upon an individual seafarer to accept a hazardous engagement. Disclosure and due diligence. RPSL companies and seafarers are expected to verify the intended route of the vessel, its flag, the reputation and welfare record of the owner or manager, the insurance position and any exposure to conflict-affected or high-risk waters before a contract is accepted. RPSL companies are further expected to provide clear information to seafarers regarding the nature of the voyage, the trading pattern and the likely exposure to high-risk areas. Grievance redressal and support. A comprehensive 24x7 grievance redressal mechanism is available through a domestic toll-free helpline (1800-889-7768), an international toll-free helpline for the United States of America (+1-888-988-0256), WhatsApp support (+91 8655856830), a dedicated e-mail address (enavik.24x7[at]gov[dot]in) and the e-Navik grievance portal, in addition to the DG Communication Centre. Verified information. Stakeholders have been advised to verify incident-related information through official Government sources and to refrain from circulating unverified reports which may prejudice the interests of seafarers and their families. This information was given by the Union Minister of Ports, Shipping and Waterways, Sarbananda Sonowal, in a written reply to the Rajya Sabha. *** MI/Indu (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2294247) आगंतुक पटल  : 231 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: हिन्दी Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways ‘SEAFARER-FIRST’ INITIATIVE प्रविष्टि तिथि:

ministry: Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways
title: DEVELOPMENT AND MODERNISATION OF PORTS IN MAHARASHTRA
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways DEVELOPMENT AND MODERNISATION OF PORTS IN MAHARASHTRA प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                04 AUG 2026 3:36PM by PIB Delhi The Government has assessed the requirement of a deep-draft port considering the projected growth in India's cargo and container traffic, particularly on the western coast. The Deep –draft Port, officially known as Vadhavan Port, is being developed as an all-weather greenfield deep-draft major port in Palghar district. The project was approved by the Union Cabinet on 19.06.2024 at an estimated cost of ₹76,220 crore. Upon completion, the port is expected to create a total cargo handling capacity of 298 million metric tonnes per annum. Vadhavan Port is expected to significantly improve Maharashtra's maritime infrastructure, trade competitiveness, logistics efficiency, industrial development and employment generation. The details of modernisation and connectivity projects undertaken for the development of Vadhavan port are at Annexure-I. title: BRICS-TCA Symposium and JMC Meeting Convenes under the Guidance of MSDE, Government of India
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship BRICS-TCA Symposium and JMC Meeting Convenes under the Guidance of MSDE, Government of India Two-day BRICS-TCA meeting examined digital, green and demographic shifts affecting skills and workforce needs India placed proposals for a BRICS International Skill Gap Study, BRICS Skills Competition and Compendium of Good Practices before the JMC प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                04 AUG 2026 7:10PM by PIB Delhi The BRICS Technical and Vocational Education and Training Cooperation Alliance (BRICS-TCA) Research Symposium and Joint Management Committee (JMC) Meeting was held during August 3 - 4, 2026, at Kaushal Bhawan, New Delhi. The event was held under the theme "Sustainable and Digitally Enabled TVET: The BRICS Perspective", the two-day meeting brought together representatives from BRICS countries, international organisations, academia, industry and training institutions. The event was convened by National Skill Development Corporation (NSDC), under the guidance of the Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE), Government of India. Smt. Debashree Mukherjee, Secretary, MSDE, said, “Skills are no longer merely a social intervention; they are critical economic infrastructure that shapes productivity, industrial competitiveness and workforce resilience. As BRICS nations, representing over 40 per cent of the world’s population, we have both the opportunity and the responsibility to build agile, inclusive and future-ready skilling systems. Through deeper cooperation in labour-market intelligence, institutional strengthening, joint research and emerging areas such as AI and green technologies, BRICS-TCA can help translate our collective demographic strength into shared prosperity and a more resilient global workforce.” Shri. Anandrao V. Patil, Additional Secretary, Ministry of Education, emphasised lifelong learning, stating, “A degree can no longer mark the end of learning. Education systems must allow learners to move flexibly between classrooms, workplaces and digital platforms throughout their lives. India’s National Education Policy 2020 supports this through multidisciplinary education, credit portability and the integration of vocational and higher education. BRICS cooperation can carry this forward through joint curricula, institutional exchanges and wider recognition of qualifications and micro-credentials.” Shri. Rajiv Bodwade, Joint Secretary (MER-III), Ministry of External Affairs, underscored the importance of skill diplomacy, stating, “Under India’s BRICS Chairship, skills cooperation must translate our shared demographic and economic strengths into practical, people-centric outcomes. A stronger focus on skills diplomacy can support orderly mobility, credible certification and closer institutional coordination across member countries. India remains ready to share its experience in migration partnerships, digital skilling platforms and transparent mobility systems to advance secure and mutually beneficial workforce pathways across the Global South.” Shri. Arunkumar Pillai, Chief Executive Officer, NSDC, and Rotating Chair, BRICS-TCA, highlighted the need for practical cooperation, stating, “BRICS is navigating three transitions at once: digital, green and demographic. By 2030, 86 per cent of employers expect AI and information-processing technologies to transform business, while 39 per cent of workers’ core skills are likely to change. Renewable energy already supports 16.6 million jobs globally. At the same time, some member countries have expanding young workforces, while others face structural labour shortages. The opportunity is significant, but the real challenge is trust and recognition across skills systems. Comparable qualifications, verifiable digital credentials and common standards can turn this demographic strength into mobility, opportunity and shared growth.” The inaugural session was chaired by Smt. Debashree Mukherjee, Secretary, Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship; Shri. Dilip Kumar, Director General, Directorate General of Training; Shri. Anandrao V. Patil, Additional Secretary, Ministry of Education; Shri. Niranjan Kumar Sudhansu, Additional Secretary, Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship; Smt. Manisha Sensarma, Senior Economic Advisor, Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship; Shri. Rajiv Bodwade, Joint Secretary (MER-III), Ministry of External Affairs; and Shri. Arunkumar Pillai, Rotating Chair, BRICS-TCA and Chief Executive Officer, National Skill Development Corporation. The inaugural session was followed by a plenary session where the BRICS member countries such as Brazil, Russia, China, UAE, Iran and India presented their country's flagship initiatives on vocational education and skill development. After the plenary session, there were two panel discussions, on ‘Green Skills Development and Financing Mechanisms for Sustainability Initiatives’ and ‘Digital Transformation and AI, VR and AR for TVET’. The Joint Management Committee (JMC) meeting on August 4 considered the synopsis of deliberations of the Research Symposium and received input from member countries on future priorities. Under India’s Chairship, three proposals were discussed. First, a framework of international skill gap study for BRICS was discussed to identify the gaps in emerging occupations and workforce shortages; second, a BRICS skills competition will be conducted to promote vocational excellence and a shared understanding of competence; and third, a compendium of good practices in TVET will be developed covering industry partnerships, digital learning, qualifications, and financing mechanism. Representatives from the Ministry of New and Renewable Energy, the World Bank, International Labour Organization, UNESCO, Universities and industry including Sector Skill Councils (SSCs), also participated in the deliberations. *** SH (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2294515) आगंतुक पटल  : 76 Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship BRICS-TCA Symposium and JMC Meeting Convenes under the Guidance of MSDE, Government of India Two-day BRICS-TCA meeting examined digital, green and demographic shifts affecting skills and workforce needs India placed proposals for a BRICS International Skill Gap Study, BRICS Skills Competition and Compendium of Good Practices before the JMC प्रविष्टि तिथि:

title: Empowering Rural Dairy Entrepreneurship: How VCF-SC Enabled a Scheduled Caste Entrepreneur to Build a Successful Dairy and Milk Processing Enterprise
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment Empowering Rural Dairy Entrepreneurship: How VCF-SC Enabled a Scheduled Caste Entrepreneur to Build a Successful Dairy and Milk Processing Enterprise Bhopal, Madhya Pradesh | Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                04 AUG 2026 7:09PM by PIB Delhi Entrepreneurship, when supported with timely financial assistance and institutional backing, has the potential to transform local businesses into sustainable enterprises that generate employment and contribute to regional economic development. One such inspiring example is CR Infrabuild Private Limited , a company based in Bhopal, Madhya Pradesh , promoted by Mr. Govind Kahare , a Scheduled Caste entrepreneur. His entrepreneurial journey reflects the transformative impact of the Venture Capital Fund for Scheduled Castes (VCF-SC) under the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment. CR Infrabuild Private Limited established a Dairy and Milk Processing Unit with the objective of enhancing value addition in dairy products, expanding market access, increasing revenue and creating sustainable employment opportunities. Recognising the project's growth potential, the Venture Capital Fund for Scheduled Castes extended financial assistance of ₹ 1.26 crore in 2021 through venture capital assistance comprising equity and optionally convertible debentures. The financial support enabled the company to strengthen its production capacity, expand operations and enhance its market presence across the region. Dairy and Milk Processing Unit The financial assistance enabled the enterprise to expand its dairy processing operations, increase production capacity and establish a stronger market network. Today, the company has expanded its business across the entire state of Madhya Pradesh and has also started supplying its products to several parts of Uttar Pradesh . The enterprise has achieved an annual turnover of approximately ₹ 7 crore , while simultaneously creating additional employment opportunities and strengthening the rural dairy value chain. The impact of the intervention has been significant. Employment has increased from 10 to 30 , including 10 Scheduled Caste/Backward Class employees and 20 non-SC/BC employees . The company's asset base has grown from ₹ 1 crore before sanction to approximately ₹ 2.56 crore , reflecting sustained business growth and enhanced operational capacity. Mr. Govind Kahare, Promoter Reflecting on the journey, Mr. Govind Kahare said: "The support received under the Venture Capital Fund for Scheduled Castes (VCF-SC), Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, helped us strengthen our enterprise and establish a strong identity in the dairy sector. The financial assistance enabled us to expand our business across Madhya Pradesh and into Uttar Pradesh, increase employment opportunities and achieve significant business growth. More importantly, it has enhanced the confidence and image of Scheduled Caste entrepreneurs and inspired the younger generation to pursue entrepreneurship." The success of CR Infrabuild Private Limited demonstrates how targeted financial support under the Venture Capital Fund for Scheduled Castes is enabling Scheduled Caste entrepreneurs to establish competitive enterprises, create employment opportunities and contribute to India's inclusive economic growth. By promoting entrepreneurship in sectors such as dairy and food processing, the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment continues to empower job creators, strengthen rural livelihoods and build a more self-reliant and inclusive economy. title: Strengthening Rural Agriculture Through Modern Cold Storage: How VCF-SC Enabled Meenakshidevi Hi-Tech Agro Industry Pvt. Ltd. to Empower Farmers and Create Sustainable Livelihoods
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment Strengthening Rural Agriculture Through Modern Cold Storage: How VCF-SC Enabled Meenakshidevi Hi-Tech Agro Industry Pvt. Ltd. to Empower Farmers and Create Sustainable Livelihoods प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                04 AUG 2026 7:09PM by PIB Delhi Agriculture is the backbone of India's rural economy, but inadequate post-harvest infrastructure often results in significant losses for farmers and limits their income. Modern cold storage facilities play a crucial role in preserving agricultural produce, improving its quality and extending its shelf life, thereby ensuring better market value for farmers. Demonstrating how timely institutional support can transform rural enterprises, Meenakshidevi Hi-Tech Agro Industry Pvt. Ltd. , promoted by Ms. A. Amutha Devi , has emerged as an important contributor to agricultural infrastructure in Tiruchirappalli, Tamil Nadu, through the establishment of a modern cold storage facility. Recognising the project's potential to strengthen the agricultural value chain and generate rural employment, the Venture Capital Fund for Scheduled Castes (VCF-SC) under the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment extended financial assistance of ₹ 4.95 crore in 2017 through Venture Capital assistance comprising Equity and Optionally Convertible Debentures. The financial support enabled the company to establish a 5,000 MTPA cold storage unit consisting of five chambers of 1,000 MT each , significantly enhancing post-harvest storage capacity in the region. Modern Cold Storage Infrastructure for Agricultural Growth The project has enabled the optimum utilisation of resources while ensuring better quality and longer shelf life of agricultural produce. By providing reliable storage infrastructure, the enterprise has empowered farmers to secure remunerative prices for their produce instead of resorting to distress sales. The initiative has also generated employment opportunities in rural areas, particularly for people belonging to weaker sections, thereby contributing to inclusive rural development. Reflecting on the journey, Ms. A. Amutha Devi said: "The support received under the Venture Capital Fund for Scheduled Castes (VCF-SC), Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, has helped us establish a modern cold storage facility that benefits farmers and rural communities. The project has improved the living standards of the promoter as well as the workers, particularly those belonging to the Scheduled Caste community, while contributing to sustainable agricultural development." The success of Meenakshidevi Hi-Tech Agro Industry Pvt. Ltd. demonstrates how targeted financial assistance under the Venture Capital Fund for Scheduled Castes (VCF-SC) is enabling Scheduled Caste entrepreneurs to establish sustainable enterprises that strengthen agricultural infrastructure, generate rural employment and improve farmers' incomes. By promoting entrepreneurship and supporting infrastructure development, the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment continues to empower entrepreneurs, create livelihoods and build sustainable futures across the country. ***** SS-11-TAR-KV-GA (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2294513) आगंतुक पटल  : 41 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: हिन्दी Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment Strengthening Rural Agriculture Through Modern Cold Storage: How VCF-SC Enabled Meenakshidevi Hi-Tech Agro Industry Pvt. title: Over 2.65 Lakh Scheduled Caste Beneficiaries Covered Under Education Domain in 17,067 PM-AJAY Adarsh Gram Villages
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment Over 2.65 Lakh Scheduled Caste Beneficiaries Covered Under Education Domain in 17,067 PM-AJAY Adarsh Gram Villages 90 Hostels Sanctioned During Last 05 Five Years, ₹198.50 Crore Released for Construction of SC Hostels: Dr. Virendra Kumar प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                04 AUG 2026 7:08PM by PIB Delhi The Central Government is implementing the Pradhan Mantri Anusuchit Jaati Abhyuday Yojana (PM-AJAY) to promote the educational and socio-economic development of Scheduled Caste (SC) communities through targeted interventions under its Adarsh Gram , Grants-in-Aid , and Construction/Repair of Hostels components. The scheme seeks to improve educational outcomes, strengthen infrastructure, and provide better access to quality residential facilities for Scheduled Caste students. Union Minister of Social Justice and Empowerment Dr. Virendra Kumar , in a reply to question by Shri Rao Rajendra Singh in Lok Sabha today, informed the House that under the Adarsh Gram Component , development is being undertaken across 10 domains comprising 50 socio-economic indicators , including education. He added that as on 29 July 2026 , a total of 17,067 villages have been declared Adarsh Gram , where 2,65,509 beneficiaries have been covered under the education domain. The Minister further informed that under the Hostel Component of PM-AJAY, the Department provides central assistance to States, Union Territories, Central Universities and Institutes for constructing new hostel buildings for Scheduled Caste students. The initiative aims to increase literacy, encourage enrolment in schools and higher educational institutions, and provide adequate residential facilities, particularly in aspirational districts, SC-dominated blocks and other parts of the country. During the last five financial years ( FY 2021-22 to FY 2025-26 ), 90 hostels have been sanctioned under the scheme, benefiting 10,649 Scheduled Caste students . An amount of ₹ 198.50 crore has been released to States and Union Territories for the construction of Scheduled Caste hostels during the same period. The House was also informed that the PM-AJAY Guidelines provide for enhanced quality, safety and accessibility in hostels. These include round-the-clock deployment of lady wardens and security personnel in girls' hostels, provision of in-house coaching, medical care, health camps, IT education, sports coaching and barrier-free access for students with disabilities. The initiative aims to increase literacy, encourage enrolment in schools and higher educational institutions, and provide adequate residential facilities, particularly in aspirational districts, SC-dominated blocks and other parts of the country. During the last five financial years ( FY 2021-22 to FY 2025-26 ), 90 hostels have been sanctioned under the scheme, benefiting 10,649 Scheduled Caste students . An amount of ₹ 198.50 crore has been released to States and Union Territories for the construction of Scheduled Caste hostels during the same period. The House was also informed that the PM-AJAY Guidelines provide for enhanced quality, safety and accessibility in hostels. These include round-the-clock deployment of lady wardens and security personnel in girls' hostels, provision of in-house coaching, medical care, health camps, IT education, sports coaching and barrier-free access for students with disabilities. title: Government Strengthens Post-Matric Scholarship Scheme to Boost Higher Education Among Scheduled Caste Students
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment Government Strengthens Post-Matric Scholarship Scheme to Boost Higher Education Among Scheduled Caste Students Revised Funding Pattern, Direct Benefit Transfer and End-to-End Online Processing Ensure Greater Transparency and Timely Scholarship Delivery प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                04 AUG 2026 7:07PM by PIB Delhi The Central Government is implementing the Post-Matric Scholarship (PMS) Scheme for Scheduled Caste (SC) students with the objective of significantly increasing the Gross Enrolment Ratio (GER) of SC students in higher education, particularly those belonging to the poorest households. The scheme provides financial assistance at the post-matriculation and post-secondary levels, enabling eligible Scheduled Caste students to pursue and complete their education. Minister of State for Social Justice and Empowerment Shri Ramdas Athawale , in a written reply to Shri Golla Baburao in Rajya Sabha , informed the House that the Post-Matric Scholarship Scheme has been implemented continuously in the State of Andhra Pradesh since 2020-21. Scholarships have been disbursed to eligible applicants across all districts of the State. According to the latest available data, Andhra Pradesh received Central Assistance of ₹ 149.03 crore , benefiting 81,667 students during 2026-27 (up to 24 July 2026) . The Minister further informed that the funding pattern of the scheme was revised in 2020-21 , replacing the earlier concept of State Committed Liability with a fixed Centre-State sharing ratio of 60:40 , while the ratio for North-Eastern States has been fixed at 90:10 . The revised funding pattern has reduced the financial burden on States and enhanced the Central Government's contribution towards the scheme. The House was also informed that several transformative reforms have been introduced under the scheme to improve efficiency, transparency and accountability. These include end-to-end online processing of applications, digital verification of eligibility through linkage with available databases, faster verification, continuous monitoring, prevention of duplication and timely delivery of scholarship benefits . Further, the Government introduced Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) under the scheme from 2021-22 , ensuring that scholarship amounts are transferred directly into the Aadhaar-seeded bank accounts of eligible students. The initiative has simplified the flow of funds, improved transparency and ensured accurate targeting of beneficiaries. Applications are invited through the designated State scholarship portals or the National Scholarship Portal, while the release of the Central share is contingent upon the timely release of the corresponding State share. The Minister also informed that delays in verification of applications by States and delays in the release of the State share can consequently delay the release of the Central assistance to eligible beneficiaries. title: Government Strengthens Scholarship Delivery Through DBT; Over 47.53 Lakh Post-Matric and 26.79 Lakh Pre-Matric Scholarships Awarded in 2025-26
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment Government Strengthens Scholarship Delivery Through DBT; Over 47.53 Lakh Post-Matric and 26.79 Lakh Pre-Matric Scholarships Awarded in 2025-26 प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                04 AUG 2026 7:04PM by PIB Delhi The Central Government is implementing the Post-Matric Scholarship (PMS) for Scheduled Castes and Pre-Matric Scholarship for Scheduled Castes & Others as Centrally Sponsored Schemes to promote educational empowerment of Scheduled Caste students across the country. The schemes are implemented through State Governments and Union Territory Administrations in Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) mode, ensuring timely, transparent and efficient disbursement of scholarship benefits to eligible students. Minister of State for Social Justice and Empowerment Shri Ramdas Athawale shared these details in a written reply to Shri Kota Srinivasa Poojary, Shri Tejasvi Sury, Shri Jaswantsinh Sumanbhai Bhabhor, Shri Pradeep Kumar Singh, Shri Bharatsinhji Shankarji Dabhi, Shri Yogender Chandolia, Smt. Kamlesh Jangde, Shri Ramesh Awasthi, Shri Captain Brijesh Chowta, Shri Radheshyam Rathiya, Shri Suresh Kumar Kashyap, Shri Janardan Mishra, Shri Naba Charan Majh, Shri Trivendra Singh Rawat, Shri Avimanyu Sethi, Shri Bibhu Prasad Tarai, Shri Chavda Vinod Lakhamshi and Shri Khagen Murmu . The House was informed that both scholarship schemes are open-ended and demand-driven , enabling all eligible students enrolled in recognised educational institutions across India to avail scholarship benefits. Annual Action Plans are received from States and Union Territories in accordance with the scheme guidelines. The written reply further stated that the Post-Matric Scholarship Scheme follows a funding pattern of 60:40 between the Centre and States and 90:10 for North-Eastern States , while the Pre-Matric Scholarship Scheme follows a 60:40 funding pattern , 90:10 for North-Eastern States, Uttarakhand and Himachal Pradesh , and 100 per cent Central funding for Union Territories without legislatures . The House was also informed that the Government has introduced several reforms to enhance transparency, accountability and continuous monitoring of the scholarship schemes. Through Aadhaar-enabled Direct Benefit Transfer, scholarship amounts are credited directly into beneficiaries' bank accounts, eliminating leakages, ensuring accurate targeting and enabling faster flow of funds. Applications are processed through designated State Scholarship Portals and the National Scholarship Portal, while verification and approval are undertaken by the respective State Governments and Union Territories as per the scheme guidelines. According to the data shared in Parliament, during 2025-26 , the Post-Matric Scholarship Scheme benefited 47,53,420 students across the country, while the Pre-Matric Scholarship Scheme benefited 26,79,049 students , reaffirming the Government's continued commitment towards expanding educational opportunities for Scheduled Caste students. The reply further provided district-wise information for Dakshina Kannada (Karnataka), Dahod (Gujarat) and Shimla (Himachal Pradesh) . Between 2022-23 and 2025-26 , the Post-Matric Scholarship Scheme covered 29,184 beneficiaries with Central Assistance amounting to ₹ 35.91 crore , while the Pre-Matric Scholarship Scheme covered 34,184 beneficiaries with Central Assistance of ₹ 8.15 crore across these districts. ***** PR-051-TAR-KV/GA (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2294509) आगंतुक पटल  : 40 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: Urdu , हिन्दी Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment Government Strengthens Scholarship Delivery Through DBT; Over 47.53 Lakh Post-Matric and 26.79 Lakh Pre-Matric Scholarships Awarded in 2025-26 प्रविष्टि तिथि:

title: RASHTRIYA VAYOSHRI SCHEME AND DEENDAYAL DISABLED REHABILITATION SCHEME
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment RASHTRIYA VAYOSHRI SCHEME AND DEENDAYAL DISABLED REHABILITATION SCHEME प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                04 AUG 2026 4:19PM by PIB Delhi A third-party impact evaluation of the Rashtriya Vayoshri Yojana (RVY) and the Deendayal Divyangjan Rehabilitation Scheme (DDRS) has been conducted for their appraisal. The evaluation study has reported that RVY is exceptionally well aligned with the needs of eligible senior citizens. The Scheme has had a transformative impact on the mobility and functional independence of beneficiaries by providing assistive devices that enable them to walk independently and move around without assistance. It is particularly effective in promoting independent living and reducing reliance on caregivers for basic mobility and daily functioning. The evaluation study of DDRS indicates that the Scheme has delivered significant outcomes in education, rehabilitation, assistive support, and livelihood inclusion. It highlights the provision of educational and therapeutic services, leading to substantial functional improvement, along with the distribution of free assistive devices that have demonstrated high usability and beneficiary satisfaction. The evaluation also notes improved livelihood linkages, strong community and parental engagement, and enhanced transparency and timeliness through the e-Anudaan digital platform. Overall, the findings reflect high beneficiary satisfaction, improved social inclusion, and an enhanced quality of life. This information is given by the Minister of State for Social Justice and Empowerment, Shri Ramdas Athawale, in a written reply in the Lok Sabha today. ***** KV/HK (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2294289) आगंतुक पटल  : 163 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: Urdu , हिन्दी , Gujarati Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment RASHTRIYA VAYOSHRI SCHEME AND DEENDAYAL DISABLED REHABILITATION SCHEME प्रविष्टि तिथि:

title: Meeting of Heads of National Statistical Offices of BRICS Countries
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Statistics & Programme Implementation Meeting of Heads of National Statistical Offices of BRICS Countries “Quality Statistics as Driver of Change” प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                04 AUG 2026 4:38PM by PIB Delhi The two-day meeting of Heads of National Statistical Offices (NSO) of BRICS Member Countries was concluded on 4th August 2026, at Lucknow, Uttar Pradesh, India under the theme "Quality Statistics as a Driver of Change" aligned with the overarching BRICS theme, "Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability" . The event brought together more than 350 participants including representatives from National Statistical Offices of BRICS, policy makers, academia, think-tanks, civil society organisation and technical experts. During the 2 nd day, the main technical Session-III on ‘Identifying Common Innovation Areas for Potential BRICS Collaboration’ included two presentations on the theme of Modern Survey Methods & Digital Data Collection were made. India and Egypt shared their experiences in using digital platforms for collection of survey and census data. India presented the experience and lessons learnt during the shift from Paper based survey to modern survey tools like e-SIGMA (e-Survey Information Gathering and Management Application) that is a Computer Assisted Personal Interview (CAPI) enabled platform, designed to integrate large-scale sample surveys into a cloud-based architecture. Egypt highlighted the use of geospatial technology in producing their official statistics. The importance of use of AI in survey implementations and more use of administrative data in a nuanced manner in conjunction with survey data was also emphasised. Technical Session IV focused on strengthening macroeconomic and sectoral statistics, highlighting key strategies and progress made by BRICS member countries in strengthening macro-economic statistics. India presented its transition roadmap for implementing the System of National Accounts, 2025 (2025 SNA) and demonstrated effective use of administrative data in official statistics. China shared its progress and early practical experiences in introducing the 2025 SNA framework. Meanwhile, Brazil showcased the integration of alternative data sources particularly publicly available online data from expanding e-commerce and intermediary platforms emphasizing that non-traditional data can complement existing sources to significantly enhance quality of statistics produced by member countries in a rapidly changing technological landscape. Indonesia also presented its implementation plan to transition to 2025 SNA while also highlighting the adoption of ISIC 5 by them. Along side the Meeting of Heads of National Statistical Offices of BRICS Countries 2026, the Ministry, in collaboration with the Janaagraha Centre for Citizenship and Democracy, organized the side event titled "Building AI-Ready Public Data Systems in the Evolving Data Ecosystem". The discussions emphasized the importance of interoperable, trusted, and high-quality public data systems in enabling responsible AI adoption and supporting evidence-based governance. This side event featured a moderated roundtable discussion on the practical building blocks for AI-ready public data systems, followed by country case studies from India, South Africa, Russia, Indonesia, China, the UAE, and other partner organizations. Participants shared experiences on strengthening data governance, interoperability, metadata standards, institutional collaboration, and capacity building to transform fragmented data systems into AI-ready ecosystems. The deliberations highlighted the importance of international cooperation, knowledge exchange, and the adoption of best practices to build resilient public data systems that can effectively harness the potential of artificial intelligence for public good. On the sidelines of the Meeting of Heads of National Statistical Offices (NSOs), the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI), Government of India, and BPS–Statistics Indonesia signed a Letter of Intent (LoI) during a bilateral meeting to strengthen cooperation in official statistics, capacity building, and strategic collaboration. The LoI provides a framework for collaboration in areas such as knowledge exchange, technological and methodological advancement, human resource development, and emerging areas including AI, metadata standardization, and open data. The session concluded with adoption of the BRICS Joint Statement followed by concluding remarks session. The formal adoption of the Joint Statement marks a significant milestone in strengthening statistical frameworks across BRICS member countries, laying the groundwork for more robust, transparent, and policy-relevant official statistics. The Joint Statement may be accessed at https://www.mospi.gov.in/uploads/latestReleases/latest_release_1785840278403_a094383d-aeca-4106-a3d4-02fd91a2686e_Joint_statement_for_Meeting_of_Heads_of_NSOs.pdf . ********** Samrat/Dileep/Sundaram (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2294324) आगंतुक पटल  : 224 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: Urdu , हिन्दी Ministry of Statistics & Programme Implementation Meeting of Heads of National Statistical Offices of BRICS Countries “Quality Statistics as Driver of Change” प्रविष्टि तिथि:

title: President of India to present Handloom Awards 2025 on Aug 7, National Handloom Day, recognising outstanding achievement in India's Handloom Sector
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Textiles President of India to present Handloom Awards 2025 on Aug 7, National Handloom Day, recognising outstanding achievement in India's Handloom Sector प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                04 AUG 2026 6:53PM by PIB Delhi The President of India will present the prestigious Handloom Awards during the National Handloom Day celebrations on 7 August 2026 . The function will be attended by the Union Minister of Textiles, Shri Giriraj Singh, senior dignitaries, representatives of the handloom industry, master weavers, designers, exporters, artisans, and other distinguished guests. A total of 22 awardees, comprising 3 Sant Kabir Handloom Awardees and 19 National Handloom Awardees , will be honoured for their exceptional contribution towards preserving, promoting and advancing India's rich handloom traditions. (List of Sant Kabir and National Handloom Awardees for 2025) Celebrating Excellence in Handloom The Ministry of Textiles has announced the recipients of the Sant Kabir Handloom Awards and National Handloom Awards 2025 , acknowledging outstanding excellence in weaving, innovation, design development, marketing initiatives, start-up ventures and producer companies associated with the handloom sector. The awards are instituted under the Handloom Marketing Assistance (HMA) component of the National Handloom Development Programme (NHDP) and represent the highest national recognition for excellence in the handloom ecosystem. The awards will be presented during the National Handloom Day celebrations to honour individuals and organisations whose work has significantly strengthened India's handloom heritage and enhanced its competitiveness in domestic and international markets. The event is expected to witness participation from Members of Parliament, senior government officials, industry experts, academic institutions, exporters, designers and handloom weavers from across the country. Handloom Awards The Handloom Awards are intended to encourage excellence, innovation and sustained commitment in the handloom sector. They recognise outstanding craftsmanship, adoption of modern techniques while preserving traditional skills, product diversification, design innovation and contributions towards the socio-economic development of weaving communities. Sant Kabir Handloom Award The award is the country's highest recognition for handloom weavers who have demonstrated extraordinary craftsmanship and lifelong dedication to the preservation and promotion of India's weaving traditions. Recipients are selected based on exceptional technical skill, innovation, sustained contribution to the sector, promotion of traditional weaving practices, mentoring of artisans and efforts towards community development. The award comprises of:- Gold Coin (Mounted) Tamrapatra Shawl Certificate National Handloom Award The National Handloom Award honours handloom weavers and other stakeholders who have displayed outstanding creativity, quality, innovation and excellence in their respective fields. The award seeks to inspire artisans and institutions to continuously raise standards in craftsmanship, product development and market outreach while preserving India's diverse handloom traditions. The award comprises of :- Tamrapatra Shawl Certificate Selection Process Awardees in the weaving category are selected through a rigorous multi-level evaluation process involving Zonal, Headquarters and Central Level Selection Committees. These committees comprise experienced professionals, technical experts and senior government officials who assess nominations against prescribed eligibility criteria and evaluation parameters. For categories relating to design development, marketing, start-up ventures and producer companies, nominations undergo a structured evaluation by the Headquarters Committee and the Central Level Committee before final approval. The selection mechanism ensures transparency, objectivity and recognition of genuine excellence across all segments of the handloom sector. The award comprises of:- Gold Coin (Mounted) Tamrapatra Shawl Certificate National Handloom Award The National Handloom Award honours handloom weavers and other stakeholders who have displayed outstanding creativity, quality, innovation and excellence in their respective fields. The award seeks to inspire artisans and institutions to continuously raise standards in craftsmanship, product development and market outreach while preserving India's diverse handloom traditions. The award comprises of :- Tamrapatra Shawl Certificate Selection Process Awardees in the weaving category are selected through a rigorous multi-level evaluation process involving Zonal, Headquarters and Central Level Selection Committees. These committees comprise experienced professionals, technical experts and senior government officials who assess nominations against prescribed eligibility criteria and evaluation parameters. For categories relating to design development, marketing, start-up ventures and producer companies, nominations undergo a structured evaluation by the Headquarters Committee and the Central Level Committee before final approval. The selection mechanism ensures transparency, objectivity and recognition of genuine excellence across all segments of the handloom sector. title: GRANTS TO STARTUPS IN TECHNICAL TEXTILES
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Textiles GRANTS TO STARTUPS IN TECHNICAL TEXTILES प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                04 AUG 2026 1:42PM by PIB Delhi Under the the Ministry of Textile's National Technical Textiles Mission (NTTM), the scheme of "Grant for Research and Entrepreneurship across Aspiring Innovators in Technical Textiles (GREAT)" aims to support the start-up ecosystem in the technical textiles sector by providing assistance to young innovators, scientists, technologists, and start-up ventures in translating their ideas into commercial technologies and products. The total budget allocated to the NTTM for the current financial year (2026-27) is Rs. 256 crore, which includes the provision for releasing grants to start-ups under the GREAT scheme. An Evaluation and Monitoring Committee (EMC) has been constituted under NTTM to evaluate, monitor, and review the technical and financial parameters of the start-up proposals. Based on the criteria laid out in the GREAT guidelines, the EMC submits its recommendations to the Empowered Programme Committee (EPC) under NTTM for approval of start-up proposals. GREAT guidelines are available at https://nttm.texmin.gov.in/. The grants provided to start-ups under NTTM are aimed at promoting innovation, commercialization of indigenous technologies, and the development of value-added technical textile products. The anticipated economic impact of these grants is fundamentally driven by robust collaborations between the supported start-ups and established industry partners. By fostering strong synergies between innovators and industry stakeholders for prototype development, field trials, and market launches, the scheme ensures market-ready commercialization. This active industry engagement is anticipated to successfully scale these start-ups, significantly strengthen the overall technical textiles ecosystem in the country, and thereby catalyze broader sustainable industry growth and employment generation. Under NTTM, a total of 31 start-ups have been approved at a total cost of Rs 15.40 crore, of which Rs 13.65 crore is the Government of India share, details of which are given below. A Review and Monitoring Committee has been constituted to assess and oversee the progress of the approved start-ups, with the authority to recommend for release of subsequent instalments of grant and closure of projects to the Empowered Programme Committee under NTTM. Further, various public events, workshops, seminars and outreach activities are being organized nationwide to disseminate information about the scheme and facilitate industry engagement for scaling up the potential start-up projects. Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Textiles MISSION FOR COTTON PRODUCTIVITY प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                04 AUG 2026 1:41PM by PIB Delhi The Mission for Cotton Productivity (KAPAS KANTI) was approved by the Government on 5th May, 2026 with an overall outlay of Rs. 5,659.22 crore for a period of five years (2026-27 to 2030-31). Of this, Component-I(A) implemented by the Department of Agricultural Research and Education (DARE) has an outlay of Rs. 555.05 crore and Component-I(B) implemented by the Department of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare (DA&FW) has an outlay of Rs. 3,804.17 crore . Components-II and III, implemented by the Cotton Corporation of India and the National Jute Board under the administrative control of the Ministry of Textiles, have approved outlays of Rs. 1,000 crore and Rs. 300 crore, respectively. Under Component-I(A), an amount of approximately Rs. 11.50 crore has been approved for cotton productivity-related activities under the All India Coordinated Research Project (AICRP) at Raichur, Chamarajanagar and Dharwad in Karnataka. During 2026-27 , an amount of Rs. 4,850.13 lakh (Central Share: Rs. 2,910.08 lakh and State Share: Rs. 1,940.05 lakh) has been allocated to Karnataka under Component-I(B). The Government of Karnataka has earmarked Rs. 1,100.81 lakh for Raichur district under Component-I(B) during 2026-27 . Under Component-I(B), the Mission initially covers 140 potential districts across 14 major cotton-growing States. The selection of these districts has been based on their cotton-growing potential. The list of districts is indicative, and the States have flexibility to revise the districts covered based on their annual plans, requirements and/or performance. Raichur has been included as it is one of the major cotton-growing districts in Karnataka. The Government of Karnataka has informed the district-wise physical targets for upscaling of technologies through demonstrations, including targeted beneficiaries, under Component-I(B) of the Mission for 2026-27. The details are placed below. The mission envisages to increase the production to 40 lakh bales of cotton and enhance productivity to 860 kg lint/ha by 2030-31 for Karnataka. The year wise targets provided by State Government of Karnataka are placed below . The details are as follows: (i) Cotton Testing Laboratories: Under Component-II of the Mission, provision has been made for setting up 50 cotton testing laboratories in clusters of cotton-producing districts across the country. The Mission does not specify State-wise or district-wise allocation of these laboratories. Their allocation will be determined through the process prescribed under the scheme, including the Request for Proposal (RFP) for implementation in Public-Private Partnership (PPP) mode. (ii) Kasturi Cotton Bharat Traceability Facilities: The Mission provides for output-based incentives for production of Kasturi Cotton Bharat-certified cotton bales by eligible Ginning and Processing (G&P) factories. Eligible G&P factories, including those located in Karnataka, are eligible for consideration under the scheme, subject to its provisions. (iii) Ginning and Processing (G&P) Units: The Mission provides for output-based incentives to eligible G&P factories for production of Kasturi Cotton Bharat-certified cotton bales, in accordance with the provisions of the scheme. The Government of Karnataka has furnished the year-wise targets under the Mission, which are placed below. Implementation of Component-I(B) of the Mission is monitored through State Level Committees and District Level Committees constituted in accordance with the provisions of the Mission. The monitoring mechanism is applicable to all districts covered under the Mission, including Raichur. The Mission provides for monitoring against the year-wise targets furnished by the State Government. title: BHARAT TEX 2026
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Textiles BHARAT TEX 2026 प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                04 AUG 2026 1:41PM by PIB Delhi Bharat Tex 2026, organized by the Bharat Tex Trade Federation (BTTF) with the support of the Ministry of Textiles, has been conceived around the Hon'ble Prime Minister's 5F Vision of Farm to Fibre to Factory to Fashion to Foreign. Since its inception in the year 2024, Bharat Tex mirrored this value chain directly in its physical layout, with exhibition halls sequenced from fibres, yarns and raw materials through fabric and apparel manufacturing to finished, export-ready products, enabling buyers to engage with the complete textile value chain under a single unified platform. The Bharat Tex serves as a platform for facilitating Business-to-Business (B2B), Government-to-Government (G2G) and Business-to-Government (B2G) engagement among global and domestic stakeholders across the textile value chain. The event provides opportunities for manufacturers, exporters, artisan groups, handloom and handicraft clusters, MSMEs, global brands, retailers, sourcing companies and investors to interact through buyer-seller meetings, business networking sessions, country engagements and thematic discussions. Facilitated through the Export Promotion Councils (EPCs), regional weavers, handloom cooperatives and artisanal exporters engaged directly with international buyers through structured B2B matchmaking sessions, enabling traditional craft clusters to showcase their products to global sourcing and procurement teams. Indi Haat, organized alongside Bharat Tex 2026, further complemented these efforts by bringing together weavers and artisans from across the country, providing them with a dedicated platform to interact with domestic and international buyers and expand their market outreach. In addition, MSMEs, start-ups, and weavers from Champion and Aspirational Districts were invited to participate in the event, providing them exposure to the broader textile ecosystem, emerging market trends, technological innovations and networking opportunities with industry leaders, buyers and institutional stakeholders. Together, these initiatives sought to foster inclusive participation and create greater market access for stakeholders across different segments of the textile sector. The State of Chhattisgarh was provided a dedicated 100 sq. metre exhibition pavilion at Bharat Tex 2026. The pavilion showcased the State's rich textile and handicraft traditions, handloom products, regional clusters, industrial capabilities and investment opportunities before domestic and international buyers, global brands, industry leaders and investors. It also highlighted the State's efforts to promote traditional crafts alongside modern textile value chains. Bharat Tex 2026 featured a dedicated Eco-Stitch Sustainability & Circularity Hub, presented jointly by the Clothing Manufacturers Association of India (CMAI) and the Global Alliance for Textile Sustainability (GATS), under the theme “Sustainable, Circular and Competitive Bharat.” The Hub comprised six curated zone, the India Impact Wall, Circularity at Scale, From Waste to Global Wardrobe, Made in Circular Bharat, the Material & Innovation Library, and the Circular Bharat Forum, bringing together recyclers, manufacturers, brands, innovators and technology providers working on circular textile solutions. The Ministry is also promoting circularity and sustainability through 'Weave the Future', an initiative of the Office of the Development Commissioner (Handlooms), which facilitates collaboration among artisans, designers, industry, academic institutions, and innovators to encourage responsible production, resource efficiency, material innovation, and sustainable livelihoods. The initiative also promotes upcycling, recycling, repair, repurposing and circular design practices, thereby strengthening the competitiveness and sustainability of India's regional textile hubs. To further promote knowledge exchange and adoption of sustainable practices, 41 dedicated knowledge sessions were organized on themes such as circular economy, sustainable fibres and materials, textile recycling, ESG and sustainability reporting, traceability, responsible sourcing, decarbonisation, resource efficiency, water stewardship, digital product passports, climate resilience, green finance and emerging global sustainability regulations. Overseas buyer participation across the three editions of Bharat Tex held so far is given below: Edition Dates & Venue(s) Overseas/International Buyers Countries Represented Bharat Tex 2024 26th – 29th February 2024; Bharat Mandapam&Yashobhoomi, New Delhi Approx. 3,000 111 Bharat Tex 2025 14th – 17th February 2025; Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi & India Expo Centre & Mart, Greater Noida 4,335 126 Bharat Tex 2026 14th – 17th July 2026; Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi 6,090 (Including Buying Houses) 138 The Bharat Tex 2026 recorded the following key outcomes: 1,647 exhibiting companies (1,628 domestic and 19 international) across 65,000+ square metres of exhibition space, conducted over 29,000 structured B2B meetings. Additionally, over 40 MoUs signed across trade, investment, technology, sustainability and institutional collaboration, including a Letter of Intent between the Bharat Tex Trade Federation and Première Vision Paris. During Bharat Tex 2026, 22 new buyer markets were added to the buyer network, further expanding India's global sourcing footprint. The event also facilitated the onboarding of over 500 new Indian exporters through the participating EPCs, broadening the country's export base and enabling greater participation of Indian enterprises in international markets. Collectively, these outcomes strengthened Bharat Tex 2026 as a platform for promoting exports, fostering international business partnerships and enhancing the global visibility of the Indian textile and apparel industry. This information was provided by THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR TEXTILES SHRI PABITRA MARGHERITA in a written reply to a question in Lok Sabha today. **** MAM/VN (Lok Sabha US Q2620) (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2294192) आगंतुक पटल  : 328 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: Urdu , हिन्दी Ministry of Textiles BHARAT TEX 2026 प्रविष्टि तिथि:

ministry: Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports
title: Dr. Mansukh Mandaviya felicitates Commonwealth Games 2026 medallists in boxing, judo and para-athletics; calls on athletes to mentor the next generation
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports Dr. Mansukh Mandaviya felicitates Commonwealth Games 2026 medallists in boxing, judo and para-athletics; calls on athletes to mentor the next generation Dr. Mandaviya highlights ₹36,000 crore expanded Khelo India scheme; says investment will ensure sustained growth of Indian sports प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                04 AUG 2026 5:32PM by PIB Delhi New Delhi, August 4: Union Minister for Youth Affairs and Sports Dr Mansukh Mandaviya today felicitated Indian athletes who returned from the Commonwealth Games 2026 after delivering historic performances in boxing, judo and para-athletics. Congratulating the champions, Dr. Mandaviya urged them to extend their contribution to Indian sport beyond their competitive careers by mentoring and inspiring the next generation of athletes. The felicitation ceremony brought together members of the Indian boxing contingent, which topped the boxing medal tally with an impressive haul of 10 medals, including seven gold and three silver. The Union Sports Minister also honoured the judo contingent, which scripted India’s best-ever Commonwealth Games campaign in the discipline by securing four medals, including two historic golds, and the para-athletics contingent, whose outstanding performances in Glasgow marked a watershed moment for Indian para sport. The medal winners were presented cash awards of Rs 30 lakh for gold, Rs 20 lakh for silver and Rs 10 lakh for bronze. Interacting with the athletes, Dr. Mandaviya asked the athletes to think beyond their playing careers and become contributors to the next generation of Indian sport. With the revamped Khelo India scheme now backed by a Rs 36,000-crore investment, he encouraged the athletes to consider establishing sports academies and nurturing young talent after retirement. “Let us not just win a Commonwealth Games medal with the aim to bag a government job. I urge all of you to run sports academies once you retire from your active career,” Dr Mandaviya said, adding that the athletes’ mission should be “India first.” “While you were playing for the gold in Glasgow, we launched the expanded Khelo India scheme by investing a total of Rs. 36000 Crore, that will take care of greater continued investment in the growth of Indian sports in the coming years,” he added. content:
