                04 AUG 2026 6:56PM by PIB Delhi On the basis of the result of the written part of the Indian Economic Service/Indian Statistical Service Examination 2026 held by the UPSC from 19th June to 21st June, 2026, the candidates with the under mentioned Roll Numbers have qualified for Interview/Personality Test. The candidature of these candidates is PROVISIONAL subject to their being found eligible in all respects. The candidates would be required to produce the original certificates in support of their claims relating to age, educational qualifications, community, benchmark disability (where applicable) etc. at the time of the Personality Test. They are, therefore, advised to keep their certificates ready and check beforehand the requirement of certificates in accordance with the important instructions available on the website of the Commission before appearing in the Personality Test. The Commission shall provide a window of 15 (Fifteen) days after the declaration of result of written part of Indian Economic Service/Indian Statistical Service (IES/ISS) Examination, 2026. All the candidates, as per Rule 4.1(2) of Rules of IES/ISS Examination, 2026, who qualified for the Personality Test/Interview shall be required to mandatorily login to the portal (https://upsconline.nic.in) during this period and shall be required to update their details/educational qualification status (whether appearing/appeared) alongwith proof of passing the requisite qualifying examination, and upload the relevant documents as proof of their claim, failing which, such candidates will not be allowed to participate in the further stages of this examination and no correspondence will be entertained by the Commission in this regard. In this period, all the candidates, who qualified for Personality Test shall also be provided an option to update the Correspondence/ Permanent Postal Address, Higher Educational Qualification, Achievement in different fields (if any), Employment Details/Service Experience, details of the Service allocated on the basis of earlier/previous Indian Economic Service/ Indian Statistical Service Examination (if any), Marital Status, PwBD Recommendation details in past, Parental details, Debarment information, earlier Examination details, OBC/EWS Annexure (wherever applicable), Socio-economic questionnaire, whichever is applicable and submit their Online Application Form. The candidates are advised to regularly visit the Commission’s website with regard to further updates. The instruction for updating the Application Form and Rules of the Indian Economic Service/Indian Statistical Service Examination, 2026, must be read carefully with regard to the certificates that will be produced at the time of Interview. The candidates will be solely responsible for not producing sufficient proof in support of his/her age, date of birth, educational qualification, community (SC/ST/OBC/EWS) and physical disability certificate (in the case of PwBD candidates). The schedule of the Personality Test (Interview) of candidates, who have qualified for the Personality Test, will be uploaded on the Commission’s website in due course of time. The exact date of interview will, however, be intimated to the candidates through e-Summon Letter. The candidates are requested to visit the Commission’s website (https://upsc.gov.in) for updates in this regard. No request for change in the date and time of Personality Test intimated to the candidates will ordinarily be entertained under any circumstances. The mark-sheet of candidates will be uploaded on the Commission's website after the publication of final result (i.e. after conducting Personality Test) and will remain available on the website for a period of 30 days. The candidates can access the marks-sheets after keying in their Roll Numbers and date of birth. The printed/hard copies of the marks-sheet would, however, be issued by the UPSC to candidates based on specific request accompanied by a self-addressed stamped envelope. Candidates desirous of obtaining printed/hard copies of the marks sheets should make the request within 30 days of the display of the marks on the Commission's website, beyond which such requests would not be entertained. The candidates may obtain any information/clarification regarding their issue(s) (if any) in respect of the above-mentioned Examination on Tel. No. 011-40303444/24041001 of the Commission’s Call Centre from 09:00 AM to 08:00 PM. content:

                04 AUG 2026 2:18PM by PIB Delhi Major common infrastructure facilities under implementation include water supply system, power infrastructure, Common Effluent Treatment Plant (CETP) with Zero Liquid Discharge (ZLD), steam generation system, warehouse, centre of excellence, solvent recovery system, emergency response centre and solid waste management facilities. The present status of physical and financial progress component-wise of the Himachal Pradesh Bulk Drug Park is as under : Sl. No. Common Infrastructure Facility Approved Cost (Rs. crore) Expenditure incurred (₹ in crore) Status 1 Common Effluent Treatment Plant (CETP), Solid Waste management 49.73 - Tender released. 2 Incinerator cost 18.00 - Tender under preparation 3 Cost of Collection & Landfill site 37.00 - Tender under preparation 4 Storm Water Drain Network 86.71 9.68 12% work completed 5 Common Solvent Storage System, Solvent Recovery & Distillation 30.00 - Tender under preparation 6 Common Warehouse 60.71 - Tender under preparation 7 Internal Power Distribution Network Within park 65.00 14.26 Tender under preparation 8 Internal Road network, Compound Wall 149.44 15.03 10% work completed 9 Raw, Potable and Demineralised Water 141.95 55.6 60% work completed 10 Steam generation and distribution system 312.30 - Tender released. 11 Advanced Laboratory Testing Centre 22.73 - Tender under preparation 12 Emergency Response Centre 20.17 - Tender under preparation 13 Safety / Hazardous Operations Audit Centre 14.43 - Tender under preparation 14 Centre of Excellence 110.29 - Tender under preparation Department of Pharmaceuticals (DoP), Government of India has sanctioned an amount of ₹ 1000 crore on 11.10.2022 for development of Bulk Drug Park in Haroli, District Una, Himachal Pradesh under the Scheme for ‘Promotion of Bulk Drug Parks’ and out of which an amount of ₹ 225 crore has been released on 20.02.2023. The State Government, has also sanctioned an amount of ₹118.46 crore and released an amount of ₹ 35.53 crore as state share in F.Y. 22-23 towards development of Common Infrastructure Facilities (CIF). O n the basis of representations received from the State Governments concerned, the status of projects, the level of fund utilisation and the anticipated completion of projects in FY2026–27, the tenure of the scheme has been extended up to FY2026-27. The review of the progress of the Bulk Drug Park being developed in Himachal Pradesh is regularly carried out by the Scheme Steering Committee of the scheme for “Promotion of Bulk Drug Park”, Secretary and Joint Secretary in the Department of Pharmaceuticals and by High Powered Committee headed by Hon’ble Minister of Industries, Himachal Pradesh. Primary reasons affecting delay is the grant of Environmental Clearance which has been granted on 25.09.2025, procedural requirement for permission for felling of trees and bids for procurement. The State Government and implementing agencies are closely monitoring project execution and expediting statutory clearances, tendering and award of contracts for critical infrastructure components. Following receipt of Environmental Clearance, project activities have gained momentum, and multiple infrastructure packages are under implementation or advanced stages of procurement to ensure timely completion and operationalization of the park. This information was given by Minister of State for Chemicals and Fertilizers, Smt. title: Support to pharmaceutical MSME clusters in Himachal Pradesh under SPI
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers : Department of Pharmaceuticals Support to pharmaceutical MSME clusters in Himachal Pradesh under SPI प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                04 AUG 2026 2:16PM by PIB Delhi Under a sub-scheme namely, Assistance to Pharmaceutical Industry for Common Facilities (APICF) of the umbrella Central Sector Scheme for Strengthening of Pharmaceuticals Industry (SPI) for strengthening the existing pharmaceutical cluster’s capacity for sustained growth by supporting creation of common infrastructure facilities. Under the sub-scheme, two projects viz M/s Welzo Research & Development Private Limited and M/s Himachal Pradesh Testing Lab Limited (HPTLL) located in the Solan District, Himachal Pradesh have been approved in the FY 2022-23 (with sanction Grant-in-aid of ₹19.53 crore) and FY 2025-26 (with sanction Grant-in-aid of ₹17.87 crore) respectively. Under the sub-scheme API-CF, no proposal from Himachal Pradesh is pending. One project viz M/s Welzo Research & Development Private Limited approved for establishing Research & Development and Testing Laboratory has been completed with central grant-in-aid of ₹5.86 crore released in FY 2022-23, ₹4.88 crore released in FY 2023-24, ₹6.84 crore released in FY 2024-25 and ₹1.95 crore released in FY 2025-26. Second project viz M/s Himachal Pradesh Testing Lab Limited (HPTLL) has been approved for establishing Common Facility Centre for Research & Development and centre of excellence for skill development. Pending the procedural requirement as per the sub-scheme from HPTLL, financial assistance has not been released yet. In addition to the above, under the sub-scheme namely Revamped Pharmaceutical Technology Upgradation Assistance Scheme (RPTUAS) of the umbrella Central Sector Scheme for Strengthening of Pharmaceuticals Industry (SPI) to facilitate technology and processes upgradation of existing pharmaceutical units to Revised Schedule-M and World Health Organization - Good Manufacturing Practices (WHO-GMP) certification , a total of 16 Pharmaceutical units with sanction amount of ₹17.19 crores and 27 Pharmaceutical units with sanction amount of ₹29.02 crores have been approved in the FY 2024-25 and FY 2025-26 respectively in Solan District, Himachal Pradesh. Out of the approved pharmaceutical units, incentive of ₹6.42 crore to seven pharmaceutical units have been released. Further, a total of 21 applications from pharmaceutical units located in Himachal Pradesh are pending under the said sub-scheme due to temporary restriction is in place pending the finalisation of the decision of Expenditure Finance Committee/Standing Finance Committee on extension of the sub scheme. This information was given by Minister of State for Chemicals and Fertilizers, Smt. ministry: Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers - Department of Fertilizers
title: One Nation, One Fertilizer' Initiative Strengthens Fertilizer Availability and Distribution Across the Country
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers : Department of Fertilizers One Nation, One Fertilizer' Initiative Strengthens Fertilizer Availability and Distribution Across the Country Advance Planning, Digital Monitoring and Coordinated Supply Mechanism Support Timely Fertilizer Availability Nationwide प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                04 AUG 2026 4:05PM by PIB Delhi The Government of India has strengthened the country's fertilizer distribution system through the 'One Nation, One Fertilizer' initiative under the “Pradhanmantri Bhartiya Janurvarak Pariyojana” (PMBJP). Implemented with effect from 24 August 2022, the initiative mandates all Public Sector, Cooperative and Private Sector fertilizer companies to market subsidized fertilizers under the common “BHARAT” brand across the country. The objective of the scheme is to increase the availability basket of fertilizers; take care of dilemma among farmers in choosing from plethora of brands manufactured by various companies available in the markets, reduce the crisscross movement and further ensure timely supply of fertilizers across the country. By consolidating branding under a single “BHARAT” brand, the scheme fosters transparency, combats malpractices, and ensures equitable access to essential nutrients for crops.  Presently, all the subsidized fertilizers viz. Urea, DAP, MOP and NPKS grades are marketed under the Bharat Brand. The Government has complemented the initiative with a robust fertilizer supply and distribution mechanism to ensure timely availability of fertilizers. Before the commencement of every cropping season, the Department of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare (DA&FW), in consultation with State Governments, assesses the State-wise and month-wise fertilizer requirement. Based on these projections, the Department of Fertilizers (DoF) allocates adequate quantities of fertilizers through monthly supply plans and continuously monitors their availability across the country. To strengthen transparency and real-time monitoring, the movement of all major subsidized fertilizers is tracked through the Integrated Fertilizer Management System (iFMS), an online web-based platform that monitors fertilizer movement across the supply chain. To bridge the gap between domestic production and demand, fertilizer imports are finalized well in advance to ensure timely availability during the cropping season. The Government also regularly advises State Governments to coordinate with fertilizer manufacturers and importers for timely placement of indents and streamlined supplies. In addition, continuous coordination is maintained with the Ministry of Railways to ensure adequate availability of railway rakes, priority movement of fertilizers and timely evacuation of fertilizer consignments to various States. Distribution of fertilizers at the district level is undertaken by the respective State Governments. In view of above, the availability of fertilizers viz. Urea, DAP, MOP and NPKS in the country has remained adequate during the ongoing Kharif 2026 season.                         04 AUG 2026 4:05PM by PIB Delhi The Government of India has strengthened the country's fertilizer distribution system through the 'One Nation, One Fertilizer' initiative under the “Pradhanmantri Bhartiya Janurvarak Pariyojana” (PMBJP). Implemented with effect from 24 August 2022, the initiative mandates all Public Sector, Cooperative and Private Sector fertilizer companies to market subsidized fertilizers under the common “BHARAT” brand across the country. The objective of the scheme is to increase the availability basket of fertilizers; take care of dilemma among farmers in choosing from plethora of brands manufactured by various companies available in the markets, reduce the crisscross movement and further ensure timely supply of fertilizers across the country. By consolidating branding under a single “BHARAT” brand, the scheme fosters transparency, combats malpractices, and ensures equitable access to essential nutrients for crops.  Presently, all the subsidized fertilizers viz. Urea, DAP, MOP and NPKS grades are marketed under the Bharat Brand. The Government has complemented the initiative with a robust fertilizer supply and distribution mechanism to ensure timely availability of fertilizers. Before the commencement of every cropping season, the Department of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare (DA&FW), in consultation with State Governments, assesses the State-wise and month-wise fertilizer requirement. Based on these projections, the Department of Fertilizers (DoF) allocates adequate quantities of fertilizers through monthly supply plans and continuously monitors their availability across the country. To strengthen transparency and real-time monitoring, the movement of all major subsidized fertilizers is tracked through the Integrated Fertilizer Management System (iFMS), an online web-based platform that monitors fertilizer movement across the supply chain. To bridge the gap between domestic production and demand, fertilizer imports are finalized well in advance to ensure timely availability during the cropping season. The Government also regularly advises State Governments to coordinate with fertilizer manufacturers and importers for timely placement of indents and streamlined supplies. In addition, continuous coordination is maintained with the Ministry of Railways to ensure adequate availability of railway rakes, priority movement of fertilizers and timely evacuation of fertilizer consignments to various States. Distribution of fertilizers at the district level is undertaken by the respective State Governments. In view of above, the availability of fertilizers viz. Urea, DAP, MOP and NPKS in the country has remained adequate during the ongoing Kharif 2026 season. title: PM-PRANAM Promotes Balanced Use of Fertilizer, Organic Farming and Natural Farming Across the Country
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers : Department of Fertilizers PM-PRANAM Promotes Balanced Use of Fertilizer, Organic Farming and Natural Farming Across the Country 5 States/UTs Reduce Chemical Fertilizer Consumption Under PM-PRANAM in 2025-26 Government Expands Organic Farming, Natural Farming and Precision Nutrient Management to Improve Soil Health प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                04 AUG 2026 4:04PM by PIB Delhi The Government of India is promoting balanced and sustainable fertilizer use through the PM Programme for Restoration, Awareness Generation, Nourishment and Amelioration of Mother Earth (PM-PRANAM), while simultaneously expanding organic farming, natural farming and precision nutrient management to improve soil health, reduce dependence on chemical fertilizers and promote environmentally sustainable agriculture. Approved by the Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs (CCEA) on 28 June 2023 for the period 2023-24 to 2025-26, PM-PRANAM supports the mass movement initiated by States and Union Territories for balanced fertilizer use, adoption of alternative fertilizers, promotion of organic farming and implementation of resource conservation technologies. The scheme covers all States and Union Territories and provides incentives for reducing the consumption of chemical fertilizers, namely Urea, DAP, NPK and MOP, in comparison with the average consumption of the previous three financial years. The incentive is equivalent to 50% of the fertilizer subsidy saved, of which 95% is earmarked for the concerned State/UT and 5% is retained by the Government of India. Out of the State share, 65% is to be utilized for capital expenditure projects, preferably under Centrally Sponsored Schemes, while the remaining 30% is available for other activities, including Information, Education and Communication (IEC) initiatives. During 2025-26, 5 States/UTs namely Dadra and Nagar Haveli, Delhi, Goa, Manipur and Mizoram recorded a cumulative reduction of 0.18 Lakh Metric Tons in the consumption of chemical fertilizers (Urea, DAP, NPKs and MOP) compared with the average consumption of the previous three financial years. The Government has informed that incentives under the scheme have not yet been disbursed. The Government has taken several steps to train farmers in precision farming techniques for the efficient and balanced use of nutrients and to promote the large-scale production of certified organic compost through various schemes of the Department of Agriculture and Farmers’ Welfare. The details are as follows: Organic Farming (PKVY & MOVCDNER) Organic farming is being promoted through Paramparagat Krishi Vikas Yojana (PKVY) in the States/UTs and Mission Organic Value Chain Development for North Eastern Region (MOVCDNER) for the North Eastern States since 2015-16. Both schemes stress on end-to-end support to farmers engaged in organic farming i.e. from production to processing, certification and marketing. Primary focus of the schemes is to form organic clusters, with preference to small and marginal farmers, to create a supply chain. Both the schemes are implemented through States /UT Governments. Under PKVY, assistance of Rs. 31,500 per ha is provided over 3 years for promotion of organic farming. Out of this, assistance of Rs. 15,000 per ha is provided to farmers through Direct Benefit Transfer for on- farm /off –farm organic inputs. Under MOVCDNER, assistance of Rs. 46,500/ha is provided over 3 years for creation of Farmers Producer Organization, support to farmers for organic inputs etc. Out of this, assistance @ Rs. 32,500/ ha is provided to farmers for off -farm /on –farm organic inputs under the scheme including Rs. 15,000 as Direct Benefit Transfer to the farmers. Under PKVY Scheme, since its inception (as on 30.06.2026), 18.93 lakh hectares area has been covered benefitting 33.63 lakh farmers and a total of ₹2811.36 crore (central share) has been released. Under MOVCDNER Scheme since its inception (as on 30.06.2026), 2.36 lakh hectares brought under organic farming benefitting 2.74 lakh farmers and a total of ₹1548.62 crore (central share) has been released. National Mission on Natural Farming (NMNF) The Government is also implementing the National Mission on Natural Farming (NMNF), launched on 25 November 2024, to promote chemical-free farming integrated with livestock, diversified cropping systems and traditional Indian agricultural knowledge. The Mission has a total financial outlay of ₹2,481 crore, comprising a Central share of ₹1,584 crore and a State share of ₹897 crore, up to the 15th Finance Commission period (March 2026). Farmers adopting natural farming are eligible for an Output Based Incentive of ₹4,000 per acre per year for 2 years, limited to one acre per farmer. `During FY 2025-26, 18,893 clusters covering 10.32 lakh hectares and involving 20.93 lakh farmers were formed under the Mission. To support field-level implementation, 33,257 Krishi Sakhis/Community Resource Persons (CRPs) have been trained and 7,601 Bio-Input Resource Centres (BRCs) established. In addition, 33.89 lakh farmers have been have been made aware about natural farming, 18.13 lakh soil samples have been collected and ₹599.68 crore has been utilized against a budget allocation of ₹725 crore during the financial year 2025-26. More than 22.47 lakh farmers have been registered under the Natural Farming Certification System (NFCS), of which over 14.43 lakh farmers have been certified. To promote precision nutrient management, the Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR) has developed drip fertigation schedules for 50 crops covering 14 agro-ecological regions, which are being disseminated through Krishi Vigyan Kendras (KVKs), frontline demonstrations, field demonstrations and farmer training programmes. ICAR has also standardized and promoted the use of Farm Yard Manure (FYM), phosphocompost, vermicompost, bio-enriched compost, municipal solid waste compost and enriched fermented organic manures through demonstrations, public awareness campaigns, training programmes and media outreach. This information was provided by Smt. Anupriya Patel, Minister of State in the Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers , in a written reply to a question in the Rajya Sabha today. *** Neeraj Kumar Bhatt/Shatrughna Prasad cmc.fertilizers[at]gmail[dot]com (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2294268) आगंतुक पटल  : 272 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: हिन्दी , Gujarati Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers : Department of Fertilizers PM-PRANAM Promotes Balanced Use of Fertilizer, Organic Farming and Natural Farming Across the Country 5 States/UTs Reduce Chemical Fertilizer Consumption Under PM-PRANAM in 2025-26 Government Expands Organic Farming, Natural Farming and Precision Nutrient Management to Improve Soil Health प्रविष्टि तिथि:

National Mission on Natural Farming (NMNF) The Government is also implementing the National Mission on Natural Farming (NMNF), launched on 25 November 2024, to promote chemical-free farming integrated with livestock, diversified cropping systems and traditional Indian agricultural knowledge. The Mission has a total financial outlay of ₹2,481 crore, comprising a Central share of ₹1,584 crore and a State share of ₹897 crore, up to the 15th Finance Commission period (March 2026). Farmers adopting natural farming are eligible for an Output Based Incentive of ₹4,000 per acre per year for 2 years, limited to one acre per farmer. `During FY 2025-26, 18,893 clusters covering 10.32 lakh hectares and involving 20.93 lakh farmers were formed under the Mission. To support field-level implementation, 33,257 Krishi Sakhis/Community Resource Persons (CRPs) have been trained and 7,601 Bio-Input Resource Centres (BRCs) established. In addition, 33.89 lakh farmers have been have been made aware about natural farming, 18.13 lakh soil samples have been collected and ₹599.68 crore has been utilized against a budget allocation of ₹725 crore during the financial year 2025-26. More than 22.47 lakh farmers have been registered under the Natural Farming Certification System (NFCS), of which over 14.43 lakh farmers have been certified. To promote precision nutrient management, the Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR) has developed drip fertigation schedules for 50 crops covering 14 agro-ecological regions, which are being disseminated through Krishi Vigyan Kendras (KVKs), frontline demonstrations, field demonstrations and farmer training programmes. ICAR has also standardized and promoted the use of Farm Yard Manure (FYM), phosphocompost, vermicompost, bio-enriched compost, municipal solid waste compost and enriched fermented organic manures through demonstrations, public awareness campaigns, training programmes and media outreach. This information was provided by Smt.
